101.e: RASAAVAL STANZA
Then the gods ran towards the goddess
With bowed heads.
The flowers were showered
And all the saints (hods) were pleased.6.
The goddess was worshipped
With the recitation of Vesdas manifested by Brahma.
When they fell at the feet of the goddess
All their sufferings ended.7.
They made their supplication,
And pleased the goddess
Who wore all her weapons,
And mounted the lion.8.
The songs resounded without interruption
The sounds was heard by the demon-king,
Who made preparations for the war.9.
The demon-king marched forward
And appointed four generals
One was Chamar, the second was Chichhur,
Both brave and persistent.10.
The third was the brave biralachh,
They were all mighty warriors and most tenacious.
They were great archers
And marched forward like dark clouds.11.
DOHRA

101.g: ਬਾਣਿ ਜਿਤੇ ਰਾਛਸਨਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਛਾਡਤ ਭਏ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
101.t: baan jite raachhasan mil chhaaddat bhe apaar ||
101.e: The arrows showered by all the demons together in great numbers,

101.g: ਫੂਲਮਾਲ ਹੁਐ ਮਾਤ ਉਰਿ ਸੋਭੇ ਸਭੇ ਸੁਧਾਰ ॥੧੨॥
101.t: foolamaal huaai maat ur sobhe sabhe sudhaar ||12||
101.e: Became a garland the neck of the goddess (the universal mother), bedecking it.12.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
All the shafts shot by the demons with their hands,
Were intercepted by the goddess to protect herself.

101.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਢਾਲ ਢਾਹੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਪਾਸ ਪੇਲੇ ॥
101.t: kite ddaal ddaahe kite paas pele ||
101.e: Many were thrown on the ground with her shield and many were entrapped within the baited trap.

101.g: ਭਰੇ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ਲੋਹੂ ਜਨੋ ਫਾਗ ਖੇਲੈ ॥੧੩॥
101.t: bhare basatr lohoo jano faag khelai ||13||
101.e: The clothes saturated with blood created an illusion of Holi.13.

101.g: ਦ੍ਰੁਗਾ ਹੂੰ ਕੀਯੰ ਖੇਤ ਧੁੰਕੇ ਨਗਾਰੇ ॥
101.t: dhrugaa hoo(n) keeya(n) khet dhu(n)ke nagaare ||
101.e: The trumpets sounded and Durga began to wage war.
She had pattas, axes and baits in her hands
She caught of pellet bow, mace and pellets.

101.g: ਹਠੀ ਮਾਰ ਹੀ ਮਾਰ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਪੁਕਾਰੈ ॥੧੪॥
101.t: haThee maar hee maar kai kai pukaarai ||14||
101.e: The persistent warriors were shouting “Kill, Kill”.14.
The goddess held eight weapons in her eitht hands,
And hit them on the heads of chief demons.
The demon-king rored like a lion in the battlefield,

101.g: ਕਰੇ ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡੰ ਸੁ ਜੋਧਾ ਅਪਾਰੰ ॥੧੫॥
101.t: kare kha(n)dd kha(n)dda(n) su jodhaa apaara(n) ||15||
101.e: And chopped into bits, many great warriors.15.
TOTAK STANZA

101.g: ਤਬ ਦਾਨਵ ਰੋਸ ਭਰੇ ਸਬ ਹੀ ॥
101.t: tab dhaanav ros bhare sab hee ||
101.e: All the demons were filled with anger,

101.g: ਜਗ ਮਾਤ ਕੇ ਬਾਣ ਲਗੈ ਜਬ ਹੀ ॥
101.t: jag maat ke baan lagai jab hee ||
101.e: When the were pierced by the arrows of the Mother of the worls.
Those brave warriors caught hold of their weapons with pleasure,

102.e: And began to shoot arrows like the rain-drops.16.

102.g: ਜਨੁ ਘੋਰ ਕੈ ਸਿਆਮ ਘਟਾ ਘੁਮਡੀ ॥
102.t: jan ghor kai siaam ghaTaa ghumaddee ||
102.e: Like the roaring and advancing dark clouds,
The forces of the demon-king marched forward.

102.g: ਜਗ ਮਾਤ ਬਿਰੂਥਨਿ ਮੋ ਧਸਿ ਕੈ ॥
102.t: jag maat biroothan mo dhas kai ||
102.e: The Mother of the world, penetrating into the armies of the enemy,

102.g: ਧਨੁ ਸਾਇਕ ਹਾਥ ਗਹਿਯੋ ਹਸਿ ਕੈ ॥੧੭॥
102.t: dhan saik haath gahiyo has kai ||17||
102.e: She caught hold of the bow and arrows smilingly.17.
She overthrew in the battlefield the herds of elephants,
And chopped into halves some of them.
On the heads of some of them she struck such a mighty blow,
That the bodies were pierced from the heads to the foot-palm.

102.g: ਤਨ ਝਝਰ ਹੁਐ ਰਣ ਭੂਮਿ ਗਿਰੇ ॥
102.t: tan jhajhar huaai ran bhoom gire ||
102.e: The decayed bodies fell in the battlefield

102.g: ਇਕ ਭਾਜ ਚਲੇ ਫਿਰ ਕੈ ਨ ਫਿਰੇ ॥
102.t: eik bhaaj chale fir kai na fire ||
102.e: Some ran away and did not return

102.g: ਇਕਿ ਹਾਥ ਹਥਿਆਰ ਲੈ ਆਨਿ ਬਹੇ ॥
102.t: eik haath hathiaar lai aan bahe ||
102.e: Some have caught hold of weapons and entered the battlefield

102.g: ਲਰਿ ਕੈ ਮਰਿ ਕੈ ਗਿਰਿ ਖੇਤਿ ਰਹੇ ॥੧੯॥
102.t: lar kai mar kai gir khet rahe ||19||
102.e: And after fighting have died and fallen in the field.19.
NARAAJ STANZA
Then the demon-king gathered all the war-paraphernalis.
He drove his horse forward and wanted to kill the Mother (goddess).20.
Then the goddess Durga challenged him, taking up her bow and arrows
She wounded (one of) the generals named Chamar and threw him down on the ground from his elephatnt.21
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
Then the hero named Biralachh was filled with ire.

102.g: ਸਜੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਦੇਹੰ ਚਲੋ ਜੁਧ ਧਾਮੰ ॥
102.t: saje sasatr dheha(n) chalo judh dhaama(n) ||
102.e: He bedecked himself with weapons and walked towards the battlefield.

102.g: ਸਿਰੰ ਸਿੰਘ ਕੇ ਆਨਿ ਘਾਯੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੰ ॥
102.t: sira(n) si(n)gh ke aan ghaaya(n) prahaara(n) ||
102.e: He struck his weapon on the head of the lion and wounded him,

102.g: ਬਲੀ ਸਿੰਘ ਸੋ ਹਾਥ ਸੋ ਮਾਰਿ ਡਾਰੰ ॥੨੨॥
102.t: balee si(n)gh so haath so maar ddaara(n) ||22||
102.e: But the brave lion killed him with his hands.22.
When Biralachh was killed, Pinagachh ran forward
Going in front of Durga, he uttered some inronical words.

102.g: ਕਰੀ ਅਭ੍ਰਿ ਜ੍ਯੋ ਗਰਜ ਕੈ ਬਾਣ ਬਰਖੰ ॥
102.t: karee abhr jayo garaj kai baan barakha(n) ||
102.e: Roaring like a cloud, he showered a volley of arrows

102.g: ਮਹਾ ਸੂਰ ਬੀਰੰ ਭਰੇ ਜੁਧ ਹਰਖੰ ॥੨੩॥
102.t: mahaa soor beera(n) bhare judh harakha(n) ||23||
102.e: That great hero was filled with pleasure in the battlefield.23.
Then the goddess caught hold of her bow and arrows.

102.g: ਹਨਿਯੋ ਦੁਸਟ ਕੇ ਘਾਇ ਸੀਸੰ ਮਝਾਰੰ ॥
102.t: haniyo dhusaT ke ghai seesa(n) majhaara(n) ||
102.e: She wounded the tyrant on his head with her shaft

102.g: ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਝੂਮਿ ਭੂਮੰ ਗਏ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਛੁਟੰ ॥
102.t: giriyo jhoom bhooma(n) ge praan chhuTa(n) ||
102.e: Who swayed, fell down of the goround and breathed his last.

102.g: ਮਨੋ ਮੇਰ ਕੋ ਸਾਤਵੌ ਸ੍ਰਿੰਗ ਟੁਟੰ ॥੨੪॥
102.t: mano mer ko saatavau sira(n)g TuTa(n) ||24||
102.e: It seemed that the seventh peak of Sumeru mountain had fallen down.24.
When the warriors like Pingachh fell in the field,
Other warriors holding their weapons marched forward.
Then the goddess in great ire shot many arrows,

102.g: ਬਿਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਕੇ ਜੁਧ ਮਧੰ ਗਿਰਾਏ ॥੨੫॥
102.t: binaa praan ke judh madha(n) giraae ||25||
102.e: Which laid to rest many warriors in the battlefield.25.
CHAUPAI
The enemies who came before the goddess, they were all killed by her.
When all the army was thus effaced, then the egoistic demon-king was filled with rage.26.
Then the goddess Durga herself waged the war, and picked up and killed the warriors wearing armour.
The flame of ire manifested itself from her forehead, which appeared in the form of goddess kalka.27.

103.e: MADHUBHAAR STANZA
The flames of fire come from her mouth and she herself came out from the forehead (of Durga).
She killed the great elephants and the warriors on horseback.28.
The arrows are being shot and the swords are glistening.
The daggers are being struck and it appears that the festival of Holi is being celebrated.29.
The weapons are being use unhesitatingly, which create clattering sounds.
The guns boom and produce roaring sounds. 30
The Mother (goddess) challenges and the wounds bust.
The youthful warriors fight and the horses dance.31
ROOAAL STANZA

103.g: ਧਾਈਯੋ ਅਸੁਰੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ਤਹਿ ਨਿਜ ਕੋਪ ਓਪ ਬਢਾਇ ॥
103.t: dhaieeyo asureaa(n)dhr teh nij kop op baddai ||
103.e: With increased anger, the demon-king sped forward.

103.g: ਸੰਗ ਲੈ ਚਤੁਰੰਗ ਸੈਨਾ ਸੁਧ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਨਚਾਇ ॥
103.t: sa(n)g lai chatura(n)g sainaa sudh sasatr nachai ||
103.e: He had four kinds of forces with him, who cause the dance of sharp weapons.

103.g: ਦੇਬਿ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਲਗੈ ਗਿਰੈ ਰਣਿ ਰੁਝਿ ਜੁਝਿ ਜੁਆਣ ॥
103.t: dheb sasatr lagai girai ran rujh jujh juaan ||
103.e: Whosoever was struck by the weapons of the goddess, those fighting warriors fell in the field.

103.g: ਪੀਲਰਾਜ ਫਿਰੇ ਕਹੂੰ ਰਣ ਸੁਛ ਛੁਛ ਕਿਕਾਣ ॥੩੨॥
103.t: peelaraaj fire kahoo(n) ran suchh chhuchh kikaan ||32||
103.e: Somewhere the elephants and somewhere horses are roaming without riders in the battlefield.32.

103.g: ਚੀਰ ਚਾਮਰ ਪੁੰਜ ਕੁੰਜਰ ਬਾਜ ਰਾਜ ਅਨੇਕ ॥
103.t: cheer chaamar pu(n)j ku(n)jar baaj raaj anek ||
103.e: Somewhere clothes, turbans and fly-whisks are lying scattered and somewhere elephants, horses and chieftains are lying dead.

103.g: ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਸੁਭੇ ਕਹੂੰ ਸਰਦਾਰ ਸੁਆਰ ਅਨੇਕ ॥
103.t: sasatr asatr subhe kahoo(n) saradhaar suaar anek ||
103.e: Somewhere generals and warriors with weapons and aromuts are lying down.

103.g: ਤੇਗੁ ਤੀਰ ਤੁਫੰਗ ਤਬਰ ਕੁਹੁਕ ਬਾਨ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
103.t: teg teer tufa(n)g tabar kuhuk baan ana(n)t ||
103.e: Somewhere the sonund of arrows, swords, guns, axes and special shafts is being heard.

103.g: ਬੇਧਿ ਬੇਧਿ ਗਿਰੈ ਬਰਛਿਨ ਸੂਰ ਸੋਭਾਵੰਤ ॥੩੩॥
103.t: bedh bedh girai barachhin soor sobhaava(n)t ||33||
103.e: Somewhere the heroes pierced by the daggers have fallen gracefully.33.

103.g: ਗ੍ਰਿਧ ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਉਡੇ ਤਹਾ ਫਿਕਰੰਤ ਸੁਆਨ ਸ੍ਰਿੰਗਾਲ ॥
103.t: giradh biradh udde tahaa fikara(n)t suaan sira(n)gaal ||
103.e: Large-sized vultures are flying there, the dogs are barking and the jackals are howling.

103.g: ਮਤ ਦੰਤਿ ਸਪਛ ਪਬੈ ਕੰਕ ਬੰਕ ਰਸਾਲ ॥
103.t: mat dha(n)t sapachh pabai ka(n)k ba(n)k rasaal ||
103.e: The intoxicated elephants look like the winged mountains and the crows, flying down to eat the flesh.

103.g: ਛੁਦ੍ਰ ਮੀਨ ਛੁਰੁੱਧ੍ਰਕਾ ਅਰੁ ਚਰਮ ਕਛਪ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
103.t: chhudhr meen chhuru'dhrakaa ar charam kachhap ana(n)t ||
103.e: Thhe swords on the bodies of the demons appear like small fish and the shields look like tortoises.

103.g: ਨਕ੍ਰ ਬਕ੍ਰ ਸੁ ਬਰਮ ਸੋਭਿਤ ਸ੍ਰੋਣ ਨੀਰ ਦੁਰੰਤ ॥੩੪॥
103.t: nakr bakr su baram sobhit sron neer dhura(n)t ||34||
103.e: On their bodies, the steel-armour looks elegant and the blood is flowing down like flood.34.

103.g: ਨਵ ਸੂਰ ਨਵਕਾ ਸੇ ਰਥੀ ਅਤਿਰਥੀ ਜਾਨੁ ਜਹਾਜ ॥
103.t: nav soor navakaa se rathee atirathee jaan jahaaj ||
103.e: The new young warriors appear like boats and thhe charioteers look like shimps.

103.g: ਲਾਦਿ ਲਾਦਿ ਮਨੋ ਚਲੇ ਧਨ ਧੀਰ ਬੀਰ ਸਲਾਜ ॥
103.t: laadh laadh mano chale dhan dheer beer salaaj ||
103.e: All this appears as if the traders loading their commodities are coyly running out of the battlefield.

103.g: ਮੋਲੁ ਬੀਚ ਫਿਰੈ ਚੁਕਾਤ ਦਲਾਲ ਖੇਤ ਖਤੰਗ ॥
103.t: mol beech firai chukaat dhalaal khet khata(n)g ||
103.e: The arrows of the battlefield are like the agents, who are busy in settling the account of the transaction.

103.g: ਗਾਹਿ ਗਾਹਿ ਫਿਰੇ ਫਵਜਨਿ ਝਾਰਿ ਦਿਰਬ ਨਿਖੰਗ ॥੩੫॥
103.t: gaeh gaeh fire favajan jhaar dhirab nikha(n)g ||35||
103.e: The armies are fastly moving in the field for settlement and emptying their treasure of quivers.35.

103.g: ਅੰਗ ਭੰਗ ਗਿਰੇ ਕਹੂੰ ਬਹੁਰੰਗ ਰੰਗਿਤ ਬਸਤ੍ਰ ॥
103.t: a(n)g bha(n)g gire kahoo(n) bahura(n)g ra(n)git basatr ||
103.e: Some where multi-coloured garments and chopped limbs are lying.

103.g: ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮ ਸੁਭੰ ਕਹੂੰ ਰਣੰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਰੁ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ॥
103.t: charam baram subha(n) kahoo(n) rana(n) sasatr r asatr ||
103.e: Somewhere there are shields and armours and somewhere there only weapons.

103.g: ਮੁੰਡ ਤੁੰਡ ਧੁਜਾ ਪਤਾਕਾ ਟੂਕ ਟਾਕ ਅਰੇਕ ॥
103.t: mu(n)dd tu(n)dd dhujaa pataakaa Took Taak arek ||
103.e: Somewhere there are heads, flags and ensigns scattered here and there.

103.g: ਜੂਝ ਜੂਝ ਪਰੇ ਸਬੈ ਅਰਿ ਬਾਚਿਯੋ ਨਹੀ ਏਕ ॥੩੬॥
103.t: joojh joojh pare sabai ar baachiyo nahee ek ||36||
103.e: In the battlefield all the enemies have fallen down while fighting and none has been left alive.36.

103.g: ਕੋਪ ਕੈ ਮਹਿਖੇਸ ਦਾਨੋ ਧਾਈਯੋ ਤਿਹ ਕਾਲ ॥
103.t: kop kai mahikhes dhaano dhaieeyo teh kaal ||
103.e: Then in great ire, the demon Mahishasura marched forward.

103.g: ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਸੰਭਾਰ ਸੂਰੋ ਰੂਪ ਕੈ ਬਿਕਰਾਲ ॥
103.t: asatr sasatr sa(n)bhaar sooro roop kai bikaraal ||
103.e: He appeared in a frightful form and held up all his weapons and arms.

103.g: ਕਾਲ ਪਾਣਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਣ ਲੈ ਤਿਹ ਮਾਰਿਯੋ ਤਤਕਾਲ ॥
103.t: kaal paan kirapaan lai teh maariyo tatakaal ||
103.e: The goddess Kalka took her sword in her hand and killed him instantly.

103.g: ਜੋਤਿ ਜੋਤਿ ਬਿਖੈ ਮਿਲੀ ਤਜ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਰੰਧ੍ਰਿ ਉਤਾਲ ॥੩੭॥
103.t: jot jot bikhai milee taj brahamara(n)dhr utaal ||37||
103.e: His soul left Brahmrandhir (life-channel of Dasam Dyar) and merged in Divine Light.37.
DOHRA

103.g: ਮਹਿਖਾਸੁਰ ਕਹ ਮਾਰ ਕਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਫੁਲਤ ਭੀ ਜਗ ਮਾਇ ॥
103.t: mahikhaasur keh maar kar prafulat bhee jag mai ||
103.e: After killing Mahishasura, the Mother of the world was greatly pleased.

103.g: ਤਾ ਦਿਨ ਤੇ ਮਹਿਖੇ ਬਲੈ ਦੇਤ ਜਗਤ ਸੁਖ ਪਾਇ ॥੩੮॥
103.t: taa dhin te mahikhe balai dhet jagat sukh pai ||38||
103.e: And from that day the whole world gives the sacrifice of the animals for the attainment of peace.38.

103.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਮਹਿਖਾਸੁਰ ਬਧਹ ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਧਿਆਇ ਸੰਪੂਰਨੰਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੧॥
103.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre mahikhaasur badheh pratham dhiaai sa(n)poorana(n)m sat subham sat ||1||
103.e: Here ends the First Chapter entitled ‘Killing of Mahishasura’ of Chandi Charitra in BACHITTAR NATAK.1.
Here begins the description of the war with Dhumar Nain :
KULAK STANZA
Then the goddess roared and there was continuous intonation.
All were delighted and felt comfortable.1.39.
The trumpents sounded and all the gods shouted.
They eulogise the godess and shower flowers on her. 2.40.
They worshipped the goddess in various ways and sang her poraises.
They have touhed her feet and all their sorrows have ended.3.41.
They sang the songs of victory and showered flowers.
They bowed their heads and obtained great comfort.4.42.
DOHRA

103.g: ਲੋਪ ਚੰਡਿਕਾ ਜੂ ਭਈ ਦੈ ਦੇਵਨ ਕੋ ਰਾਜੁ ॥
103.t: lop cha(n)ddikaa joo bhiee dhai dhevan ko raaj ||
103.e: The goddess Chandi disappeared after bestowing kingdom on the gods.

103.g: ਬਹੁਰ ਸੁੰਭ ਨੈਸੁੰਭ ਦੁਐ ਦੈਤ ਬੜੇ ਸਿਰਤਾਜ ॥੫॥੪੩॥
103.t: bahur su(n)bh naisu(n)bh dhuaai dhait baRe sirataaj ||5||43||
103.e: Then after some time, both the demons kings came to power.5.43.
CHAUPAI

103.g: ਸੁੰਭ ਨਿਸੁੰਭ ਚੜੇ ਲੈ ਕੈ ਦਲ ॥
103.t: su(n)bh nisu(n)bh chaRe lai kai dhal ||
103.e: Both Sumbh and Nisumbh marched with their forces.

103.g: ਅਰਿ ਅਨੇਕ ਜੀਤੇ ਜਿਨ ਜਲਿ ਥਲਿ ॥
103.t: ar anek jeete jin jal thal ||
103.e: They conquered many enemies in water and on land.
They seized the kingdom of Indra, the king of gods.
Sheshanaga sent his head-jewel as a gift.6.44.

104.e: They snatched the treasure of Kuber
And conquered the kings of various countries.
Wherever they sent their forces
They returned after conquering many countries.7.45.
DOHRA

104.g: ਦੇਵ ਸਬੈ ਤ੍ਰਾਸਤਿ ਭਏ ਮਨ ਮੋ ਕੀਯੋ ਬਿਚਾਰ ॥
104.t: dhev sabai traasat bhe man mo keeyo bichaar ||
104.e: All the gods were filled with fear and thought in their mind

104.g: ਸਰਨ ਭਵਾਨੀ ਕੀ ਸਬੈ ਭਾਜਿ ਪਰੇ ਨਿਰਧਾਰ ॥੮॥੪੬॥
104.t: saran bhavaanee kee sabai bhaaj pare niradhaar ||8||46||
104.e: Being helpless, they all ran to come under the refuge of the goddess.8.46.
NARAAJ STANZA
The gods ran in great fear and felt ashamed with particular self-abasment.
They had fitted poisonous shafts in their bows and in this way they went ot reside in the city of goddess.9.47.
Then the goddess was filled with great rage and marched towards the battlefield with her weapons and arms.
She drank the nectar in ther delight and roared wihile taking the sword in her hand.10.48.
RASAAVAL STANZA
Listening to the talk of the gods, the queen (goddess) munted the lion.
She had worn all her auspicious weapons and she is the one who effaces all the sins.11.49.
The goddess commanded that highly inebriating trumpets besounded.
Then the conches created great noise, which was heard. In all the four directions.12.50.
The demons marched forward and brought great forces.
Their faces and eyes were red like blood and they shouted prickig words.13.51.
Four types of forces rushed and shouted from their mouths: “Kill, Kill”.
They took up in their hands the arrows, daggers and swords.14.52.
They are all active in warfare and shoot arrows.
The weapons like swods and daggers glisten.15.53.
The great heroes rushed forward and many on them shot arrows.
They strike blows on the enemy with much swiftness like the watter-bird.16.54.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
With elevated tail and full of rage the lion ran forward.

104.g: ਇਤੇ ਸੰਖ ਲੈ ਹਾਥਿ ਦੇਵੀ ਬਜਾਯੋ ॥
104.t: eite sa(n)kh lai haath dhevee bajaayo ||
104.e: There the goddess holding the conch in her hand, blew it.
Its sound reverberated in all the fourteen regions.

104.g: ਚਮਕਿਯੋ ਮੁਖੰ ਜੁਧ ਕੇ ਮਧਿ ਨੂਰੰ ॥੧੭॥੫੫॥
104.t: chamakiyo mukha(n) judh ke madh noora(n) ||17||55||
104.e: The face of the goddess was filled with brightness in the battlefield.17.55.

104.g: ਤਬੈ ਧੂਮ੍ਰ ਨੈਣੰ ਮਚਿਯੋ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੀ ॥
104.t: tabai dhoomr naina(n) machiyo sasatr dhaaree ||
104.e: Then Dhumar Nain, the weapon-wielder, was greatly excited.

104.g: ਲਏ ਸੰਗ ਜੋਧਾ ਬਡੇ ਬੀਰ ਭਾਰੀ ॥
104.t: le sa(n)g jodhaa badde beer bhaaree ||
104.e: He took many brave warriors with him.

105.g: ਲਯੋ ਬੇੜਿ ਪਬੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਉੱਚੰ ॥
105.t: layo beR paba(n) keeyo naadh u'cha(n) ||
105.e: They besieged the mountain and began to shout at the top of their voice.
Which when heard could destroy the pregnancy of women.18.56.

105.g: ਸੁਣਿਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਸ੍ਰਵਣੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਦੇਵਿ ਕੋਪੰ ॥
105.t: suniyo naadh sravana(n) keeyo dhev kopa(n) ||
105.e: When the goddess heard voice of the demon-chief, she was greatly enraged.

105.g: ਸਜੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ਧਰੇ ਸੀਸਿ ਟੋਪੰ ॥
105.t: saje charam barama(n) dhare sees Topa(n) ||
105.e: She bedecked herself with shield and armour and wore the steel-helmet on her head.

105.g: ਭਈ ਸਿੰਘ ਸੁਆਰੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਉੱਚੰ ॥
105.t: bhiee si(n)gh suaara(n) keeyo naadh u'cha(n) ||
105.e: She mounted the lion and shouted loudly.

105.g: ਸੁਨੇ ਦੀਹ ਦਾਨਵਾਨ ਕੇ ਮਾਨ ਮੁਚੰ ॥੧੯॥੫੭॥
105.t: sune dheeh dhaanavaan ke maan mucha(n) ||19||57||
105.e: Hearing her shouts, the pride of the demons was destroyed.19.57.

105.g: ਮਹਾ ਕੋਪਿ ਦੇਵੀ ਧਸੀ ਸੈਨ ਮਧੰ ॥
105.t: mahaa kop dhevee dhasee sain madha(n) ||
105.e: In great ire, the goddess penetrated into the demon-army.

105.g: ਕਰੇ ਬੀਰ ਬੰਕੇ ਤਹਾ ਅਧੁ ਅਧੰ ॥
105.t: kare beer ba(n)ke tahaa adh adha(n) ||
105.e: She chopped into halves the great heroes.

105.g: ਜਿਸੈ ਧਾਇ ਕੈ ਸੂਲ ਸੈਥੀ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
105.t: jisai dhai kai sool saithee prahaariyo ||
105.e: On whomsoever the goddess struck her blow with her trident and the destructive weapon (Saihathi)

105.g: ਤਿਨੇ ਫੇਰਿ ਪਾਣੰ ਨ ਬਾਣੰ ਸੰਭਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੨੦॥੫੮॥
105.t: tine fer paana(n) na baana(n) sa(n)bhaariyo ||20||58||
105.e: He could not hold again his bow and arrows in his hands.20.58.
RASAAVAL STANZA
Whosover was shot with the arrow, he was killed instantly.
Wherever the lion rushed forward, he destroyed the army.21.59.
All those who were killed, they were thrown into caves.
The enemies who confronted coul not return alive.22.60.
Those who were active in the battlefield, they were all decimated.
Those who caught hold of weapons, they were all killed.23.61.
Then the mother Kali flared up like the flaming fire.
To whomsoever she struck, he departed for heaven.24.62.
The whole army was destroyed within a very short time.
Dhumar Nain was killed and the gods heard about it in heaven.25.63.
DOHRA

105.g: ਭਜੀ ਬਿਰੂਥਨਿ ਦਾਨਵੀ ਗਈ ਭੂਪ ਕੇ ਪਾਸ ॥
105.t: bhajee biroothan dhaanavee giee bhoop ke paas ||
105.e: The demon forces ran towards their king.

105.g: ਧੂਮ੍ਰਨੈਣ ਕਾਲੀ ਹਨਿਯੋ ਭਜੀਯੋ ਸੈਨ ਨਿਰਾਸ ॥੨੬॥੬੪॥
105.t: dhoomranain kaalee haniyo bhajeeyo sain niraas ||26||64||
105.e: Intimating him that Kali had killed Dhumar Nain and the forces had fled in disappointment.26.64.

105.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰ ਧੂਮ੍ਰਨੈਨ ਬਧਤ ਦੁਤੀਆ ਧਿਆਇ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨॥
105.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitr dhoomranain badhat dhuteeaa dhiaai sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||2||
105.e: Here ends the Second Chapter entitled ‘Killing of Dhumar Nain’, which forms part of Chandi Charitra of BACHITTAR NATAK.2.
Now the battle with Chand and Mund is described:
DOHRA

105.g: ਇਹ ਬਿਧ ਦੈਤ ਸੰਘਾਰ ਕਰ ਧਵਲਾ ਚਲੀ ਅਵਾਸ ॥
105.t: eeh bidh dhait sa(n)ghaar kar dhavalaa chalee avaas ||
105.e: In this way, killing the demons, the goddess Durga went to her abode.

105.g: ਜੋ ਯਹ ਕਥਾ ਪੜੈ ਸੁਨੈ ਰਿਧਿ ਸਿਧਿ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਤਾਸ ॥੧॥੬੫॥
105.t: jo yeh kathaa paRai sunai ridh sidh gireh taas ||1||65||
105.e: He who read or listens to this discourse, he will attain in his house wealth and miraculous powers.1.65.
CHAUPAI
When it was learnt that Dhumar Nain had been killed,
The demon-king then called Chand and Mund.
They were sent after bestowing many honours on them.

105.g: ਹੈ ਗੈ ਪਤਿ ਦੀਏ ਰਥ ਨਾਨਾ ॥੨॥੬੬॥
105.t: hai gai pat dhe'ee rath naanaa ||2||66||
105.e: And also many gifts like horses, elephants and chariots.2.66.
Those who had earlier seen the goddess
They were sent towards kailash mountain (as spies).

105.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੀ ਤਨਿਕ ਭਨਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਪਾਈ ॥
105.t: tin kee tanik bhanak sun paiee ||
105.e: When the goddess heard some rumour about them
She then promptly came down with her weapons and armour.3.67.

106.g: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ॥
106.t: rooaal chha(n)dh ||
106.e: ROOAAL STANZA

106.g: ਸਾਜਿ ਸਾਜਿ ਚਲੇ ਤਹਾ ਰਣਿ ਰਾਛਸੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ਅਨੇਕ ॥
106.t: saaj saaj chale tahaa ran raachhaseaa(n)dhr anek ||
106.e: Decorating their forces many demon-generals marched towards the battlefield.

106.g: ਅਰਧ ਮੁੰਡਿਤ ਮੁੰਡਿਤੇਕ ਜਟਾ ਧਰੇ ਸੁ ਅਰੇਕ ॥
106.t: aradh mu(n)ddit mu(n)dditek jaTaa dhare su arek ||
106.e: Many warriors are with half-shaven heads, many with fullshaven hads and many are with matted hair.

106.g: ਕੋਪਿ ਓਪੰ ਦੈ ਸਬੈ ਕਰਿ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਨਚਾਇ ॥
106.t: kop opa(n) dhai sabai kar sasatr asatr nachai ||
106.e: All of them in great fury, are causing the dance of their weapons and armour.

106.g: ਧਾਇ ਧਾਇ ਕਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰਨ ਤਿਛ ਤੇਗ ਕੰਪਾਇ ॥੪॥੬੮॥
106.t: dhai dhai karai prahaaran tichh teg ka(n)pai ||4||68||
106.e: They are running and striking blows, causing their sharp swords to shake and glitter. 4.68

106.g: ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਲਗੇ ਜਿਤੇ ਸਬ ਫੂਲ ਮਾਲ ਹੁਐ ਗਏ ॥
106.t: sasatr asatr lage jite sab fool maal huaai ge ||
106.e: All the blows of weapons and arms, which struck the goddess, they appeared as garlands of flowers around her neck.

106.g: ਕੋਪ ਓਪ ਬਿਲੋਕਿ ਅਤਿਭੁਤ ਦਾਨਵੰ ਬਿਸਮੈ ਭਏ ॥
106.t: kop op bilok atibhut dhaanava(n) bisamai bhe ||
106.e: Seeing this all the demons were filled with anger and astonishment.

106.g: ਦਉਰ ਦਉਰ ਅਨੇਕ ਆਯੁਧ ਫੇਰਿ ਫੇਰਿ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰਹੀ ॥
106.t: dhaur dhaur anek aayudh fer fer prahaarahee ||
106.e: Many of them, running ahead repeatedly strike blows with their weapons.

106.g: ਜੂਝਿ ਜੂਝਿ ਗਿਰੈ ਅਰੇਕ ਸੁ ਮਾਰ ਮਾਰ ਪੁਕਾਰਹੀ ॥੫॥੬੯॥
106.t: joojh joojh girai arek su maar maar pukaarahee ||5||69||
106.e: And with shouts of “kill, kill”, they are fighting and falling down.5.69.

106.g: ਰੇਲਿ ਰੇਲਿ ਚਲੇ ਹਏਾਂਦ੍ਰਨ ਪੇਲਿ ਪੇਲਿ ਗਜੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: rel rel chale heaa(n)dhran pel pel gajeaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: The horse-rider generals are driving forward theh horses and the elephant-rider generals are goading their elephants.

106.g: ਝੇਲਿ ਝੇਲਿ ਅਨੰਤ ਆਯੁਧ ਹੇਲਿ ਹੇਲਿ ਰਿਪੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: jhel jhel ana(n)t aayudh hel hel ripeaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: Facing unlimited weapons, the enemies’ generals, enduring the blows, are still making an assault.

106.g: ਗਾਹਿ ਗਾਹਿ ਫਿਰੇ ਫਵਜਨ ਬਾਹਿ ਬਾਹਿ ਖਤੰਗ ॥
106.t: gaeh gaeh fire favajan baeh baeh khata(n)g ||
106.e: The armies crushing the warriors are marching forward and showering their arrows.

106.g: ਅੰਗ ਭੰਗ ਗਿਰੇ ਕਹੂੰ ਰਣਿ ਰੰਗ ਸੂਰ ਉਤੰਗ ॥੬॥੭੦॥
106.t: a(n)g bha(n)g gire kahoo(n) ran ra(n)g soor uta(n)g ||6||70||
106.e: Many heroic fighters, becoming limbless, have fallen down in the battlefield.6.70.

106.g: ਝਾਰਿ ਝਾਰਿ ਫਿਰੇ ਸਰੋਤਮ ਡਾਰਿ ਝਾਰਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਨ ॥
106.t: jhaar jhaar fire sarotam ddaar jhaar kirapaan ||
106.e: Some where the shafts are falling like rain-showers and somewhere the swords are striking blows collectively.

106.g: ਸੈਲ ਸੇ ਰਣਿ ਪੁੰਜ ਕੁੰਜਰ ਸੂਰ ਸੀਸ ਬਖਾਨ ॥
106.t: sail se ran pu(n)j ku(n)jar soor sees bakhaan ||
106.e: The elephants seen together are like stony rocks and the heads of the warriors appear like stones.

106.g: ਬਕ੍ਰ ਨਕ੍ਰ ਭੁਜਾ ਸੁ ਸੋਭਿਤ ਚਕ੍ਰ ਸੇ ਰਥ ਚਕ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: bakr nakr bhujaa su sobhit chakr se rath chakr ||
106.e: The crooked arms appear like octopus and the chariot wheels are like tortoises.

106.g: ਕੇਸ ਪਾਸਿ ਸਿਬਾਲ ਸੋਹਤ ਅਸਥ ਚੂਰ ਸਰਕ੍ਰ ॥੭॥੭੧॥
106.t: kes paas sibaal sohat asath choor sarakr ||7||71||
106.e: The hair seem like noose and scum and the crushed bones like sand.7.71.

106.g: ਸਜਿ ਸਜਿ ਚਲੇ ਹਥਿਆਰਨ ਗਜਿ ਗਜਿ ਗਜੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: saj saj chale hathiaaran gaj gaj gajeaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: The warriors have bedecked themselves with weapons and the elephants are roaring wihil moving forward.

106.g: ਬਜਿ ਬਜਿ ਸਬਜ ਬਾਜਨ ਭਜਿ ਭਜਿ ਹਏਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: baj baj sabaj baajan bhaj bhaj heaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: The horse-riding warriors are speedily moving with the sounds of various types of musical instruments.

106.g: ਮਾਰ ਮਾਰ ਪੁਕਾਰ ਕੈ ਹਥੀਆਰ ਹਾਥਿ ਸੰਭਾਰ ॥
106.t: maar maar pukaar kai hatheeaar haath sa(n)bhaar ||
106.e: Holding their weapons in their hands, the heroes are shouting “kill, kill”.

106.g: ਧਾਇ ਧਾਇ ਪਰੇ ਨਿਸਾਚ ਬਾਇ ਸੰਖ ਅਪਾਰ ॥੮॥੭੨॥
106.t: dhai dhai pare nisaach bai sa(n)kh apaar ||8||72||
106.e: Blowing many conches, the demons are running in the battlefield.8.72.

106.g: ਸੰਖ ਗੋਯਮੰ ਗਜੀਯੰ ਅਰੁ ਸਜੀਯੰ ਰਿਪੁਰਾਜ ॥
106.t: sa(n)kh goyama(n) gajeeya(n) ar sajeeya(n) ripuraaj ||
106.e: The conches and horns are being blown loudly and the generals of the enemy are ready for war.

106.g: ਭਾਜਿ ਭਾਜਿ ਚਲੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਤਜਿ ਲਾਜ ਬੀਰ ਨਿਲਾਜ ॥
106.t: bhaaj bhaaj chale kite taj laaj beer nilaaj ||
106.e: Somewhere the cowards, forsaking their shame, are running away.

106.g: ਭੀਮ ਭੇਰੀ ਭੁੰਕੀਅੰ ਅਰੁ ਧੁੰਕੀਅੰ ਸੁ ਨਿਸਾਣ ॥
106.t: bheem bheree bhu(n)keea(n) ar dhu(n)keea(n) su nisaan ||
106.e: The sound of large-sized drums is being heard and the flags are fluttering.

106.g: ਗਾਹਿ ਗਾਹਿ ਫਿਰੇ ਫਵਜਨ ਬਾਹਿ ਬਾਹਿ ਗਦਾਣ ॥੯॥੭੩॥
106.t: gaeh gaeh fire favajan baeh baeh gadhaan ||9||73||
106.e: The forces are roaming and striking their maces.9.73.

106.g: ਬੀਰ ਕੰਗਨੇ ਬੰਧਹੀ ਅਰੁ ਅਛਰੈ ਸਿਰ ਤੇਲੁ ॥
106.t: beer ka(n)gane ba(n)dhahee ar achharai sir tel ||
106.e: The heavenly maids are bedecking themselves and offering ornaments to the warriors.

106.g: ਬੀਰ ਬੀਨਿ ਬਰੇ ਬਰੰਗਨ ਡਾਰਿ ਡਾਰਿ ਫੁਲੇਲ ॥
106.t: beer been bare bara(n)gan ddaar ddaar fulel ||
106.e: Selecting their heroes, the heavenly ladies are being bound with them in wedlock by showrering the oil impregnated with the essence of flowers.

106.g: ਘਾਲਿ ਘਾਲਿ ਬਿਵਾਨ ਲੇਗੀ ਫੇਰਿ ਫੇਰਿ ਸੁ ਬੀਰ ॥
106.t: ghaal ghaal bivaan legee fer fer su beer ||
106.e: They have taken away the warriors with them in their vehicles.

106.g: ਕੂਦਿ ਕੂਦਿ ਪਰੇ ਤਹਾ ਤੇ ਝਾਗਿ ਝਾਗਿ ਸੁ ਤੀਰ ॥੧੦॥੭੪॥
106.t: koodh koodh pare tahaa te jhaag jhaag su teer ||10||74||
106.e: The heroes inebriated for fighting in thhe war, jump from the vehicles and being shot with arrows, fall down below.10.74

106.g: ਹਾਕਿ ਹਾਕਿ ਲਰੇ ਤਹਾ ਰਣਿ ਰੀਝਿ ਰੀਝਿ ਭਟੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: haak haak lare tahaa ran reejh reejh bhaTeaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: Delightfully shouting in the battlefield, the heroic generals have waged war.

106.g: ਜੀਤਿ ਜੀਤਿ ਲਯੋ ਜਿਨੈ ਕਈ ਬਾਰ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਉਪੇਾਂਦ੍ਰ ॥
106.t: jeet jeet layo jinai kiee baar i(n)dhr upeaa(n)dhr ||
106.e: Who had several times conquered the king and other chieftains of gods.

106.g: ਕਾਟਿ ਕਾਟਿ ਦਏ ਕਪਾਲੀ ਬਾਟਿ ਬਾਟਿ ਦਿਸਾਨ ॥
106.t: kaaT kaaT dhe kapaalee baaT baaT dhisaan ||
106.e: Whom Durga (Kapali) chpped and threw in various directions.

106.g: ਡਾਟਿ ਡਾਟਿ ਕਰਿ ਦਲੰ ਸੁਰ ਪਗੁ ਪਬ ਪਿਸਾਨ ॥੧੧॥੭੫॥
106.t: ddaaT ddaaT kar dhala(n) sur pag pab pisaan ||11||75||
106.e: And with those who had ground the mountains with the strength of their hands and feet  11.75.

106.g: ਧਾਇ ਧਾਇ ਸੰਘਾਰੀਅੰ ਰਿਪੁ ਰਾਜ ਬਾਜ ਅਨੰਤ ॥
106.t: dhai dhai sa(n)ghaareea(n) rip raaj baaj ana(n)t ||
106.e: The enemies speedily marching agead are killing countless horses.

106.g: ਸ੍ਰੋਣ ਕੀ ਸਰਤਾ ਉਠੀ ਰਣ ਮਧਿ ਰੂਪ ਦੁਰੰਤ ॥
106.t: sron kee sarataa uThee ran madh roop dhura(n)t ||
106.e: And in the battlefield, the terrible stream of blood is flowing.

106.g: ਬਾਣ ਅਉਰ ਕਮਾਣ ਸੈਹਥੀ ਸੂਲ ਤਿਛੁ ਕੁਠਾਰ ॥
106.t: baan aaur kamaan saihathee sool tichh kuThaar ||
106.e: The weapons like bow and arrows, sword, trident and sharpo axe are being used.

106.g: ਚੰਡ ਮੁੰਡ ਹਣੇ ਦੋਊ ਕਰਿ ਕੋਪ ਕਾਲਿ ਕ੍ਰਵਾਰ ॥੧੨॥੭੬॥
106.t: cha(n)dd mu(n)dd hane dhouoo kar kop kaal kravaar ||12||76||
106.e: The goddess Kali in great rage, struck down and killed both Chand and Mund.12.76.

106.g: ਦੋਹਰਾ ॥
106.t: dhoharaa ||
106.e: DOHRA

106.g: ਚੰਡ ਮੁੰਡ ਮਾਰੇ ਦੋਊ ਕਾਲੀ ਕੋਪਿ ਕ੍ਰਵਾਰਿ ॥
106.t: cha(n)dd mu(n)dd maare dhouoo kaalee kop kravaar ||
106.e: Kali in great rage, struck down both Chand and Mund and killed them.

106.g: ਅਉਰ ਜਿਤੀ ਸੈਨਾ ਹੁਤੀ ਛਿਨ ਮੋ ਦਈ ਸੰਘਾਰ ॥੧੩॥੭੭॥
106.t: aaur jitee sainaa hutee chhin mo dhiee sa(n)ghaar ||13||77||
106.e: And all the army, that was there, was destroyed in and instant.13.77.

106.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਚੰਡ ਮੁੰਡ ਬਧਹ ਤ੍ਰਿਤਯੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤ ॥੩॥
106.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre cha(n)dd mu(n)dd badheh tiratayo dhiaai sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||3||
106.e: Here ends the Third Chapter entitled ‘Killing of Chad and Mund’ of Chandi Charitra in BACHITTAR NATAK.3.

106.g: ਅਥ ਰਕਤ ਬੀਰਜ ਜੁਧ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
106.t: ath rakat beeraj judh kathana(n) ||
106.e: Now the war with Rakat Biraj is described:

106.g: ਸੋਰਠਾ ॥
106.t: soraThaa ||
106.e: SORATHA

106.g: ਸੁਨੀ ਭੂਪ ਇਮ ਗਾਥ ਚੰਡ ਮੁੰਡ ਕਾਲੀ ਹਨੇ ॥
106.t: sunee bhoop im gaath cha(n)dd mu(n)dd kaalee hane ||
106.e: The demons-king heard this news that Kali had killed Chand and Mund.

106.g: ਬੈਠ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਸੋ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਕਰਤ ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਭਏ ॥੧॥੭੮॥
106.t: baiTh bhraat so bhraat ma(n)tr karat ieh bidh bhe ||1||78||
106.e: Then the brothers sat and decided in this manner: 1.78.

106.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
106.t: chauapiee ||
106.e: CHAUPAI

106.g: ਰਕਤਬੀਜ ਤਪ ਭੂਪਿ ਬੁਲਾਯੋ ॥
106.t: rakatabeej tap bhoop bulaayo ||

106.g: ਅਮਿਤ ਦਰਬੁ ਦੇ ਤਹਾ ਪਠਾਯੋ ॥
106.t: amit dharab dhe tahaa paThaayo ||
106.e: Then the king called Rakat Beej and sent him after giving him enormous wealth.

106.g: ਬਹੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਦਈ ਬਿਰੂਥਨ ਸੰਗਾ ॥
106.t: bahu bidh dhiee biroothan sa(n)gaa ||

106.g: ਹੈ ਗੈ ਰਥ ਪੈਦਲ ਚਤੁਰੰਗਾ ॥੨॥੭੯॥
106.t: hai gai rath paidhal chatura(n)gaa ||2||79||
106.e: He was also given various types of forces, which was fourfold: on horses, on elephants, on chariots and on foot.2.79.

106.g: ਰਕਤਬੀਜ ਦੈ ਚਲਿਯੋ ਨਗਾਰਾ ॥
106.t: rakatabeej dhai chaliyo nagaaraa ||

106.g: ਦੇਵ ਲੋਗ ਲਉ ਸੁਨੀ ਪੁਕਾਰਾ ॥
106.t: dhev log lau sunee pukaaraa ||
106.e: Rakat Beej marched after sounding his trumpet, which was heard even in the habitation of gods.

106.g: ਕੰਪੀ ਭੂਮਿ ਗਗਨ ਥਹਰਾਨਾ ॥
106.t: ka(n)pee bhoom gagan thaharaanaa ||

106.g: ਦੇਵਨ ਜੁਤਿ ਦਿਵਰਾਜ ਡਰਾਨਾ ॥੩॥੮੦॥
106.t: dhevan jut dhivaraaj ddaraanaa ||3||80||
106.e: The earth ttrembled and the sky vibrated, all the godds including the king were filled with fear.3.80.

106.g: ਧਵਲਾ ਗਿਰਿ ਕੇ ਜਬ ਤਟ ਆਇ ॥
106.t: dhavalaa gir ke jab taT aai ||

106.g: ਦੁੰਦਭਿ ਢੋਲ ਮ੍ਰਿਦੰਗ ਬਜਾਏ ॥
106.t: dhu(n)dhabh ddol miradha(n)g bajaae ||
106.e: When they came near the Kailash mountain, they sounded trumpets, drums and tabours.

106.g: ਜਬ ਹੀ ਸੁਨਾ ਕੁਲਾਹਲ ਕਾਨਾ ॥
106.t: jab hee sunaa kulaahal kaanaa ||

106.g: ਉਤਰੀ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਲੈ ਨਾਨਾ ॥੪॥੮੧॥
106.t: autaree sasatr asatr lai naanaa ||4||81||
106.e: When the gods heard the noises with their ears, the goddess Durga descended the mountain, taking many weapons and arms.4.81.

106.g: ਛਹਬਰ ਲਾਇ ਬਰਖੀਯੰ ਬਾਣੰ ॥
106.t: chhahabar lai barakheeya(n) baana(n) ||

106.g: ਬਾਜ ਰਾਜ ਅਰੁ ਗਿਰੇ ਕਿਕਾਣੰ ॥
106.t: baaj raaj ar gire kikaana(n) ||
106.e: The goddess showered arrows like incessant rain, which caused the horses and their riders fall down.

106.g: ਢਹਿ ਢਹਿ ਪਰੇ ਸੁਭਟ ਸਿਰਦਾਰਾ ॥
106.t: ddeh ddeh pare subhaT siradhaaraa ||

106.g: ਜਨੁ ਕਰ ਕਟੈ ਬਿਰਛ ਸੰਗ ਆਰਾ ॥੫॥੮੨॥
106.t: jan kar kaTai birachh sa(n)g aaraa ||5||82||
106.e: Many warriors and their chieftainsfell, it seemed as if the trees had been sawed.5.82.

106.g: ਜੇ ਜੇ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਾਮੁਹੇ ਭਏ ॥
106.t: je je satr saamuhe bhe ||

106.g: ਬਹੁਰ ਜੀਅਤ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਕੇ ਨਹੀ ਗਏ ॥
106.t: bahur jeeat gireh ke nahee ge ||
106.e: Those enemies ho came in front of her, they could not again return to their homes alive.

106.g: ਜਿਹ ਪਰ ਪਰਤ ਭਈ ਤਰਵਾਰਾ ॥
106.t: jeh par parat bhiee taravaaraa ||

106.g: ਇਕਿ ਇਕਿ ਤੇ ਭਏ ਦੋ ਦੋ ਚਾਰਾ ॥੬॥੮੩॥
106.t: eik ik te bhe dho dho chaaraa ||6||83||
106.e: Those who were struck by the sword, they fell down in two halves or four quarters.6.83.

106.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
106.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
106.e: BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

106.g: ਝਿਮੀ ਤੇਜ ਤੇਗੰ ਸੁਰੋਸੰ ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੰ ॥
106.t: jhimee tej tega(n) surosa(n) prahaara(n) ||
106.e: The sword which she has struck in ire

106.g: ਖਿਮੀ ਦਾਮਿਨੀ ਜਾਣ ਭਾਦੋ ਮਝਾਰੰ ॥
106.t: khimee dhaaminee jaan bhaadho majhaara(n) ||
106.e: It hath hlistened like lightning in the month of Bhadon.

106.g: ਉਦੇ ਨਦ ਨਾਦੰ ਕੜਕੇ ਕਮਾਣੰ ॥
106.t: audhe nadh naadha(n) kaRake kamaana(n) ||
106.e: The jingling sound of bows appears like the sound of flowing stream.

106.g: ਮਚਿਯੋ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ਅਭੂਤੰ ਭਯਾਣੰ ॥੭॥੮੪॥
106.t: machiyo loh kroha(n) abhoota(n) bhayaana(n) ||7||84||
106.e: And the steel-weapons have been struck in great anger, which appear unique and frightening.7.84.

106.g: ਬਜੇ ਭੇਰਿ ਭੇਰੀ ਜੁਝਾਰੇ ਝਣੰਕੇ ॥
106.t: baje bher bheree jujhaare jhana(n)ke ||
106.e: The sound of drums rises in the battle and the warriors glisten their weapons.

107.g: ਪਰੀ ਕੁਟ ਕੁਟੰ ਲਗੇ ਧੀਰ ਧਕੇ ॥
107.t: paree kuT kuTa(n) lage dheer dhake ||
107.e: There is a great rush of blows and the men of endurance are experiencing shocks.
The vultures shriek and the clarionets are being played.
It appears that terrible tigers are roaring and roaming.8.85.
On the other side the demon warrior Rkat Beej was infuriated.

107.g: ਪ੍ਰਹਾਰੇ ਭਲੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਸੋ ਆਨਿ ਤੀਰੰ ॥
107.t: prahaare bhalee bhaat so aan teera(n) ||
107.e: He shot his arrows very dexterously.

107.g: ਉਤੇ ਦਉਰ ਦੇਵੀ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਖਗ ਪਾਤੰ ॥
107.t: aute dhaur dhevee kariyo khag paata(n) ||
107.e: The goddess then speedily struck her sword.

107.g: ਗਰਿਯੋ ਮੂਰਛਾ ਹੁਐ ਭਯੋ ਜਾਨੁ ਘਾਤੰ ॥੯॥੮੬॥
107.t: gariyo moorachhaa huaai bhayo jaan ghaata(n) ||9||86||
107.e: Which cused the demon to fall senseless, it seemed that he has passed away.9.86.
When he came to senses, the mighty hero roared.

107.g: ਘਰੀ ਚਾਰ ਲਉ ਸਾਰ ਸੋ ਸਾਰ ਬਜਿਯੋ ॥
107.t: gharee chaar lau saar so saar bajiyo ||
107.e: For four gharis, the steel clasged with steel.

107.g: ਲਗੇ ਬਾਣ ਸ੍ਰੋਣੰ ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਭੂਮਿ ਜੁਧੇ ॥
107.t: lage baan srona(n) giriyo bhoom judhe ||
107.e: With the infliction of the arrow of the goddess, the blood of Rakat Beej began to fall on the ground.

107.g: ਉਠੇ ਬੀਰ ਤੇਤੇ ਕੀਏ ਨਾਦ ਕ੍ਰੁਧੰ ॥੧੦॥੮੭॥
107.t: auThe beer tete ke'ee naadh krudha(n) ||10||87||
107.e: With innumerable drops of blood arose innumerable Rakat Beejas, who began to shout with rage.10.87

107.g: ਉਠੇ ਬੀਰ ਜੇਤੇ ਤਿਤੇ ਕਾਲ ਕੂਟੇ ॥
107.t: auThe beer jete tite kaal kooTe ||
107.e: All the warriors who arose, were destroyed by Kali.

107.g: ਪਰੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ਕਹੂੰ ਗਾਤ ਟੂਟੇ ॥
107.t: pare charam barama(n) kahoo(n) gaat TooTe ||
107.e: Somewhere their shields, armour and wounded bodies are lying scattered

107.g: ਜਿਤੀ ਭੂਮਿ ਮਧੰ ਪਰੀ ਸ੍ਰੋਣ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
107.t: jitee bhoom madha(n) paree sron dhaara(n) ||
107.e: With all the drops of blood that fall on the ground.

107.g: ਜਗੇ ਸੂਰ ਤੇਤੇ ਕੀਏ ਮਾਰ ਮਾਰੰ ॥੧੧॥੮੮॥
107.t: jage soor tete ke'ee maar maara(n) ||11||88||
107.e: The same number of warriors arise shouting “kill, kill”. 11.88.

107.g: ਪਰੀ ਕੁਟ ਕੁਟੰ ਰੁਲੇ ਤਛ ਮੁਛੰ ॥
107.t: paree kuT kuTa(n) rule tachh muchha(n) ||
107.e: There were struck blows after blows and the warriors being chopped are rolling in dust.

107.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਮੁੰਡ ਤੁੰਡੰ ਕਹੂੰ ਮਾਸੁ ਮੁਛੰ ॥
107.t: kahoo(n) mu(n)dd tu(n)dda(n) kahoo(n) maas muchha(n) ||
107.e: Their heads, faces and pieces of flesh are lying scattered.

107.g: ਭਯੋ ਚਾਰ ਸੈ ਕੋਸ ਲਉ ਬੀਰ ਖੇਤੰ ॥
107.t: bhayo chaar sai kos lau beer kheta(n) ||
107.e: For four hundred kos, the battlefield was occupied by warriors.
Most of whom are lying dead or senseless.12.89.
RASAAVAL STANZA
They have fixed firmly their banners and in excitement their rage is increasing.13.90.
The warriors filled with delight are showering their arrows.
All the four types of forces are moving forward and staying in their arens.14.91.
With the use of all the weapons, the stream of blood began to flow.
The most honoured warriors arose with bow and arrows in their hands.15.92.
They are raaring in great anger, and the clarionets and drums are being played.
Filled with great fury, the wielders of canopies are much excited.16.93.
There are shouts after shouts and the forces are running hither and thither.
With great ire, the steel is being used, and the inebriated warriors look glorious.17.94.
The warriors with chopped limbs have fallen and the red blood appears like flaming fire.
The jingling and the twanging sounds of weapons are being heard.18.95.
The weapons are being struck with clinking sound and both sides wan their victory.
Many are intoxicated with wine and in great fury, they appear highly inflamed.19.96.

108.e: They are flushed with rage and are absorbed in waging war.
They offer arrows and are discussing archery.20.97.
The heroes are absorbed in heroic feats and are rainiong the shafts.
They are penetrating into the warrior-stronghold and do not turn away their eyes from it.21.98.
They are striking their weapons, facing the enemy and are pulling their bow-strings.
They are showering the arrows and striking the sharp steel-arms.22.99.
The stream of blood has become full and the houris are roaming in the sky.
The goddess Kali is roaring in the firmament and the female demon of the begging bowl is laughing.23.100.
Somewhere there are dead horses and somewhere the fallen mighty warriors.
Somewhere there are broken shields and somewhere the wounded elephants are roaming.24.101.
Somewhere the armour is penetrated and the inflicted skein is being seen.
Somewhere there are chopped elephants and somewhere the saddles of horses are seen cut down.25.102.
The brave warriors are engaged in inimical acts, all of them are fightning with their weapons.
Realising the presence of warriors in the battlefield, the ghosts and evil spirits are dancing.26.103.
The meat-eaters are dancing, those who roam in the sky, are laughing.
The crows are cawing and the elegant warriors are intoxicated.27.104.
The wears of canopies are full of fury and from their bows shoot their arrows.
They are desirous of their victory and thus are shooting their sharp shafts.28.105.
Ganas, Gandharvas, spies, minstrels and the Siddhas with miraculous powers.
All of them laugh and the warriors are inebriatedwith rage.29.106.
The vampires are belching and the egoist warriors are shouting.
The drums are creating loud sound and there are clanging noises.30.107.
The mighty warriors are roaring and the new instruments are being sounded.
The trumpets are resounding and the forces of Durga and the demons are fighting.31.108.

109.e: BIJAI STANZA

109.g: ਜੇਤਕ ਬਾਣ ਚਲੇ ਅਰਿ ਓਰ ਤੇ ਫੂਲ ਕੀ ਮਾਲ ਹੁਐ ਕੰਠਿ ਬਿਰਾਜੇ ॥
109.t: jetak baan chale ar or te fool kee maal huaai ka(n)Th biraaje ||
109.e: All the arrows shot by the enemy bedeck as garlands of flowers around the neck of the goddess.

109.g: ਦਾਨਵ ਪੁੰਗਵ ਪੇਖਿ ਅਚੰਭਵ ਛੋਡਿ ਭਜੇ ਰਣ ਏਕ ਨ ਗਾਜੇ ॥
109.t: dhaanav pu(n)gav pekh acha(n)bhav chhodd bhaje ran ek na gaaje ||
109.e: Seeing this wonder the forces of the enemy have run away from the battlefield and none could stay there.

109.g: ਕੁੰਜਰ ਪੁੰਜ ਗਿਰੇ ਤਿਹ ਠਉਰ ਭਰੇ ਸਭ ਸ੍ਰੋਣਤ ਪੈ ਗਨ ਤਾਜੇ ॥
109.t: ku(n)jar pu(n)j gire teh Thaur bhare sabh sronat pai gan taaje ||
109.e: Many elephants have fallen at that place alongwith many healthy steeds, all are smeared with blood.

109.g: ਜਾਨੁਕ ਨੀਰਧ ਮਧਿ ਛਪੇ ਭ੍ਰਮਿ ਭੂਧਰ ਕੇ ਭਯ ਤੇ ਨਗ ਭਾਜੇ ॥੩੨॥੧੦੯॥
109.t: jaanuk neeradh madh chhape bhram bhoodhar ke bhay te nag bhaaje ||32||109||
109.e: It appears that running away out of the fear of Indra, the mountains have hidden themselves in the sea.32.109.
MANOHAR STANZA

109.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਜਗਮਾਤ ਕਮਾਨ ਲੈ ਹਾਥਿ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥਨਿ ਸੰਖ ਪ੍ਰਜ੍ਰਯੋ ਜਬ ਜੁਧੰ ॥
109.t: sree jagamaat kamaan lai haath pramaathan sa(n)kh prajrayo jab judha(n) ||
109.e: When the Mother of Universe waged the war, holding her bow in her hand and blowing her conch

109.g: ਗਾਤਹ ਸੈਣ ਸੰਘਾਰਤ ਸੂਰ ਬਬਕਤਿ ਸਿੰਘ ਭ੍ਰਮ੍ਯੋ ਰਣਿ ਕ੍ਰੁਧੰ ॥
109.t: gaateh sain sa(n)ghaarat soor babakat si(n)gh bhramayo ran krudha(n) ||
109.e: Her lion walked roaring in the field in great ire, crushing and destroying the forces of the enemy.

109.g: ਕਉਚਹਿ ਭੇਦਿ ਅਭੇਦਿਤ ਅੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਉਤੰਗ ਸੋ ਸੋਭਿਤ ਸੁਧੰ ॥
109.t: kaucheh bhedh abhedhit a(n)g sura(n)g uta(n)g so sobhit sudha(n) ||
109.e: He smashed the clinging helmets of soldiers and is basking in the blood of their wounds.

109.g: ਮਾਨੋ ਬਿਸਾਲ ਬੜਵਾਨਲ ਜੁਆਲ ਸਮੁਦ੍ਰ ਕੇ ਮਧਿ ਬਿਰਾਜਤ ਉਧੰ ॥੩੩॥੧੧੦॥
109.t: maano bisaal baRavaanal juaal samudhr ke madh biraajat udha(n) ||33||110||
109.e: The rising flames of fire extended in midst of the ocean.33.110.

109.g: ਪੂਰ ਰਹੀ ਭਵਿ ਭੂਰ ਧਨੁਰ ਧੁਨਿ ਧੂਰ ਉਡੀ ਨਭ ਮੰਡਲ ਛਾਯੋ ॥
109.t: poor rahee bhav bhoor dhanur dhun dhoor uddee nabh ma(n)ddal chhaayo ||
109.e: The sound of the bow permeates the whole universe and the flying dust of the battlefield hath spread over the whole firmament.

109.g: ਨੂਰ ਭਰੇ ਮੁਖ ਮਾਰਿ ਗਿਰੇ ਰਣਿ ਹੂਰਨ ਹੇਰਿ ਹੀਯੋ ਹੁਲਸਾਯੋ ॥
109.t: noor bhare mukh maar gire ran hooran her heeyo hulasaayo ||
109.e: The brightened faces have fallen after receiving blows and seeing them, the hearts of the vampires have been pleased.

109.g: ਪੂਰਣ ਰੋਸ ਭਰੇ ਅਰਿ ਤੂਰਣ ਪੂਰਿ ਪਰੇ ਰਣ ਭੂਮਿ ਸੁਹਾਯੋ ॥
109.t: pooran ros bhare ar tooran poor pare ran bhoom suhaayo ||
109.e: The forces of the extremely infuriated enemies are elegantly stationed in the whole battlefield

109.g: ਚੂਰ ਭਏ ਅਰਿ ਰੂਰੇ ਗਿਰੇ ਭਟ ਚੂਰਣ ਜਾਨੁਕ ਬੈਦ ਬਨਾਯੋ ॥੩੪॥੧੧੧॥
109.t: choor bhe ar roore gire bhaT chooran jaanuk baidh banaayo ||34||111||
109.e: Winsome and youthful warriors are falling in bits in this manner as though the apothecary after grinding the earth, hath prepared the digestive medicine (Churan).34.111.
SANGEET BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The sounds of the blows of the daggers and swords are being heard.
The sounds of the shafts and gunshots are being heard.
Various sounds of musical instruments are resounding.
The warriors are roaring and shouting loudly.35.112.
The great heroes have been struck.
And the brave fighters are belching.36.113.
The worriors seem pleased on shooting sharp arrows on the bodies.
There are loud shouts with porofound resoundings, and the poets describe them in their verses.37.114.
The demons are running away and the heroes are shouting loudly.
The sounds are produced by the striking axes and daggers. The arrows and the guns are creating their own noses.38.115.
The loud noise of drums and the resounding of conches and trumpets is being heard in the battlefield.
The musical instruments of the warriors are being played and the ghosts and goblins are dancing.39.116.
The noises of the arrows and shafts, daggers and swords are being heard.
The music of the musical instruments and the drumming of the trumpets resounds and the warriors and chieftains are doing their job amidst such resonance.40.117.
The conches, clarionets and the drums resounded.
The trumpets and musical instruments produced their sounds and alongwith their resonance, the warriors thundered.41.118.
NARAAJ STANZA
All the forms of demons created with the spilling of the blood of Rakat Beej on ground, were killed by the goddess.
All the forms that are going to materialize, will also be destroyed by Durga.42.119.
With the showering of weapons (on Rakat Beej), the currents of blood ooxed out (from the body of Rakat Beej).
All the drops that fell (on the ground), the goddess Kali drank them all.43.120.
RASAAVAL STANZA
The demon-chief Rakat Beej became bloodless and his limbs became very weak.
Ultimatley he fell down on the ground wavering like the clound on he earth.44.121.
All the gods were pleased (to see this) and they showered the flowers.
Rakat Beej was killed and in this way the goddess saved the saints.45.122.

109.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਰਕਤ ਬੀਰਜ ਬਧਹ ਚਤੁਰਥ ਧਿਆਯ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੪॥
109.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre rakat beeraj badheh chaturath dhiaay sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||4||
109.e: Thus the Fourth Chapter entitled “The Killing of Rakat Beej” of Chandi Charitra of BACHITTAR is completed.4.
Now the battle with Nisumbh is described:
DOHRA

109.g: ਸੁੰਭ ਨਿਸੁੰਭ ਸੁਣਿਯੋ ਜਬੈ ਰਕਤਬੀਰਜ ਕੋ ਨਾਸ ॥
109.t: su(n)bh nisu(n)bh suniyo jabai rakatabeeraj ko naas ||
109.e: When Sumbh and Nisumbh heard about the destruction of Rakat Beej

109.g: ਆਪ ਚੜਤ ਭੈ ਜੋਰਿ ਦਲ ਸਜੇ ਪਰਸੁ ਅਰੁ ਪਾਸਿ ॥੧॥੧੨੩॥
109.t: aap chaRat bhai jor dhal saje paras ar paas ||1||123||
109.e: They marched forward themselves gathering their forces and bedecking themselves with axes and nooses.1.123.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The mighty warriors Sumbh and Nisumbh began the invasion.

109.g: ਉਠੇ ਨਦ ਨਾਦੰ ਸੁ ਧਉਸਾ ਧੁਕਾਰੰ ॥
109.t: auThe nadh naadha(n) su dhausaa dhukaara(n) ||
109.e: The sound of musical instruments and trumpets resounded.

109.g: ਭਈ ਅਸਟ ਸੈ ਕੋਸ ਲਉ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਛਾਯੰ ॥
109.t: bhiee asaT sai kos lau chhatr chhaaya(n) ||
109.e: The shade of canopies spread over eight hundred kos.

109.g: ਭਜੇ ਚੰਦ ਸੂਰੰ ਡਰਿਯੋ ਦੇਵ ਰਾਯੰ ॥੨॥੧੨੪॥
109.t: bhaje cha(n)dh soora(n) ddariyo dhev raaya(n) ||2||124||
109.e: And the sun and moon sped away and Indra, the king of gods was frightened.2.124.

109.g: ਭਕਾ ਭੁੰਕ ਭੇਰੀ ਢਕਾ ਢੁੰਕ ਢੋਲੰ ॥
109.t: bhakaa bhu(n)k bheree ddakaa ddu(n)k ddola(n) ||
109.e: The drum and the tabor reverberated.

110.g: ਫਟੀ ਨਖ ਸਿੰਘੰ ਮੁਖੰ ਡਢ ਕੋਲੰ ॥
110.t: faTee nakh si(n)gha(n) mukha(n) ddadd kola(n) ||
110.e: The earth splitted because of the roar of the lion and the attack of his nails.

110.g: ਡਮਾ ਡੰਮਿ ਡਉਰੂ ਡਕਾ ਡੁੰਕ ਡੰਕੰ ॥
110.t: ddamaa dda(n)m ddauroo ddakaa ddu(n)k dda(n)ka(n) ||
110.e: The sound of the trumpets and the tabors is being heard.
And the huge vultures and crows are shrieking and flying .3.125.

110.g: ਖੁਰੰ ਖੇਹ ਉਠੀ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਗੈਨ ਪੂਰੰ ॥
110.t: khura(n) kheh uThee rahiyo gain poora(n) ||
110.e: The sky is filled with the dust risen by the hooves of the animals.

110.g: ਦਲੇ ਸਿੰਧੁ ਬਿਧੰ ਭਏ ਪਬ ਚੂਰੰ ॥
110.t: dhale si(n)dh bidha(n) bhe pab choora(n) ||
110.e: And these animals have broken into prices Vidhyachal mountain and other small mounts.

110.g: ਸੁਣੋ ਸੋਰ ਕਾਲੀ ਗਹੈ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਣੰ ॥
110.t: suno sor kaalee gahai sasatr paana(n) ||
110.e: The goddess Kali hearing the din, held her weapons in her hands.
While roaring she ate up the limps of the killed youthful warriors.4.126.
RASAAVAL STANZA
The brave warriors are thundering and the horses are speedily moving.
The bows are being pulled and the shafts are raining.5.127.
From this side the lion hath roared and the conch hath been blown.
Its sound is filling the atmosphere. The sky is filled with the dust risen from the battlefield.6.128.
The warriors have bedecked themselves with weapons and are thundering like clouds.
They are furiously moving, carrying countless weapons.7.129.
From all four sides the warriors are closing their ranks, shouting “kill, kill”.
The mighty warriors are thundering and countless weapons are striking blows.8.130.
Carrying the powerful weapons in their hands, their faces and eyes are becoming blood-red.
In great fury, they are marching and showering their arrows.9.131.
Many of the tyrants have been killed and consequently countless weapons are lying scattered hither and thither.
The goddess hath been pleased and is showering her arrows.10.132.
BELI BINDRAM STANZA
The crows are uttering “caw, caw” and the blood of mighty heroes is flowing.
The arrows and swords are waving in the wind and the ghosts and evil spirits are catching the dead.11.133.
The tobors are resounding and the swords are glistening.
The sounds of striking daggers and the thundering of the warriors are being heard.12.134.
The arrows shot from the bows create surprises in the minds of the warriors.
The vampires are fearing from the sound of the labor and the female demons are wandering and laughing.13.135.
Because of the rain of sharp arrows, the blood is splashing.

111.e: Many warriors are roaring and the jackals, in particular, being pleased, are howling.14.136.
The immortal Durga, the dyer with blood, is moving, pleased with her task.
The roaring lion is running and such is the continuous situation in the battlefield.15.137.
The drums are resounding and the daggers are clanking.
The fighting warriors, in great fury, are striking their swords.16.138.
DOHRA

111.g: ਭਜੀ ਚਮੂੰ ਸਬ ਦਾਨਵੀ ਸੁੰਭ ਨਿਰਖ ਨਿਜ ਨੈਣ ॥
111.t: bhajee chamoo(n) sab dhaanavee su(n)bh nirakh nij nain ||
111.e: Seeing with his own eyes the running demon-army

111.g: ਨਿਕਟ ਬਿਕਟ ਭਟ ਜੇ ਹੁਤੇ ਤਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਤਿ ਬੁਲਿਯੋ ਬੈਣ ॥੧੭॥੧੩੯॥
111.t: nikaT bikaT bhaT je hute tin prat buliyo bain ||17||139||
111.e: Sumbh spoke to the mighty warriors standing near him.17.139.
NARAAJ STANZA
Srriking his foot on the earth Sumbh sent Nisumbh saying
“Go immediately and bring Durga after binding her.”18.140.
Thundering and in great fury, he marched forward alongwith his army.
The trumpets were sounded, hearing which caused the king of gods run away.19.141.
Beating his drums, he marched forward taking countless warriors with him.
He called and gathered so many brave fighters, seeing whom the gods were frightened.20.142.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA
The king of gods trembled and reated all his painful circumstances to Lord Shiva.
When he gave out all his feflections, Shiva asked him about the number of his warriors.21.143.
(He further asked him) to make friends all others through all possible means
So that the victory of the mother of the world is assured.22.144.
Bring out all your powers, and send them in the war
So that they may go before enemies and in great rage destroy them.23.145.
The wise gods did as advised
And sent their boundless powers from amoungst themselves to the battlefield.24.146.
BIRADH NIRAAJ STANZA

111.g: ਚਲੀ ਸਕਤਿ ਸੀਘ੍ਰ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਣਿ ਪਾਣਿ ਧਾਰ ਕੈ ॥
111.t: chalee sakat seeghr sree kirapaan paan dhaar kai ||
111.e: Immediately the powers wore the sword and went towards the arena of war

111.g: ਉਠੇ ਸੁ ਗ੍ਰਿਧ ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਡਉਰ ਡਾਕਣੀ ਡਕਾਰ ਕੈ ॥
111.t: auThe su giradh biradh ddaur ddaakanee ddakaar kai ||
111.e: And with them ran the great vultures nd belching vampires.

111.g: ਹਸੇ ਸੁ ਰੰਗ ਕੰਕ ਬੰਕਯੰ ਕਬੰਧ ਅੰਧ ਉਠਹੀ ॥
111.t: hase su ra(n)g ka(n)k ba(n)kaya(n) kaba(n)dh a(n)dh uThahee ||
111.e: The terrible crows smiled and the blind headless bodies also moved.

111.g: ਬਿਸੇਖ ਦੇਵਤਾ ਰੁ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਣ ਧਾਰ ਬੁਠਹੀ ॥੨੫॥੧੪੭॥
111.t: bisekh dhevataa r beer baan dhaar buThahee ||25||147||
111.e: From this side, the gods and other heroes began to shower shafts.25.147.
RASAAVAL STANZA
All the powers came and went back paying their obeisance.
They wore terrible arms and killed many great warriors.26.148.
Their faces and eyes are reddened with blood and they are uttering challenging words from their mouths.
They are holding arms, daggers and swords in their hands.27.149.
From the other side, the demons are thundering, and the trumpets are resounding.
They are wearing cruel armour, holding winsome shields in their hands.28.150.
They began to roar from all the four sides and hearing their voices, all the gods trembled.
The sharp arrows were shot and the garments and fly-whisks were torn.29.151.
Inebriated with extreme ferocity, the warriors are seen with brightened faces.
The goddess Durga, being very much pleased, hath begun showering the rain of arrows.30.152.
On this side, the goddess is busy in killing and on the other side the lion is tearing up all.
Hearing the roars of the Ganas (attendants) of Shiva, the demons have become frightened.31.153.

112.e: There was rain of arrows and with this the goddess became victorious.
All the tyrants were killed by the goddess and the Mother saved the saints.32.154.
The goddess killed Nisumbh and destroyed the army of demons.
On this side the lion roared and form the other side all the demons fled.33.155.
On the victory of the army of gods, there was rain of flowers.
The saints hailed it nd the demos trembled with fear.34.156.

112.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਨਿਸੁੰਭ ਬਧਹ ਪੰਚਮੋ ਧਿਆਇ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੫॥
112.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre nisu(n)bh badheh pa(n)chamo dhiaai sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||5||
112.e: Here ends the Fifth Chapter entitled ‘The Killing of Nisumbh’ of Chandi Charitra in BACHITTAR NATAK.5.
Now the war with Sumbh is described:
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

112.g: ਲਘੁੰ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਜੁਝਿਯੋ ਸੁਨਿਯੋ ਸੁੰਭ ਰਾਯੰ ॥
112.t: laghu(n) bhraat jujhiyo suniyo su(n)bh raaya(n) ||
112.e: When Sumbh heard about the death of his younger brother

112.g: ਸਜੈ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰੰ ਚੜਿਯੋ ਚਉਪ ਚਾਯੰ ॥
112.t: sajai sasatr asatra(n) chaRiyo chaup chaaya(n) ||
112.e: He, in fury and excitement, marched forward to wage war, bedecking himself with arms and amour.

112.g: ਭਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਉਚੰ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਪੂਰ ਗੈਣੰ ॥
112.t: bhayo naadh ucha(n) rahiyo poor gaina(n) ||
112.e: There was terrible sound which permeted in the firmament.
Hearing this sound, the gods, demons and Shiva all trembled.1.157.

112.g: ਡਰਿਯੋ ਚਾਰ ਬਕਤ੍ਰੰ ਟਰਿਯੋ ਦੇਵ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
112.t: ddariyo chaar bakatra(n) Tariyo dhev raaja(n) ||
112.e: Brahma was fightened and the throne of Indra, the king of gods, wavered.

112.g: ਡਿਗੇ ਪਬ ਸਰਬੰ ਸ੍ਰਜੇ ਸੁਭ ਸਾਜੰ ॥
112.t: ddige pab saraba(n) sraje subh saaja(n) ||
112.e: Seeing the bedecked form of the demon-king, the mountains also began to fall.

112.g: ਪਰੇ ਹੂਹ ਦੈ ਕੈ ਭਰੇ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ॥
112.t: pare hooh dhai kai bhare loh kroha(n) ||
112.e: Shriking and screaming in great ire the demons appear

112.g: ਮਨੋ ਮੇਰ ਕੋ ਸਾਤਵੋ ਸ੍ਰਿੰਗ ਸੋਹੰ ॥੨॥੧੫੮॥
112.t: mano mer ko saatavo sira(n)g soha(n) ||2||158||
112.e: Like the seventh peak of Sumeru mountain.2.158.

112.g: ਸਜਿਯੋ ਸੈਨ ਸੁਭੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਉਚੰ ॥
112.t: sajiyo sain subha(n) keeyo naadh ucha(n) ||
112.e: Bedecking himself, Sumbh raised a terrible sound
Hearing which the pregnancy of women was miscarried.

112.g: ਪਰਿਯੋ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ਉਠੀ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਝਾਰੰ ॥
112.t: pariyo loh kroha(n) uThee sasatr jhaara(n) ||
112.e: The furious warriors made continuous use of steel arms and the weapons began to rain.
The voices of vultures and vampires were heard in the battlefield.3.159.

112.g: ਬਹੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰੰ ਕਟੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ॥
112.t: bahe sasatr asatra(n) kaTe charam barama(n) ||
112.e: With the use of weapons and arms, the winsome armours were being cut

112.g: ਭਲੇ ਕੈ ਨਿਬਾਹਿਯੋ ਭਟੰ ਸੁਆਮਿ ਧਰਮੰ ॥
112.t: bhale kai nibaahiyo bhaTa(n) suaam dharama(n) ||
112.e: And the warriors performed their religious duties in a nice manner.

112.g: ਉਠੀ ਕੂਹ ਜੂਹੰ ਗਿਰੇ ਚਉਰ ਚੀਰੰ ॥
112.t: auThee kooh jooha(n) gire chaur cheera(n) ||
112.e: There was consternation in the whole battlefield and the canopies and garments began to fall.

112.g: ਰੁਲੇ ਤਛ ਮੁਛੰ ਪਰੀ ਗਛ ਤੀਰੰ ॥੪॥੧੬੦॥
112.t: rule tachh muchha(n) paree gachh teera(n) ||4||160||
112.e: The chopped bodies were being trodden in the dust and because of the infliction of arrows, the warriors were becoming senseless.4.160.
The warriors fell in the battlefield along with the elephants and goads.
The headless trunks began to dance senselessly.

112.g: ਉਡੈ ਗ੍ਰਿਧ ਬ੍ਰਿਧੰ ਰੜੈ ਕੰਕ ਬੰਕੰ ॥
112.t: auddai giradh biradha(n) raRai ka(n)k ba(n)ka(n) ||
112.e: The large-sized vultures began to fly and the crows with curved beaks began to caw.

112.g: ਭਕਾ ਭੁੰਕ ਭੇਰੀ ਡਾਹ ਡੂਹ ਡੰਕੰ ॥੫॥੧੬੧॥
112.t: bhakaa bhu(n)k bheree ddaeh ddooh dda(n)ka(n) ||5||161||
112.e: The frightful sound of drums and the clatter of tabors was heard.5.161.

112.g: ਟਕਾ ਟੁਕ ਟੋਪੰ ਢਕਾ ਢੁਕ ਢਾਲੰ ॥
112.t: Takaa Tuk Topa(n) ddakaa dduk ddaala(n) ||
112.e: There was knocking of helmets and the sound of blows on the shields.
The swords began to chop the bodies with terrible noises.

112.g: ਹਲਾ ਚਾਲ ਬੀਰੰ ਧਮਾ ਧੰਮਿ ਸਾਗੰ ॥
112.t: halaa chaal beera(n) dhamaa dha(n)m saaga(n) ||
112.e: The warriors were attacked continuously and the clatter of daggers was being heard.

112.g: ਪਰੀ ਹਾਲ ਹੂਲੰ ਸੁਣਿਯੋ ਲੋਗ ਨਾਗੰ ॥੬॥੧੬੨॥
112.t: paree haal hoola(n) suniyo log naaga(n) ||6||162||
112.e: There was such consternation that its noise was heard in the netherworld by the Nagas.6.162.
The vampires, female demons, ghosts
Headless trunks and the kapalikas are dancing in the battlefield.
All the gods appear pleased and the demon-king is getting furious.

112.g: ਕਿਧੋ ਅਗਨਿ ਜੁਆਲੰ ਭਯੋ ਆਪ ਭੇਸੰ ॥੭॥੧੬੩॥
112.t: kidho agan juaala(n) bhayo aap bhesa(n) ||7||163||
112.e: It appears that the flame of fire is blazing.7.163.
DOHRA

112.g: ਸੁੰਭਾਸੁਰ ਜੇਤਿਕੁ ਅਸੁਰ ਪਠਏ ਕੋਪੁ ਬਢਾਇ ॥
112.t: su(n)bhaasur jetik asur paThe kop baddai ||
112.e: All those demons, sent by Sumbh, I great fury

112.g: ਤੇ ਦੇਬੀ ਸੋਖਤ ਕਰੇ ਬੂੰਦ ਤਵਾ ਕੀ ਨਿਆਇ ॥੮॥੧੬੪॥
112.t: te dhebee sokhat kare boo(n)dh tavaa kee niaai ||8||164||
112.e: Were destroyed by the goddess like the water-drops on the hot iron-griddle.8.164.
NARAAJ STANZA

113.e: He (demon-king) marched forward, in great fury, bedecking himself with an army of warriors.
He moved, wearing his weapons, with shouts of “kill, kill”.9.165.
SANGEET MADHUBHAAE STANZA
There were sounds of clattering and twanging.
The warriors were shouting loudly and thundering profoundly.10.166.
The resonance of trumpets was precipitating the youthful warriors.
Those brave men were jumping and engaged in chivalrous acts. 11.167.
In great rage, the warriors showed signs of anger on their faces.
They were striking their swords.12.168.
The arrows shot by the warriors were blowing away
And throwing down those coming in front of them.13.169.
The winsome brave horse-riders were fighting courageously.14.170.
Several types of noise were spreading in the battlefield.15.171.
The arms were being swung in the battlefield and the stream of blood was flowing.
Manifesting her frightful form, Kapali Durga was dancing.16.172.
NARAAJ STANZA
Killing the countless tyrants, Durga effaced many sufferings.
The blinds trunks were rising and moving and they were being felled on the ground with the shower of arrows.17.173.
The sounds of working bows and striking daggers are being heard.
In this continuous shower of arrows the significantly honoured heroes have been tasted.18.174.
SANGEET NARAAJ STANZA
Alongwith the clattering of swords, the daggers are striking fastly.
The heroic warriors have been inspired to face the fighters. 19.175.
RASAAVAL STANZA

114.e: The striking swords are glistening and the daggers are striking fastly.
The brave warriors are giving blows of maces on the back of the lion.20.176.
Somewhere the blood is being drunk, somewhere the head is lying broken.
Somewhere there is din and somewhere the heroes are rising again.21.177.
Somewhere the warriors are lying in the dust, somewhere there is repetition of the shouts of “kill, kill”.
Somewhere the minstrels are eulogizing the warriors and somewhere warriors with wounded bellies are lying down.22.178.
The bearers of canopies are running away and somewhere the blood is being flowin.
Somewhere the tyrants are being destroyed and the warriors are running hither and thither like the Persian wheel.23.179.
All the warriors are bedecked with the bow
And all of them are holding their swords like the dreadful saw.24.180.
They are verily of dark complexion like the saltish sea.
Though they have been destroyed several times, but still they are shouting “kill, kill”.25.181.
Bhavani (Durga) hath destroyed all like the jawahan plant destroyed by the continuous rain.
Many other brave demons have been crushed under her feet.26.182.
The enemies have been destroyed in the first round and thrown away. They have been struck on their bodies with weapons and made cool (by death).
Many mighty warriors have been killed and the sound of the drums is continuously being heard.27.183.
Wonderful type of arrows have been shot and because of them many fighters have expired.
When the demon-warriors of great might saw the goddess in person, they became senseless.28.184
Many brave fighters were torn by the lion and thrown on the ground.
And many huge demons were personally killed and destroyed by the goddess.29.185.
Many real heroes who stuck fast before the goddess.
And who were extremely hard-hearted and renowned for their mercilessness ultimately ran away.30.186.
The egoist warriors with brightened faces who ran forward.
And also the mighty and furious heroes were killed by the dreadful death.31.187.
DOHRA

114.g: ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਦੁਸਟ ਪ੍ਰਜਾਰ ਕੈ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਕਰਿ ਲੀਨ ॥
114.t: eeh bidh dhusaT prajaar kai sasatr asatr kar leen ||
114.e: In this way, destroying the tyrants, Durga again wore her weapons and armour.

114.g: ਬਾਣ ਬੂੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮੈ ਬਰਖ ਸਿੰਘ ਨਾਦ ਪੁਨਿ ਕੀਨ ॥੩੨॥੧੮੮॥
114.t: baan boo(n)dh pirathamai barakh si(n)gh naadh pun keen ||32||188||
114.e: At first she showered her arrows and then her lion roared heavily.32.188.
RASAAVAL STANZA
When the demon-king Sumbh heard all that had happened, he marched forward in great excitement.
His soldiers bedecked with weapons came forward to wage war.33.189.
The sound created by drums, bows
And trumpets were continuously heard.34.190.
The swords of the persistent and renowned fighters glistened.
The great heroes raised loud shouts and the trumpets sounded.35.191.
The demons thundered from all the four sides and the gods collectively trembled.
Showering her arrows Durga herself is testing the dtength of all.36.192.
CHAUPAI
All those demons, carrying their weapons, came in front of the goddess were all subjected to death.
The edges of the swords are glistening and the headless trunks, in dreadful forms are raising their voices.37.193.

115.e: DOHRA

115.g: ਹੈ ਗੈ ਰਥ ਪੈਦਲ ਕਟੇ ਬਚਿਯੋ ਨ ਜੀਵਤ ਕੋਇ ॥
115.t: hai gai rath paidhal kaTe bachiyo na jeevat koi ||
115.e: The elephants, horses and warriors on foot were all chopped and none could survive.

115.g: ਤਬ ਆਪੇ ਨਿਕਸਿਯੋ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਸੁੰਭ ਕਰੈ ਸੋ ਹੋਇ ॥੩੮॥੧੯੪॥
115.t: tab aape nikasiyo nirapat su(n)bh karai so hoi ||38||194||
115.e: Then the king Sumbh himself marched forward for war and on seeing him it appears that whatever he desires, he will achive.38.194.
CHAUPI
On this side, Durga after reflecting, called a female messenger of Shiva and making her conscious gave this message in her ear:
“Send Lord Shiva to the place, where the demon-king is standing.”39.195.

115.g: ਸਿਵ ਦੂਤੀ ਜਬ ਇਮ ਸੁਨ ਪਾਵਾ ॥
115.t: siv dhootee jab im sun paavaa ||

115.e: When the female messenger of Shiva heard this, she sent Shiva as a messenger of Shiva

115.g: ਸਿਵ ਦੂਤੀ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਭਯੋ ਨਾਮਾ ॥
115.t: siv dhootee taa te bhayo naamaa ||

115.e: Since that day, the name of Durga became" shiv- Duti" ( the messenger of shiva ), all men and women know this.40.196.

115.g: ਸਿਵ ਕਹੀ ਦੈਤ ਰਾਜ ਸੁਨਿ ਬਾਤਾ ॥
115.t: siv kahee dhait raaj sun baataa ||

115.e: Shiva said to the demon-king, “Listen to my words, the mother of she universe hath said this
“That either you return the kingdom to gods or wage the war with me.”41.197.

115.g: ਦੈਤ ਰਾਜ ਇਹ ਬਾਤ ਨ ਮਾਨੀ ॥
115.t: dhait raaj ieh baat na maanee ||

115.e: The demon-king Sumbh did not accept this proposal and in his pride, marched forward for war.
The place where Kali, like death, was thundering, that demon-king reached there.42.198.
There the edges of sword glistened and the ghosts, goblins and evil spirits began to dance.
There the blind headless trunks came into motion senselessly. There many Bhairavas and Bhimas began to roam.43.199.
The clarionets, drums and trumpets sounded any many types.
The tambourines, tabors etc., were played loudly and the musical instruments like Shahnai etc., were being played in such numbers that they cannot be counted.44.200.
MADHUBHAAR STANZA
The horses are neighing and the trumpets are resounding.
The bedecked warriors are roaring profoundly.45.201.
The heroes coming near unhesitatingly are striking blows and jumping.
The smart warriors fight each other and the beautiful heroes are bedecking themselves. The heavenly damsels (apsaras) are feeling inspired.46.202.
The horses are being chopped and the faces are being torn.
The sound created by tridents are being heard. 47.203.
The trumpets are resounding and the youthful warriors are thundering.
The kings and chieftains are bedecked and the elephants are screeching.48.204.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
The beautiful horses are roaming hither and thither.
The elephants of the princes are roaring dreadfully.

116.g: ਬਜੇ ਸੰਖ ਭੇਰੀ ਉਠੈ ਸੰਖ ਨਾਦੰ ॥
116.t: baje sa(n)kh bheree uThai sa(n)kh naadha(n) ||
116.e: The sound of conches and drums is rising.
The clarionets are being played continuously.49.205.
The swords and daggers are producing their sounds.

116.g: ਉਠੀ ਕੂਹ ਜੂਹੰ ਭਈ ਰੇਲ ਪੇਲੰ ॥
116.t: auThee kooh jooha(n) bhiee rel pela(n) ||
116.e: There is vehement run in the whole battlefield.

116.g: ਰੁਲੇ ਤਛ ਮੁਛੰ ਗਿਰੇ ਚਉਰ ਚੀਰੰ ॥
116.t: rule tachh muchha(n) gire chaur cheera(n) ||
116.e: The bodies having been chopped and the garments and fly-whisks having been torn have fallen down.

116.g: ਕਹੂੰ ਹਥ ਮਥੰ ਕਹੂੰ ਬਰਮ ਬੀਰੰ ॥੫੦॥੨੦੬॥
116.t: kahoo(n) hath matha(n) kahoo(n) baram beera(n) ||50||206||
116.e: Somewhere the hands, somewhere the foreheads and somewhere the armours are lying scattered.50.206.
RASAAVAL STANZA
The mighty enemies are busy in fighting with all their weapons.
Holding their arms, they are shouting “kill, kill”.51.207.
Being completely dressed with their weapons the brave fighters are roaring.
There has been a volley of arrows producing hissing sounds.52.208.
Various types of musical instruments are being played and the Gandharvas are laughing.
The warriors after fixing their banners firmly are busy in fighting and their armours are being torn with arrows.53.209.
From all the four sides, the arrows are being showered.
The fierce and frightful warriors are busy in various types of prattle.54.210.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
Somewhere the brave fighters are being chopped and somewhere the arrows are being showered.
The horses without saddles are lying in dust in the battlefield.
The warriors of gods and demons both are fighting against one another.
It appears that the dreadful warriors are Bhisham Pitamahas.55.211.
The decorated horses and elephants are thundering
And the arrows of brave warriors are being shot.
The clatter of swords and the resounding of trumpets
Along the sounds of daggers and drums are being heard.56.212.

116.g: ਢਮਾ ਢਮ ਢੋਲੰ ਢਲਾ ਢੁਕ ਢਾਲੰ ॥
116.t: ddamaa ddam ddola(n) ddalaa dduk ddaala(n) ||
116.e: The sounds of drums and shields resound continuously
And the horses running hither and thither have cused consternation.

116.g: ਸਟਾ ਸਟ ਸੈਲੰ ਖਹਾ ਖੂਨਿ ਖਗੰ ॥
116.t: saTaa saT saila(n) khahaa khoon khaga(n) ||
116.e: The daggers are being struck violently and the swords are besmeared with blood.

116.g: ਤੁਟੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ਉਠੇ ਨਾਲ ਅਗੰ ॥੫੭॥੨੧੩॥
116.t: tuTe charam barama(n) uThe naal aga(n) ||57||213||
116.e: Te armours on the bodies of the warriors are breaking and the limbs are coming out with them.57.213.

116.g: ਉਠੇ ਅਗਿ ਨਾਲੰ ਖਹੇ ਖੋਲ ਖਗੰ ॥
116.t: auThe ag naala(n) khahe khol khaga(n) ||
116.e: The blows of swords on the helmets create flames of fire.
And in the utter darkness that has spread, the ghosts and goblins considering it night, have awakened.
The vampires are belching and the tabors are being played.
And in accompaniment with their sound, the ghosts and evil spirits are dancing.58.214.
BELI BINDRAM STNZA
All the blows being struck by the weapons have been annulled by the goddess Durga.
Beside these all other blows, that are being struck, are being annulled and the weapons are thrown on the ground by the goddess.59.215.
Kali herself made use of her weapons and made all the weapons of the demons ineffective.

117.e: When the gods saw (Sumbh) without weapons, they began to hail the goddess.60.216.
The musical instruments were played in the firmament and no0w the gods also began to raor.
The gods began to view repeatedly and raise shouts of victory.61.217.
Now in great rage in the battlefield, the dreadful Kali raised six hands of her arms powerfully
And struck them on the head of Sumbh and with one blow she destroyed the tyrant.62.218.
DOHRA

117.g: ਜਿਮ ਸੁੰਭਾਸੁਰ ਕੋ ਹਨਾ ਅਧਿਕ ਕੋਪ ਕੈ ਕਾਲਿ ॥
117.t: jim su(n)bhaasur ko hanaa adhik kop kai kaal ||
117.e: The manner in which, with extreme fury, Kali destroyed the demon-king Sumbh

117.g: ਤ੍ਰਯੋ ਸਾਧਨ ਕੇ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਸਭ ਚਾਬਤ ਜਾਹ ਕਰਾਲ ॥੬੩॥੨੧੯॥
117.t: trayo saadhan ke satr sabh chaabat jaeh karaal ||63||219||
117.e: All the enemies of the saints are destroyed in the same manner.63.219.

117.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਸੁੰਭ ਬਧਹ ਖਸਟਮੋ ਧਿਆਯ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੬॥
117.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre su(n)bh badheh khasaTamo dhiaay sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||6||
117.e: Here ends the Sixth Chapter entitled ‘The Killing of Sumbh’ of Chandi Charitra in BACHITTAR NATAK.6.
NOW THE WORDS OF VICTORY ARE RELATED:
BELI BINDRAM STANZA
All the gods are hailing the victory of the goddess and showering the flowers.
They brought the saffron and with great delight they applied the mark on their foreheds.1.220.
CHAUPAI
All of them extremely eulogized the goddess and repeated the mantra known as “Brahm-Kavach”.
All the saints were pleased because the tyrants have been destroyed.2.221.
The comfort of the saints increased in many ways and not even one demon could survive.
The mother of the universe ever helps the saints and is helpful to them everywhere.3.222.
Eulogy of the Goddess:
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
O Yoga-fire, Enlightener of the Earth! I salute Thee.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਸੁੰਭ ਹੰਤੀ ਨਮੋ ਕਰੂਰ ਕਾਲੰ ॥
117.t: namo su(n)bh ha(n)tee namo karoor kaala(n) ||
117.e: O the Destroyer of Sumbh and dreadful manifestation of Death!
O the Destroyer of Dhumar Nain , O the Destroyer of Rakat Beej!
O Blazing like fire Kalika! I salute Thee.4.223.
O Ambika! O Jambhaha (the killer of the demon Jambh) O manifestation of Light! I salute Thee.
O the killer of Chand and Mund! O the Sovereign of Sovereigns! I salute Thee.
O the sawer of the demon Chamar! O the one looking like a portrait! I salute Thee.
O the bearer of knowledge, unique one! I Salute Thee.5.224.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਪਰਮ ਰੂਪਾ ਨਮੋ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮਾ ॥
117.t: namo param roopaa namo kraoor karamaa ||
117.e: O the supreme manifestation of the doer of dreadful actions! I salute thee.
O the bearer of the three modes of Rajas, Sattva and Tamas.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਮਹਿਖ ਦਈਤ ਕੋ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਣੀ ॥
117.t: namo mahikh dhieet ko a(n)t karanee ||
117.e: O the manifestation of supreme steel armour, O the destroyer of Mahishasura.
Destroyer of all, the killer of all! I salute Thee.6.225.
O the killer of Biralachh, the destroyer of Karurachh.
O the one showing mercy on Brahma in her delight, O Yog Maya! I salute Thee.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਜੋਗ ਜ੍ਵਾਲੰ ਧਰੀ ਸਰਬ ਮਾਨੀ ॥੭॥੨੨੬॥
117.t: namo jog javaiaala(n) dharee sarab maanee ||7||226||
117.e: O Bhairavi, Bhavani, Jalandhari and the Destiny through all! I salute Thee.7.226.
Thou art seated everywhere, up and below.
Thou art Lakshmi, Kamakhya and Kumar Kanya.
Thou art Bhavani and manifestation of Bhairavi and Bhima,
Thou art seated at Hinglaj and Pinglaj, Thou art unique! I salute Thee.8.227.
Thou art the performer of dreadful acts, while infuriated in the battlefield.
Thou art most wise, master of powers and doer of pure deeds.
Thou art most beautiful like and apsara (heavenly damsel), Padmini and the goddess Parbati.
Thou art the source of power of Shiva, the power of Indra and the power of Brahma! I salute Thee.9.228.
Enchantress of the ghosts and goblins!
Thou art the greatest apsara, Parbati and the killer of tyrants.
Performer of gentle acts like children at the places like Hinglaj and Pinglaj.
Thou art the power of Kartikeya and Shiva etc.! I salute thee.10.229.
O the power of Yama, O the power of Bhrigu and the the wielder of weapons in Thy hands, I salute Thee.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਰਤਾ ਨਮੋ ਤੇਜ ਮਾਣੰ ॥
117.t: namo asatr dharataa namo tej maana(n) ||
117.e: Thou art the wearer of arms, most Glorious
Unconquerable for ever and conqueror of all, bearer of elegant shield
And performer of justice at all times, the Merciful Kalika! I salute thee. 11.230.
O the wielder of bow, sword, shield and mace,
The user of the disc, and of the honoured portrait, I salute Thee.
Thou art the mother of the universe and wielder of trident and dagger.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਗਿਆਨ ਬਿਗਿਆਨ ਕੀ ਗਿਆਨ ਗਿਆਤਾ ॥੧੨॥੨੩੧॥
117.t: namo giaan bigiaan kee giaan giaataa ||12||231||
117.e: Thou art the knower of all the knowledge of all sciences! I salute Thee.12.231.
Thou art the preserver and destroyer of all, science! Thou art the rider of the dead.
Thou art the destroyer of tyrants in the manifestation of Kali, I salute Thee.
O Yoga-fire! the power of Kartikeya
O Ambika! o Bhavani! I salute Thee.13.232.

117.g: ਨਮੋ ਦੋਖ ਦਾਹੀ ਨਮੋ ਦੁਖ੍ਯ ਹਰਤਾ ॥
117.t: namo dhokh dhaahee namo dhukhay harataa ||
117.e: O the effacer and destroyer of sorrows!
O the wager of war with weapons and arms!

118.e: O most healthy! O Supreme fire!
O the supreme manifestation of young and old women! I salute Thee.14.233.
O the one with dreadful teeth, the rider of the lion, I salute Thee.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਖਗ ਦਗੰ ਝਮਾ ਝਮ ਬਾੜੰ ॥
118.t: namo khag dhaga(n) jhamaa jham baaRa(n) ||
118.e: Thou art the glistening sword, annulling the daggers.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਰੂੜਿ ਗੂੜੰ ਨਮੋ ਸਰਬ ਬਿਆਪੀ ॥
118.t: namo rooR gooRa(n) namo sarab biaapee ||
118.e: Thou art most prodfound, omnipresent,
Eternal and destroyer of tyrants! I salute Thee.15.234.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਰਿਧਿ ਰੂਪੰ ਨਮੋ ਸਿਧ ਕਰਣੀ ॥
118.t: namo ridh roopa(n) namo sidh karanee ||
118.e: O the bestower of powers!
Preserver of all and destroyer of all
The one of the pure forms like silver and dreadful like the dark night

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਜੋਗ ਜ੍ਵਾਲੰ ਧਰੀ ਸਰਬ ਦਾਤ੍ਰੀ ॥੧੬॥੨੩੫॥
118.t: namo jog javaiaala(n) dharee sarab dhaatree ||16||235||
118.e: Thou art the Yoga fire and the sickle for the tyrants! I salute Thee.16.235.
O the power of righteousness of the Supreme Lord!
Thou art ever new, the destroyer of tyrants
The deceiver of all, the yoga-fire of Shiva
The steel-armour for the saints and the dreadful Kali for the saints! I salute Thee.17.236.
Thou art the breath-moving process and the early morning worship.

118.g: ਜਿਨੈ ਮੋਹ ਕੈ ਚਉਦਹੂੰ ਲੋਗ ਬੰਧਿਆ ॥
118.t: jinai moh kai chaudhahoo(n) log ba(n)dhiaa ||
118.e: Who has bound all the fourteen realms in the web of maya.
Thou art Anjani (mother of Hanuman), the crusher of the pride of all,
And the wielder and user of all the weapons! I salute Thee.18.237.
O Anjani! the masher of the pride of tyrants,
The sustainer and bestowed of pleasure to all the saints, I salute thee.
O the manifestation of trident, wielder of sword in Thy hand
The deliverer of all, the cause of causes and the manifestation of the sword! I salute Thee.19.238.
O Kali, with the begging bowl, and the besttower of bliss! I salute Thee.
O one of the most beautiful forms like the sun-rays and moon-beams.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਛੈਲ ਰੂਪਾ ਨਮੋ ਦੁਸਟ ਦਰਣੀ ॥
118.t: namo chhail roopaa namo dhusaT dharanee ||
118.e: The beauteous and the destroyer of the tyrants
The sustainer of the world and the cause of all causes! I salute Thee.20.239.
O the one who showers her weapons in her pleasure,
Thou art the deliverer of all, I salute Thee.
O goddess Durga, Thou art most wise, a Yogini
A goddess and a demoness, I salute Thee.21.240

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਘੋਰਿ ਰੂਪਾ ਨਮੋ ਚਾਰੁ ਨੈਣਾ ॥
118.t: namo ghor roopaa namo chaar nainaa ||
118.e: O the one of the dreadful forms and winsome eyes!
Thou art the wielder of trident and dagger and speaker of harsh words, I salute Thee.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਬ੍ਰਿਧ ਬੁਧੰ ਕਰੀ ਜੋਗ ਜੁਆਲਾ ॥
118.t: namo biradh budha(n) karee jog juaalaa ||
118.e: O the blazer of Yoga-fire, the manifestation of supreme wisdom,

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਚੰਡ ਮੁੰਡੀ ਮ੍ਰਿੜਾ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਾਲਾ ॥੨੨॥੨੪੧॥
118.t: namo cha(n)dd mu(n)ddee miraRaa kraoor kaalaa ||22||241||
118.e: The destroyer of Chand and Munda and performer of the heinous action of crushing their dead bodies! I salute Thee.22.241.
Thou art the bestower of bliss by destroying the great sinners.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਦਾੜ ਗਾੜਾ ਧਰੀ ਦੁਖ੍ਯ ਹਰਣੀ ॥
118.t: namo dhaaR gaaRaa dharee dhukhay haranee ||
118.e: Thou art the remover of the anguish of saints by destroying the tyrants with Thy dreadful teeth.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰ ਬੇਤਾ ਨਮੋ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਗਾਮੀ ॥
118.t: namo saasatr betaa namo sasatr gaamee ||
118.e: Thou art the knower of Shastras, knower of the use of weapons

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਜਛ ਬਿਦਿਆ ਧਰੀ ਪੂਰਣ ਕਾਮੀ ॥੨੩॥੨੪੨॥
118.t: namo jachh bidhiaa dharee pooran kaamee ||23||242||
118.e: Perfect in knowledge of Yakshas, and the fulfiller of the desires! I salute Thee.23.242.
O the giver of suffering to the enemies, all the people worship Thee.
Thou art the creator of all interests and also their destroyer.
Thou art the power of Hanuman
Thou art Kalika and manifestation of the sword and wielder of the power in Thy own hands! I salute thee.24.243.
O the masterly power of Hanuman! Thou art the goddess of Nagarkot (Kangra)
Thou art the manifestation of Kama (love). Thou art Kamakhya, the goddess.
And the bestower of bliss on al like kalratri (Kali)
O the bestower of the great miraculous powers and wealth and wielder of the sword! I salute Thee.25.244.

118.g: ਨਮੋ ਚਤੁਰ ਬਾਹੀ ਨਮੋ ਅਸਟ ਬਾਹਾ ॥
118.t: namo chatur baahee namo asaT baahaa ||
118.e: O Goddess! thou art four-armed, eight-armed,
And sustainer of the whole world.

119.e: O Ambika! Thou art the killer of the demon Jambh, the power of Kartikeya
And the crusher of the dead, O Bhavani! I salute Thee.26.245.
O the destroyer of the enemies of the gods,
White-black and red-coloured.
O fire! the enchancer of bliss by conquering illusion.
Thou art the maya of Unmanifested Brahman and the Shakti of Shiva! I salute Thee.27.246.
Thou art the bestower of cheerfulness to all, the conqueror of all and the manifestation of Kal (death).
O Kapali! (the goddess carrying begging bowl), Shiva-Shakti! (the power of Shiva) and Bhadrakali!
Thou obtainest satisfaction by piercing Durga.
Thou art pure fire-manifestation and also cold-incarnate, I salute Thee.28.247.
O the masticator of the demons, the manifestation of the banners of all religions
The source of the power of Hinglaj and Pinglaj, I salute Thee.

119.g: ਨਮੋ ਦੀਰਘ ਦਾੜਾ ਨਮੋ ਸਿਆਮ ਬਰਣੀ ॥
119.t: namo dheeragh dhaaRaa namo siaam baranee ||
119.e: O the one of the dreadful teeth, the black complexioned,
Anjani, the masher of demons! Salute Thee. 29.248.
O the adopter of half-moon and wearer of the moon as an ornament

119.g: ਨਮੋ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਊਰਧਾ ਨਮੋ ਦਾੜ ਗੂੜੰ ॥
119.t: namo i(n)dhr uooradhaa namo dhaaR gooRa(n) ||
119.e: Thou hast the power of clouds and hast dreadful jaws.
Thy forehead is like the moon, O Bhavani!
Thou art also Bhairavi and Bhutani, Thou art the wielder of the sword, I salute Thee.30.249.
O Kamakhya and Durga! Thou art the cause and deed of Kaliyuga (the iron age).
Like Apsara (heavenly damsels) and the Padmini women, Thou art the fulfiller of all desires.
Thou art the conqueror Yogini of all and performer of Yajnas (sacrifices).
Thou art the nature of all substances, Thou art the creator of the world and the destroyer of the enemies.31.250.
Thou art pure, holy, ancient, great
Perfect, maya and unconquerable.
Thou art formless, unique, nameless and abodeless.
Thou art fearless, unconquerable and treasure of the great Dharma.32.251.
Thou art indestructible, indistinguishable, deedless and Dhrma-incarnate.

119.g: ਨਮੋ ਬਾਣ ਪਾਣੀ ਧਰੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ॥
119.t: namo baan paanee dhare charam barama(n) ||
119.e: O the holder of the arrow in Thy hand and wearer of the armour, I salute Thee.
Thou art unconquerable, indistinguishable, formless, eternal
Shapeless and the cause of nirvana (salvation) and all the works.33.252.
Thou art Parbati, fulfiller of the wishes, the power of Krishna
Most powerful, the power of Vamana and art like the fire of the Yajna (sacrifice).
O the chewer of the enemies and masher of their pride
Sustainer and destroyer in Thy pleasure, I salute Thee.34.253.
O the rider of the steed-like lion
O Bhavani of beautiful limbs! Thou art the destroyer of all engaged in the war.

119.g: ਨਮੋ ਭੀਮਿ ਸਰੂਪਾ ਨਮੋ ਲੋਕ ਮਾਤਾ ॥
119.t: namo bheem saroopaa namo lok maataa ||
119.e: O the mother of the universe having large body!
Thou art the power of Yama, the giver of the fruit of actions performed in the world, Thou art also the power of Brahma! I salute Thee.35.254.
O the most pure power of God!
Thou art the maya and Gayatri, sustaining all.
Thou art Chamunda, the wearer of the necklace of head, Thou art also the fire of the matted locks of Shiva
Thou art the donor of boons and destroyer of tyrants, but Thou Thyself ever remain indivisible.36.255.

119.g: ਸਬੈ ਸੰਤ ਉਬਾਰੀ ਬਰੰ ਬ੍ਰਯੂਹ ਦਾਤਾ ॥
119.t: sabai sa(n)t ubaaree bara(n) brayooh dhaataa ||
119.e: O the Saviour of all the saints and the donor of boons to all
The one who ferries across all over the terrible sea of life, the primary cause of all causes, O Bhavani! The mother of the universe.
I salute Thee again and again, O the manifestation of the sword!

119.g: ਸਦਾ ਰਾਖ ਲੈ ਮੁਹਿ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਨੀ ॥੩੭॥੨੫੬॥
119.t: sadhaa raakh lai muh kirapaa kai kirapaanee ||37||256||
119.e: Protect me ever with Thy Grace.37.256.

119.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕੇ ਚੰਡੀ ਚਰਿਤ੍ਰੇ ਦੇਵੀ ਜੂ ਕੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਨਾਮ ਸਪਤਮੋ ਧਿਆਯ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੭॥
119.t: eit sree bachitr naaTake cha(n)ddee charitre dhevee joo kee usatat baranana(n) naam sapatamo dhiaay sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||7||
119.e: Here ends the Seventh Chapter entitled ‘The Eulogy of the Goddess’ of Chandi of Chandi Charitra in BACHITTAR NATAK.7.
Description of the Praise of Chandi Charitra:
