144.t: gaddrayo jag tha(n)bha(n) kariyo hom ku(n)dda(n) ||
144.e: The columns of the sacrificial place were fixed and the sacrificial altar was constructed.

144.g: ਭਲੀ ਭਾਤ ਪੋਖੇ ਬਲੀ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਝੁੰਡੰ ॥੩੧॥੧੯੯॥
144.t: bhalee bhaat pokhe balee bipr jhu(n)dda(n) ||31||199||
144.e: He satisfied nicely the assembly of the Brahmins giving wealth in charity.31.199.

144.g: ਦਏ ਕੋਟ ਦਾਨੰ ਪਕੇ ਪਰਮ ਪਾਕੰ ॥
144.t: dhe koT dhaana(n) pake param paaka(n) ||
144.e: Millins of gifts were given in charity and pure foods were served.

144.g: ਕਲੂ ਮਧਿ ਕੀਨੋ ਬਡੋ ਧਰਮ ਸਾਕੰ ॥
144.t: kaloo madh keeno baddo dharam saaka(n) ||
144.e: The king performed a great event of Dharma in the Kaliyuga.

144.g: ਲਗੀ ਦੇਖਨੇ ਆਪ ਜਿਉ ਰਾਜ ਬਾਲਾ ॥
144.t: lagee dhekhane aap jiau raaj baalaa ||
144.e: As the queen began to scan all this,

144.g: ਮਹਾ ਰੂਪਵੰਤੀ ਮਹਾ ਜੁਆਲ ਆਲਾ ॥੩੨॥੨੦੦॥
144.t: mahaa roopava(n)tee mahaa juaal aalaa ||32||200||
144.e: She the most beautiful and abode of Supreme glory.32.200.

144.g: ਉਡ੍ਯੋ ਪਉਨ ਕੇ ਬੇਗ ਸਿਯੋ ਅਗ੍ਰ ਪਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
144.t: auddayo paun ke beg siyo agr patra(n) ||
144.e: The frontal garment of the queen flew away by the gust of wind.

144.g: ਹਸੇ ਦੇਖ ਨਗਨੰ ਤ੍ਰੀਯੰ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਛਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
144.t: hase dhekh nagana(n) treeya(n) bipr chhatra(n) ||
144.e: The Brahmins and Kshatriyas (in the assembly) seeing the nakedness of the queen laughed.

144.g: ਭਇਓ ਕੋਪ ਰਾਜਾ ਗਹੇ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਸਰਬੰ ॥
144.t: bhio kop raajaa gahe bipr saraba(n) ||
144.e: The king in great fury caught hold of all the Brahmins.

144.g: ਦਹੇ ਖੀਰ ਖੰਡੰ ਬਡੇ ਪਰਮ ਗਰਬੰ ॥੩੩॥੨੦੧॥
144.t: dhahe kheer kha(n)dda(n) badde param garaba(n) ||33||201||
144.e: All the highly proud great Pundits were burnt with hot mixture of milk and sugar.33.201.

144.g: ਪ੍ਰਿਥਮ ਬਾਧਿ ਕੈ ਸਰਬ ਮੂੰਡੇ ਮੁੰਡਾਏ ॥
144.t: piratham baadh kai sarab moo(n)dde mu(n)ddaae ||
144.e: Firstly all the Brahmins were bound down and their heads were shaved.

144.g: ਪੁਨਰ ਏਡੂਆ ਸੀਸ ਤਾ ਕੇ ਟਿਕਾਏ ॥
144.t: punar eddooaa sees taa ke Tikaae ||
144.e: Then the pads were placed on the top of their heads.

144.g: ਪੁਨਰ ਤਪਤ ਕੈ ਖੀਰ ਕੇ ਮਧਿ ਡਾਰਿਓ ॥
144.t: punar tapat kai kheer ke madh ddaario ||
144.e: Then the boiling milk was poured (within the pads).

144.g: ਇਮੰ ਸਰਬ ਬਿਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਕਉ ਜਾਰਿ ਮਾਰਿਓ ॥੩੪॥੨੦੨॥
144.t: eima(n) sarab bipraan kau jaar maario ||34||202||
144.e: And thus all the Brahmins were burnt and killed.34.202.

145.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਬਾਧਿ ਕੈ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਬਾਚੇ ਦਿਵਾਰੰ ॥
145.t: kite baadh kai bipr baache dhivaara(n) ||
145.e: Many Brahmins were entombed in the walls

145.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਬਾਧ ਫਾਸੀ ਦੀਏ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਭਾਰੰ ॥
145.t: kite baadh faasee dhe'ee bipr bhaara(n) ||
145.e: Many eminent Brahmins were hanged

145.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਬਾਰਿ ਬੋਰੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਅਗਨਿ ਜਾਰੇ ॥
145.t: kite baar bore kite agan jaare ||
145.e: Many were drowned in water and many were bound in fire

145.g: ਕਿਤੇ ਅਧਿ ਚੀਰੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਬਾਧ ਫਾਰੇ ॥੩੫॥੨੦੩॥
145.t: kite adh cheere kite baadh faare ||35||203||
145.e: Many were sawed into halves and many were bound and their bellies wre torn.35.203.

145.g: ਲਗਿਯੋ ਦੋਖ ਭੂਪੰ ਬਢਿਯੋ ਕੁਸਟ ਦੇਹੀ ॥
145.t: lagiyo dhokh bhoopa(n) baddiyo kusaT dhehee ||
145.e: The king then suffered from the blemish of Brahmin-killing and his body was inflicted by leprosy.

145.g: ਸਭੇ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਬੋਲੇ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਰਾਜ ਨੇਹੀ ॥
145.t: sabhe bipr bole kariyo raaj nehee ||
145.e: He called all other Brahmins and treated them with love.

145.g: ਕਹੋ ਕਉਨ ਸੋ ਬੈਠਿ ਕੀਜੈ ਬਿਚਾਰੰ ॥
145.t: kaho kaun so baiTh keejai bichaara(n) ||
145.e: He asked them to sit and contemplate as to how,

145.g: ਦਹੈ ਦੇਹ ਦੋਖੰ ਮਿਟੈ ਪਾਪ ਭਾਰੰ ॥੩੬॥੨੦੪॥
145.t: dhahai dheh dhokha(n) miTai paap bhaara(n) ||36||204||
145.e: The suffering of the body and the great sin can be removed.36.204.

145.g: ਬੋਲੇ ਰਾਜ ਦੁਆਰੰ ਸਬੈ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਆਏ ॥
145.t: bole raaj dhuaara(n) sabai bipr aae ||
145.e: All the invited Brahmins came to the royal court.

145.g: ਬਡੇ ਬਿਆਸ ਤੇ ਆਦਿ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਬੁਲਾਏ ॥
145.t: badde biaas te aadh lai ke bulaae ||
145.e: The eminent like Vyas and other were called.

145.g: ਦੇਖੈ ਲਾਗ ਸਾਸਤ੍ਰੰ ਬੋਲੇ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਸਰਬੰ ॥
145.t: dhekhai laag saasatra(n) bole bipr saraba(n) ||
145.e: After scanning the Shastras, all the Brahmins said,

145.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਪ੍ਰਮੇਧੰ ਬਢਿਓ ਭੂਪ ਗਰਬੰ ॥੩੭॥੨੦੫॥
145.t: kariyo bipramedha(n) baddio bhoop garaba(n) ||37||205||
145.e: “The ego of the king hath increased and because of this conceit, he mashed the Brahmins.37.205.

145.g: ਸੁਨਹੁ ਰਾਜ ਸਰਦੂਲ ਬਿਦਿਆ ਨਿਧਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: sunahu raaj saradhool bidhiaa nidhaana(n) ||
145.e: “Listen, O Supreme monarch, the treasure of learning

145.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਮੇਧੰ ਸੁ ਜਗੰ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: kariyo bipr medha(n) su jaga(n) pramaana(n) ||
145.e: “Thou didst mash the Brahmins during the sacrifice

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਅਕਸਮੰਤ੍ਰੰ ਕਹਿਓ ਨਾਹਿ ਕਉਨੈ ॥
145.t: bhio akasama(n)tra(n) kahio naeh kaunai ||
145.e: “All this happened suddenly, no one directed thee for this

145.g: ਕਰੀ ਜਉਨ ਹੋਤੀ ਭਈ ਬਾਤ ਤਉਨੈ ॥੩੮॥੨੦੬॥
145.t: karee jaun hotee bhiee baat taunai ||38||206||
145.e: “All this hath been got done by the Providence, such happening had been recorded earlier.”38.206.

145.g: ਸੁਨਹੁ ਬਿਆਸ ਤੇ ਪਰਬ ਅਸਟੰ ਦਸਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: sunahu biaas te parab asaTa(n) dhasaana(n) ||
145.e: “O King! Listen from Vyas eighteen Parvas (parts) of Mahabharata

145.g: ਦਹੈ ਦੇਹ ਤੇ ਕੁਸਟ ਸਰਬੰ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: dhahai dheh te kusaT saraba(n) nirapaana(n) ||
145.e: “Then all the ailment of leprosy will be removed from thy body.”

145.g: ਬੋਲੈ ਬਿਪ੍ਰ ਬਿਆਸੰ ਸੁਨੈ ਲਾਗ ਪਰਬੰ ॥
145.t: bolai bipr biaasa(n) sunai laag paraba(n) ||
145.e: The eminent Brahmin Vyas was then called and the king began to listen to the Parvas (of Mahabharata).

145.g: ਪਰਿਯੋ ਭੂਪ ਪਾਇਨ ਤਜੇ ਸਰਬ ਗਰਬੰ ॥੩੯॥੨੦੭॥
145.t: pariyo bhoop pain taje sarab garaba(n) ||39||207||
145.e: The king fell at the feet of Vyas forsaking all pride.39.207.

145.g: ਸੁਨਹੁ ਰਾਜ ਸਰਦੂਲ ਬਿਦਿਆ ਨਿਧਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: sunahu raaj saradhool bidhiaa nidhaana(n) ||
145.e: (Vyas said J Listen, O Supreme monarch! the treasure of learning

145.g: ਹੂਓ ਭਰਥ ਕੇ ਬੰਸ ਮੈ ਰਘੁਰਾਨੰ ॥
145.t: hooo bharath ke ba(n)s mai raghuraana(n) ||
145.e: In the linege of Bharat, there was a king named Raghu

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਤਉਨ ਕੇ ਬੰਸ ਮੈ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
145.t: bhio taun ke ba(n)s mai raam raajaa ||
145.e: In his line, there was the king Rama

145.g: ਦੀਜੈ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਦਾਨੰ ਨਿਧਾਨੰ ਬਿਰਾਜਾ ॥੪੦॥੨੦੮॥
145.t: dheejai chhatr dhaana(n) nidhaana(n) biraajaa ||40||208||
145.e: Who gave the gift of life to the kashatriyas from the wrath of Parasurama and also the treasures and comfortable living.40.208.

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਤਉਨ ਕੀ ਜਦ ਮੈ ਜਦੁ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
145.t: bhio taun kee jadh mai jadh raaja(n) ||
145.e: In his clan, there was a king named Yadu

145.g: ਦਸੰ ਚਾਰ ਚੌਦਹ ਸੁ ਬਿਦਿਆ ਸਮਾਜੰ ॥
145.t: dhasa(n) chaar chauadheh su bidhiaa samaaja(n) ||
145.e: Who was erudite in all fourteen learnings

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਤਉਨ ਕੇ ਬੰਸ ਮੈ ਸੰਤਨੇਅੰ ॥
145.t: bhio taun ke ba(n)s mai sa(n)tanea(n) ||
145.e: In his family, there was a king named Santanu

145.g: ਭਏ ਤਾਹਿ ਕੇ ਕਉਰਓ ਪਾਡਵੇਅੰ ॥੪੧॥੨੦੯॥
145.t: bhe taeh ke kauro paaddavea(n) ||41||209||
145.e: In his line, there were then Kaurvas and Pandavas.41.209.

145.g: ਭਏ ਤਉਨ ਕੇ ਬੰਸ ਮੈ ਧ੍ਰਿਤਰਾਸਟਰੰ ॥
145.t: bhe taun ke ba(n)s mai dhirataraasaTara(n) ||
145.e: In his family, there was Dhritrashtra,

145.g: ਮਹਾ ਜੁਧ ਜੋਧਾ ਪ੍ਰਬੋਧਾ ਮਹਾ ਸੁਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
145.t: mahaa judh jodhaa prabodhaa mahaa sutra(n) ||
145.e: Who was a great hero in wars and a teacher of great enemies.

145.g: ਭਏ ਤਉਨ ਕੇ ਕਉਰਵੰ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮੰ ॥
145.t: bhe taun ke kaurava(n) kraoor karama(n) ||
145.e: In his house there were Kauravas of vicious Karmas,

145.g: ਕੀਓ ਛਤ੍ਰਣੰ ਜੈਨ ਕੁਲ ਛੈਣ ਕਰਮੰ ॥੪੨॥੨੧੦॥
145.t: keeo chhatrana(n) jain kul chhain karama(n) ||42||210||
145.e: Who worked as a chisel (destroyer) for the clan of Kshatriyas.42.210.

145.g: ਕੀਓ ਭੀਖਮੇ ਅਗ੍ਰ ਸੈਨਾ ਸਮਾਜੰ ॥
145.t: keeo bheekhame agr sainaa samaaja(n) ||
145.e: They made Bhishama the General of their forces

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਕ੍ਰੁਧ ਜੁਧੰ ਸਮੁਹ ਪੰਡੁ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
145.t: bhio krudh judha(n) samuh pa(n)dd raaja(n) ||
145.e: In great fury they waged their war against the sons of Pandu.

145.g: ਤਹਾ ਗਰਜਿਯੋ ਅਰਜਨੰ ਪਰਮ ਬੀਰੰ ॥
145.t: tahaa garajiyo arajana(n) param beera(n) ||
145.e: In that war, the Supreme hereo Arjuna roared.

145.g: ਧਨੁਰ ਬੇਦ ਗਿਆਤਾ ਤਜੇ ਪਰਮ ਤੀਰੰ ॥੪੩॥੨੧੧॥
145.t: dhanur bedh giaataa taje param teera(n) ||43||211||
145.e: He was an adept in archery and shot his shafts superbly.43.211.

145.g: ਤਜੀ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਨਾ ਵਰੀ ਬੀਰ ਖੇਤੰ ॥
145.t: tajee beer baanaa varee beer kheta(n) ||
145.e: The great hero Arjuna shot his chain of arrows in the field (with such skill),

145.g: ਹਣਿਓ ਭੀਖਮੰ ਸਭੈ ਸੈਨਾ ਸਮੇਤੰ ॥
145.t: hanio bheekhama(n) sabhai sainaa sameta(n) ||
145.e: That he killed Bhishama and destroyed al his forces.

145.g: ਦਈ ਬਾਣ ਸਿਜਾ ਗਰੇ ਭੀਖਮੈਣੰ ॥
145.t: dhiee baan sijaa gare bheekhamaina(n) ||
145.e: He gave Bhishama the bed of arrows, on which he lay down.

145.g: ਜਯੰ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਇਓ ਸੁਖੰ ਪਾਡਵੇਣੰ ॥੪੪॥੨੧੨॥
145.t: jaya(n) patr paio sukha(n) paaddavena(n) ||44||212||
145.e: The great Pandava (Arjuna) attained the victory comfortably.44.212.

145.g: ਭਏ ਦ੍ਰੋਣ ਸੈਨਾਪਤੀ ਸੈਨਪਾਲੰ ॥
145.t: bhe dhron sainaapatee sainapaala(n) ||
145.e: The second general of Kauravas and master of their forces was Daronacharya.

145.g: ਭਇਓ ਘੋਰ ਜੁਧੰ ਤਹਾ ਤਉਨ ਕਾਲੰ ॥
145.t: bhio ghor judha(n) tahaa taun kaala(n) ||
145.e: There at that time a horrible war was waged.

145.g: ਹਣਿਓ ਧ੍ਰਿਸਟ ਦੋਨੰ ਤਜੇ ਦ੍ਰੋਣ ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ ॥
145.t: hanio dhirasaT dhona(n) taje dhron praana(n) ||
145.e: Dhrishtadyumna killed Dronacharya, who breathed his last.

145.g: ਕਰਿਓ ਜੁਧ ਤੇ ਦੇਵਲੋਕੰ ਪਿਆਣੰ ॥੪੫॥੨੧੩॥
145.t: kario judh te dhevaloka(n) piaana(n) ||45||213||
145.e: Dying in the battlefield, he went to heaven.45.213.

145.g: ਭਏ ਕਰਣ ਸੈਨਾਪਤੀ ਛਤ੍ਰਪਾਲੰ ॥
145.t: bhe karan sainaapatee chhatrapaala(n) ||
145.e: Karan became the third General of the Kaurva army,

145.g: ਮਚ੍ਯੋ ਜੁਧ ਕ੍ਰੁਧੰ ਮਹਾ ਬਿਕਰਾਲੰ ॥
145.t: machayo judh krudha(n) mahaa bikaraala(n) ||
145.e: Who in great fury waged a terrible war.

145.g: ਹਣਿਓ ਤਾਹਿ ਪੰਥੰ ਸਦੰ ਸੀਸੁ ਕਪਿਓ ॥
145.t: hanio taeh pa(n)tha(n) sadha(n) sees kapio ||
145.e: He was killed by Partha (Arjuna) and immediately cut off his head.

145.g: ਗਿਰਿਓ ਤਉਣ ਯੁਧਿਸਟਰੰ ਰਾਜੁ ਥਪਿਓ ॥੪੬॥੨੧੪॥
145.t: girio taun yudhisaTara(n) raaj thapio ||46||214||
145.e: After his fall (death), the rule of Yudhishtra was firmly established.46.214.

146.e: Then the brave warrior Salaya became the general of Kauravas.

146.g: ਭਲੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੁਟਿਓ ਬਲੀ ਪੰਚ ਦਲ੍ਰਯੰ ॥
146.t: bhalee bhaat kuTio balee pa(n)ch dhalraya(n) ||
146.e: He beat the brave Pandava foces fiercely,
And wounded the elephant of Yudhistra with his dagger.

146.g: ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਜੁਧ ਭੂਪੰ ਬਲੀ ਭੂਪ ਬੇਧੰ ॥੪੭॥੨੧੫॥
146.t: giriyo judh bhoopa(n) balee bhoop bedha(n) ||47||215||
146.e: Because of this Yudhistra fell down, but he killed the brave Salaya.47.215.
CHAUPAI
The day on which the king Salya died in fighting, the Kauravas felt their impending defeat.
When Salya died, Ashvathama become the general, he beat violently millions of forces for one watch.1.216.
He killed the expert charioteer Dharishtadyumna, and mashed the Pandava forces nicely.
He also killed thefive sons of Pandavas, he fought very great waars in Dvapar age.2.217.

146.g: ਭੀਮ ਸੰਗਿ ਹੁਇ ਕੈ ਅਤਿ ਕ੍ਰੁਧਾ ॥
146.t: bheem sa(n)g hui kai at krudhaa ||
146.e: Then Duryodhana, the king of Kauravas waged the war, against Bhim in great fury.
He was never defeated while fighting, but the mighty death came and killed him.3.218.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

146.g: ਤਹਾ ਭੀਮ ਕੁਰਰਾਜ ਸਿਉ ਜੁਧ ਮਚਿਓ ॥
146.t: tahaa bheem kuraraaj siau judh machio ||
146.e: There the fierce war of Duryodhana began with Bhim,

146.g: ਛੁਟੀ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਤਾਰੀ ਮਹਾ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਨਚਿਓ ॥
146.t: chhuTee braham taaree mahaa rudhr nachio ||
146.e: Because of which the meditation of Shiva was shattered and that great gods began to dance.
Because of the blows of warriors terrible sound arose

146.g: ਭਏ ਰੁੰਡ ਮੁੰਡੰ ਤਣੰ ਤਛ ਤੀਰੰ ॥੧॥੨੧੯॥
146.t: bhe ru(n)dd mu(n)dda(n) tana(n) tachh teera(n) ||1||219||
146.e: The bodies were pierced by arrows and the heads were separated from pierced by arrows and the heads were separated from the trunks.1.219.
Fighting in various ways, many warriors fell in the field

146.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਅਧ ਅਧੰ ਛੁਧੰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੰ ॥
146.t: gire adh adha(n) chhudha(n) sasatr dhaara(n) ||
146.e: Many had fallen in halves who had been hungry of the sharp edges of weapons.
The intoxicated elephants of Kauravas had been chopped in the field.
Seeing the brave warriors wields weapons in the field, the vultures were feeling pleased.2.220.
The warriors were fighting in the battlefield in enclosures.

146.g: ਹਸੈ ਗਰਜ ਠੋਕੈ ਭੁਜਾ ਹਰ ਦੁ ਗਾਜੈ ॥
146.t: hasai garaj Thokai bhujaa har dh gaajai ||
146.e: They laughed, roared and patted their arms, they challenged from both sides.
They were standing and showing feats of bravery in enclosures.
They swayed their arms and were producing terrible sounds with the blows of their maces.3.221.

146.g: ਸੁਭੇ ਸਵਰਨ ਕੇ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਬਾਧੇ ਗਜਾ ਮੈ ॥
146.t: subhe savaran ke patr baadhe gajaa mai ||
146.e: The sheets of gold covering the maces looked splendid.

146.g: ਭਈ ਅਗਨਿ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਖੀ ਕੈ ਧੁਜਾ ਮੈ ॥
146.t: bhiee agan sobhaa lakhee kai dhujaa mai ||
146.e: Their glory exhibited the blaze of fire at their tops.
The warriors moved in the field and rotated their discs.

146.g: ਅਪੋ ਆਪ ਸੈ ਨੇਕਿ ਘਾਇੰ ਸਰਾਹੈ ॥੪॥੨੨੨॥
146.t: apo aap sai nek ghai(n) saraahai ||4||222||
146.e: They appreciated those on their sides who inflicted deep wounds.4.222.

146.g: ਤਹਾ ਭੀਮ ਭਾਰੀ ਭੁਜਾ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬਾਹੈ ॥
146.t: tahaa bheem bhaaree bhujaa sasatr baahai ||
146.e: There the great warrior Bhim used his weapons with his arms.

146.g: ਭਲੀ ਭਾਤਿ ਕੈ ਕੈ ਭਲੇ ਸੈਨ ਗਾਹੈ ॥
146.t: bhalee bhaat kai kai bhale sain gaahai ||
146.e: He was trampling the armies nicely.
On the other side Yudhishtar was bound by Kshatriya discipline,
And was performing wonderful and holy Karmas.5.223.
All of them looked elegant with ornaments like armlets.
Their necklaces of gems glistened and their turbans looked graceful on the heads of both the warriors of the same age.

146.g: ਦੋਊ ਮੀਰ ਧੀਰੰ ਦੋਊ ਪਰਮ ਓਜੰ ॥
146.t: dhouoo meer dheera(n) dhouoo param oja(n) ||
146.e: Both the Chiefs were men of great strength and composure.
Both were either king Mandhata or king Bhoj.6.224.

146.g: ਦੋਊ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਨਾ ਬਧੈ ਅਧ ਅਧੰ ॥
146.t: dhouoo beer baanaa badhai adh adha(n) ||
146.e: Both the warriors had tightened their tearing shafts.

146.g: ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੀ ਮਹਾ ਜੁਧ ਕ੍ਰੁਧੰ ॥
146.t: dhouoo sasatr dhaaree mahaa judh krudha(n) ||
146.e: Both the weapon-wielding warriors began to wage war in great fury.

146.g: ਦੋਊ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮੰ ਦੋਊ ਜਾਨ ਬਾਹੰ ॥
146.t: dhouoo kraoor karama(n) dhouoo jaan baaha(n) ||
146.e: Both the heroes of violent actions had long arms like gods.
Both were great kings with extraordinary knowledge of Hindusim.7.225.

146.g: ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੰ ਦੋਊ ਪਰਮ ਦਾਨੰ ॥
146.t: dhouoo sasatr dhaara(n) dhouoo param dhaana(n) ||
146.e: Both were weapon-wielders and supreme donors.
Both were Indians and capable of protecting themselves with their shields.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਵਰਤੀ ਦੋਊ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਧਾਰੀ ॥
147.t: dhouoo sasatr varatee dhouoo chhatr dhaaree ||
147.e: Both were the users of their arms and were kings with canopies.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਪਰਮ ਜੋਧਾ ਮਹਾ ਜੁਧਕਾਰੀ ॥੮॥੨੨੬॥
147.t: dhouoo param jodhaa mahaa judhakaaree ||8||226||
147.e: Both were Supreme warriors and great fighters.8.226.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡੀ ਦੋਊ ਮੰਡ ਮੰਡੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo kha(n)dd kha(n)ddee dhouoo ma(n)dd ma(n)dda(n) ||
147.e: Both were the destroyers of their enemies and also their establishers.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਜੋਧ ਜੈਤਵਾਰੁ ਜੋਧਾ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo jodh jaitavaar jodhaa pracha(n)dda(n) ||
147.e: Both were the terrible conquerors of the great heroes.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਬੀਰ ਬਾਨੀ ਦੋਊ ਬਾਹ ਸਾਹੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo beer baanee dhouoo baeh saaha(n) ||
147.e: Both the warriors were adept in shooting arrows and had mighty arms.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਸੂਰ ਸੈਨੰ ਦੋਊ ਸੂਰ ਮਾਹੰ ॥੯॥੨੨੭॥
147.t: dhouoo soor saina(n) dhouoo soor maaha(n) ||9||227||
147.e: Both the heroes were the sun and moon of their forces.9.227.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਚਕ੍ਰਵਰਤੀ ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬੇਤਾ ॥
147.t: dhouoo chakravaratee dhouoo sasatr betaa ||
147.e: Both were the warriors universal monarchs and had knowledge of warfare.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਜੰਗ ਜੋਧੀ ਦੋਊ ਜੰਗ ਜੇਤਾ ॥
147.t: dhouoo ja(n)g jodhee dhouoo ja(n)g jetaa ||
147.e: Both were the warriors of war and conquerors of war.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਜੋਤੀ ਦੋਊ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਚਾਪੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo chitr jotee dhouoo chitr chaapa(n) ||
147.e: Both were marvelously beautiful carrying beautiful bows.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਵਰਮਾ ਦੋਊ ਦੁਸਟ ਤਾਪੰ ॥੧੦॥੨੨੮॥
147.t: dhouoo chitr varamaa dhouoo dhusaT taapa(n) ||10||228||
147.e: Both were clad in armour and were the destroyers of enemies.10.228.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖੰਡ ਖੰਡੀ ਦੋਊ ਮੰਡ ਮੰਡੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo kha(n)dd kha(n)ddee dhouoo ma(n)dd ma(n)dda(n) ||
147.e: Both were the destroyers of the enemies with their double-edged swords and were also their establishers.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਜੋਤੀ ਸੁ ਜੋਧਾ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo chitr jotee su jodhaa pracha(n)dda(n) ||
147.e: Both were Glory-incarnate and mighty heroes.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਮਤ ਬਾਰੁੰਨ ਬਿਕ੍ਰਮ ਸਮਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo mat baaru(n)n bikram samaana(n) ||
147.e: Both were intoxicate elephants and like king Vikrama.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬੇਤਾ ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਨੰ ॥੧੧॥੨੨੯॥
147.t: dhouoo sasatr betaa dhouoo sasatr paana(n) ||11||229||
147.e: Both were adepts in warfare and had weapons in their hands.11.229.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਪਰਮ ਜੋਧੇ ਦੋਊ ਕ੍ਰੁਧਵਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo param jodhe dhouoo krudhavaana(n) ||
147.e: Both were Supreme warriors full of rage.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਬੇਤਾ ਦੋਊ ਰੂਪ ਖਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo sasatr betaa dhouoo roop khaana(n) ||
147.e: Both were adepts in warfare and were the source of beauty.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਛਤ੍ਰਪਾਲੰ ਦੋਊ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਧਰਮੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo chhatrapaala(n) dhouoo chhatr dharama(n) ||
147.e: Both were Sustainers of Kshatriyas and followed the discipline of Kshatriyas.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਜੁਧ ਜੋਧਾ ਦੋਊ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਕਰਮੰ ॥੧੨॥੨੩੦॥
147.t: dhouoo judh jodhaa dhouoo kraoor karama(n) ||12||230||
147.e: Both were the heroes of war and men of violent actions.12.230.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਮੰਡਲਾਕਾਰ ਜੂਝੇ ਬਿਰਾਜੈ ॥
147.t: dhouoo ma(n)ddalaakaar joojhe biraajai ||
147.e: Both were standing and fighting in enclosures.

147.g: ਹਥੈ ਹਰ ਦੁ ਠੋਕੈ ਭੁਜਾ ਪਾਇ ਗਾਜੈ ॥
147.t: hathai har dh Thokai bhujaa pai gaajai ||
147.e: Both struck their arms with their hands and shouted loudly.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖਤ੍ਰਹਾਣੰ ਦੋਊ ਖਤ੍ਰ ਖੰਡੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo khatrahaana(n) dhouoo khatr kha(n)dda(n) ||
147.e: Both had Kshatriya discipline but both were the destroyers of Kshatriyas.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖਗ ਪਾਣੰ ਦੋਊ ਛੇਤ੍ਰ ਮੰਡੰ ॥੧੩॥੨੩੧॥
147.t: dhouoo khag paana(n) dhouoo chhetr ma(n)dda(n) ||13||231||
147.e: Both had swords in their hands and both were the adornments of th battlefield.13.231.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਚਿਤ੍ਰਜੋਤੀ ਦੋਊ ਚਾਰ ਬਿਚਾਰੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo chitrajotee dhouoo chaar bichaara(n) ||
147.e: Both were Beauty-incarnate and had lofty thoughts.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਮੰਡਲਾਕਾਰ ਖੰਡਾ ਅਬਾਰੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo ma(n)ddalaakaar kha(n)ddaa abaara(n) ||
147.e: Both were operating their double-adged swords in their enclosures.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖਗ ਖੂਨੀ ਦੋਊ ਖਤ੍ਰਹਾਣੰ ॥
147.t: dhouoo khag khoonee dhouoo khatrahaana(n) ||
147.e: Both had their swords smeared with blood and both worked against Kshatriya discipline.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਖਤ੍ਰਖੇਤਾ ਦੋਊ ਛਤ੍ਰਪਾਣੰ ॥੧੪॥੨੩੨॥
147.t: dhouoo khatrakhetaa dhouoo chhatrapaana(n) ||14||232||
147.e: Both were capable of risking their life in the battlefield.14.232.

147.g: ਦੋਊ ਬੀਰ ਬਿਬ ਆਸਤ ਧਾਰੇ ਨਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
147.t: dhouoo beer bib aasat dhaare nihaare ||
147.e: Both the heroes had their weapons in their hands.

147.g: ਰਹੇ ਬ੍ਯੋਮ ਮੈ ਭੂਪ ਗਉਨੈ ਹਕਾਰੇ ॥
147.t: rahe bayom mai bhoop gaunai hakaare ||
147.e: It seemed as if the spirits of the dead kings moving the sky were calling them.

147.g: ਹਕਾ ਹਕ ਲਾਗੀ ਧਨੰ ਧੰਨ ਜੰਪ੍ਰਯੋ ॥
147.t: hakaa hak laagee dhana(n) dha(n)n ja(n)prayo ||
147.e: They were shouting seeing their heroism, they were praising them with the words “Well done, bravo!”

147.g: ਚਕ੍ਰਯੋ ਜਛ ਰਾਜੰ ਪ੍ਰਿਥੀ ਲੋਕ ਕੰਪ੍ਯੋ ॥੧੫॥੨੩੩॥
147.t: chakrayo jachh raaja(n) pirathee lok ka(n)payo ||15||233||
147.e: The king of Yakshas seeing their bravery was astonished and the earth was trembling.15.233.

147.g: ਹਨਿਓ ਰਾਜ ਦੁਰਜੋਧਨੰ ਜੁਧ ਭੂਮੰ ॥
147.t: hanio raaj dhurajodhana(n) judh bhooma(n) ||
147.e: (Ultimately) the king Duryodhana was killed in the battlefield.

147.g: ਭਜੇ ਸਭੈ ਜੋਧਾ ਚਲੀ ਧਾਮ ਧੂਮੰ ॥
147.t: bhaje sabhai jodhaa chalee dhaam dhooma(n) ||
147.e: All the noisy warriors ran helter-skelter.

147.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਰਾਜ ਨਿਹਕੰਟਕੰ ਕਉਰਪਾਲੰ ॥
147.t: kariyo raaj nihaka(n)Taka(n) kaurapaala(n) ||
147.e: (After that) Pandavas ruled over the family of Kauravas unconcerned.

147.g: ਪੁਨਰ ਜਾਇ ਕੈ ਮਝਿ ਸਿਝੈ ਹਿਵਾਲੰ ॥੧੬॥੨੩੪॥
147.t: punar jai kai majh sijhai hivaala(n) ||16||234||
147.e: Then they went to Himalaya mountains.16.234.

147.g: ਤਹਾ ਏਕ ਗੰਧ੍ਰਬ ਸਿਉ ਜੁਧ ਮਚ੍ਯੋ ॥
147.t: tahaa ek ga(n)dhrab siau judh machayo ||
147.e: At that time a war was waged with a Gandharva.

147.g: ਤਹਾ ਭੂਰਪਾਲੰ ਧੂਰਾ ਰੰਗੁ ਰਚ੍ਯੋ ॥
147.t: tahaa bhoorapaala(n) dhooraa ra(n)g rachayo ||
147.e: There that Gandharva adopted a wonderful garb.

147.g: ਤਹਾ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਕੇ ਭੀਮ ਹਸਤੀ ਚਲਾਏ ॥
147.t: tahaa satr ke bheem hasatee chalaae ||
147.e: Bhima threw there the elephants of the enemy upwards.

147.g: ਫਿਰੇ ਮਧਿ ਗੈਣੰ ਅਜਉ ਲਉ ਨ ਆਏ ॥੧੭॥੨੩੫॥
147.t: fire madh gaina(n) ajau lau na aae ||17||235||
147.e: Which are still moving in the sky and have not returned as yet.17.235.

147.g: ਸੁਨੈ ਬੈਨ ਕਉ ਭੂਪ ਇਉ ਐਠ ਨਾਕੰ ॥
147.t: sunai bain kau bhoop iau aaiTh naaka(n) ||
147.e: Hearing these words, the king Janmeja turned his nose in such a manner,

147.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਹਾਸ ਮੰਦੈ ਬੁਲ੍ਯੋ ਏਮ ਬਾਕੰ ॥
147.t: kariyo haas ma(n)dhai bulayo em baaka(n) ||
147.e: And laughed contemptuously as though the utterance about the elephants was not true.

147.g: ਰਹਿਯੋ ਨਾਕ ਮੈ ਕੁਸਟ ਛਤ੍ਰੀ ਸਵਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: rahiyo naak mai kusaT chhatree savaana(n) ||
147.e: With this disbelief the thirty-sixth part of leprosy remained in his nose,

147.g: ਭਈ ਤਉਨ ਹੀ ਰੋਗ ਤੇ ਭੂਪ ਹਾਨੰ ॥੧੮॥੨੩੬॥
147.t: bhiee taun hee rog te bhoop haana(n) ||18||236||
147.e: And with this ailment, the king passed away.18.236.

147.g: ਚੌਪਈ ॥
147.t: chauapiee ||
147.e: CHAUPAI

147.g: ਇਮ ਚਉਰਾਸੀ ਬਰਖ ਪ੍ਰਮਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: eim chauraasee barakh pramaana(n) ||
147.e: In this way for eighty-four years,

147.g: ਸਪਤ ਮਾਹ ਚਉਬੀਸ ਦਿਨਾਨੰ ॥
147.t: sapat maeh chaubees dhinaana(n) ||
147.e: Seven months and twenty-four days,

147.g: ਰਾਜ ਕੀਓ ਜਨਮੇਜਾ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
147.t: raaj keeo janamejaa raajaa ||
147.e: The king Janmeja remained the ruler

147.g: ਕਾਲ ਨੀਸਾਨੁ ਬਹੁਰਿ ਸਿਰਿ ਗਾਜਾ ॥੧੯॥੨੩੭॥
147.t: kaal neesaan bahur sir gaajaa ||19||237||
147.e: Then, the trumpet of Death sounded over his head.19.237.

147.g: ਇਤਿ ਜਨਮੇਜਾ ਸਮਾਪਤ ਭਇਆ ॥
147.t: eit janamejaa samaapat bhiaa ||
147.e: Thus the king Janmeja breathed his last.

148.e: CHAUPAI
Asumedh and Asumedhan (the sons of Janmeja),
Were great heroes and truthful (princes).
They were very brave, mighty and archers.

148.g: ਗਾਵਤ ਕੀਰਤ ਦੇਸ ਸਭ ਘਰ ਘਰ ॥੧॥੨੩੮॥
148.t: gaavat keerat dhes sabh ghar ghar ||1||238||
148.e: Their praises were sung in every home in the country.1.238.

148.g: ਮਹਾ ਬੀਰ ਅਰੁ ਮਹਾ ਧਨੁਖ ਧਰ ॥
148.t: mahaa beer ar mahaa dhanukh dhar ||
148.e: They were supreme warriors and supreme archers.

148.g: ਕਾਪਤ ਤੀਨ ਲੋਕ ਜਾ ਕੇ ਡਰ ॥
148.t: kaapat teen lok jaa ke ddar ||
148.e: Because of their fear, the three worlds trembled.
They were kings of indivisible glory.
They were persons of unlimited splendour and the whole world remembered them.2.239.
On the other hand, Ajai Singh was a superb hero,
Who was a great monarch and adept in fourteen learnings.
He was without any vices, he was incomparable and of unweighable minght,
Who conqured many enemies and mashed them.3.240.
He was the conqueror of many wars.
None of the weapon-wielders could escape him.
He was a great hero, possessing great qualities
And all the world venerated him.4.241.
At the time of death, the king janmeja,
Consulted his council of ministers,
As to whom should the kingship be awarded?
They looked for the mark of kingship.5.242.

148.g: ਇਨ ਮਹਿ ਰਾਜ ਕਵਨ ਕਉ ਦੀਜੈ ॥
148.t: ein meh raaj kavan kau dheejai ||
148.e: Out of these three who should be given the kingship?

148.g: ਕਉਨ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਤ ਸੁਤ ਕਉ ਨ੍ਰਿਪੁ ਕੀਜੈ ॥
148.t: kaun nirapat sut kau nirap keejai ||
148.e: Which son of the king should be made the king?

148.g: ਰਜੀਆ ਪੂਤ ਨ ਰਾਜ ਕੀ ਜੋਗਾ ॥
148.t: rajeeaa poot na raaj kee jogaa ||
148.e: The son of the maid-servant is not entitled to be the king

148.g: ਯਾਹਿ ਕੇ ਜੋਗ ਨ ਰਾਜ ਕੇ ਭੋਗਾ ॥੬॥੨੪੩॥
148.t: yaeh ke jog na raaj ke bhogaa ||6||243||
148.e: The enjoyments of kingship are not meant for him.6.243.
(The eldest son) Asumedh was made the king,
And all the people cheered him as king.
The funeral rites of Janmeja were performed.
There were great rejoicings in the house of Asumedh.7.244.
Another one brother that the king had,
Was given enormous wealth and precious articles.
He was also made one of the ministers,
And placed him at another position.8.245.
The third one, who was the son of maid-servant.
He was given the position of army-general
He was made the Bakhshi

148.g: ਸਬ ਦਲ ਕੋ ਤਿਹ ਕਾਮੁ ਚਲਾਇਓ ॥੯॥੨੪੬॥
148.t: sab dhal ko teh kaam chalaio ||9||246||
148.e: And he administered all the work of the forces.9.246.
(All the brothers) were happy on getting their positions in kingdom.
The king felt great pleasure in seeing dances.
There were thirteen hundred and sixty-four Mridangs,
And millions of other musical instruments resounded in his presence.10.247.
The second brother took to heavy drinding.
He was fond of applying perfumes and seeing dances.
Both the brothers forgot to perform the royal responsibilities,

148.g: ਵਾਹੀ ਕੈ ਜਾਇ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਸਿਰ ਝੂਲਾ ॥੧੧॥੨੪੮॥
148.t: vaahee kai jai chhatr sir jhoolaa ||11||248||
148.e: And the canopy of royalty was held on the head of the third one.11.248.

148.g: ਕਰਤ ਕਰਤ ਬਹੁ ਦਿਨ ਅਸ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
148.t: karat karat bahu dhin as raajaa ||
148.e: After the passage of many days in the kingdom like this,
Both the brothers forgot the royal responsibilities.

148.g: ਮਦ ਕਰਿ ਅੰਧ ਭਏ ਦੋਊ ਭ੍ਰਾਤਾ ॥
148.t: madh kar a(n)dh bhe dhouoo bhraataa ||
148.e: Both the brother became blind with heavy drinking,

149.e: And forgot everything about kingdom.12.249.
DOHRA

149.g: ਜਿਹ ਚਾਹੇ ਤਾ ਕੋ ਹਨੇ ਜੋ ਬਾਛੈ ਸੋ ਲੇਇ ॥
149.t: jeh chaahe taa ko hane jo baachhai so lei ||
149.e: Whomsoever (Ajai Singh) wants he kills him, whatever he desires, he gets.

149.g: ਜਿਹ ਰਾਖੈ ਸੋਈ ਰਹੈ ਜਿਹ ਜਾਨੈ ਤਿਹ ਦੇਇ ॥੧੩॥੨੫੦॥
149.t: jeh raakhai soiee rahai jeh jaanai teh dhei ||13||250||
149.e: Whomsoever he protects, he remains safe, and whosoever he considers protagonist, he bestows on him the desired position.13.250.
CHAUPI

149.g: ਐਸੀ ਭਾਤ ਕੀਨੋ ਇਹ ਜਬ ਹੀ ॥
149.t: aaisee bhaat keeno ieh jab hee ||
149.e: When he began such a treatment,

149.g: ਪ੍ਰਜਾ ਲੋਕ ਸਭ ਬਸ ਭਏ ਤਬ ਹੀ ॥
149.t: prajaa lok sabh bas bhe tab hee ||
149.e: All the subject with this, came under his control

149.g: ਅਉ ਬਸਿ ਹੋਇ ਗਏ ਨੇਬ ਖਵਾਸਾ ॥
149.t: aau bas hoi ge neb khavaasaa ||
149.e: And the chieftains and other prominent persons came under his control,

149.g: ਜੋ ਰਾਖਤ ਥੇ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੀ ਆਸਾ ॥੧॥੨੫੧॥
149.t: jo raakhat the nirap kee aasaa ||1||251||
149.e: Who had earlier owned allegiance to the king.1.251.
One day all the three sagacious brothers,
Began to play chess.
When the dice was thrown, (one of the two real brothers) thought in indignation,
And uttered these words, while Ajai listened.2.252.
DOHRA

149.g: ਕਹਾ ਕਰੈ ਦਾ ਕਹ ਪਰੈ ਕਹ ਯਹ ਬਾਧੈ ਸੂਤ ॥
149.t: kahaa karai dhaa keh parai keh yeh baadhai soot ||
149.e: Let us see, what he does  how doth he throw the dice   how shalt he keep the propriety of conduct?

149.g: ਕਹਾ ਸਤ੍ਰੁ ਯਾ ਤੇ ਮਰੈ ਜੋ ਰਜੀਆ ਕਾ ਪੂਤ ॥੩॥੨੫੩॥
149.t: kahaa satr yaa te marai jo rajeeaa kaa poot ||3||253||
149.e: How shalt the enemy be killed by him, who himself is the son of maid-servant?3.253.
CHAUPI
We have thought about this game to-day.
That we utter apparently.
One of them took the gems of the kingdom.
The second one took horses, camels and elephants.1.254.
The princes distributed all the forces.
The divided the army in three parts.
They thought, how the dice be cast and the rouse be played?
How the game and trick be played?2.255.
The game of dice was began to watch the play.
The high and low all began to watch the play
The fire of jealousy increased in their hearts,
Which is said to be the destroyer of the kings.3.256.

149.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੈ ਬੀਚ ਪਰੀ ਅਸ ਖੇਲਾ ॥
149.t: tin kai beech paree as khelaa ||
149.e: The game was played thus amongst them,

149.g: ਕਟਨ ਸੁ ਹਿਤ ਭਇਉ ਮਿਟਨ ਦੁਹੇਲਾ ॥
149.t: kaTan su hit bhiau miTan dhuhelaa ||
149.e: That they reached the stage of destroying one another and it was difficult to pacify them.
In the beginning the princes put the gems and wealth to stake
Then they bet the clothes, horses and elephants, they lost all.4.257.
The wrangling increased on both the sides.

149.g: ਦੁਹ ਦਿਸ ਉਠੇ ਸੁਭਟ ਅਸ ਕਾਢਾ ॥
149.t: dhuh dhis uThe subhaT as kaaddaa ||
149.e: On both the sides, the warriors drew their swords
The sharp edges of the swords glistened,
And many corpses lay scattered there.5.258.
The vamps and demons wandered with pleasure
The vultures and ganas of Shiva manifested their pride through their gay voices.
The ghosts and goblins danced and sang.
Somewhere the Baitals raised their voice.6.259.
Somewhere the sharp edges of the swords gleamed.
The heads of warriors and trunks of elephants lay scattered on the earth.
Somewhere the intoxicated elephants were trumpeting after having fallen.
Somewhere the furious warriors in the battlefield rolled down.7.260.
Somewhere the wounded horses have fallen and are neighing.
Somewhere the terrible warriors are lying down  they have been sent.

149.g: ਕਟਿ ਗਏ ਕਹੂੰ ਕਉਚ ਅਰੁ ਚਰਮਾ ॥
149.t: kaT ge kahoo(n) kauch ar charamaa ||
149.e: Someone’s armour was cut down and someone’s was broken.

150.g: ਕਟਿ ਗਏ ਗਜ ਬਾਜਨ ਕੇ ਬਰਮਾ ॥੮॥੨੬੧॥
150.t: kaT ge gaj baajan ke baramaa ||8||261||
150.e: Somewhere the armours of elephants and horses were cut down.8.261.
Somewhere the vamps were raising joyful shrieks
Somewhere the ghosts were dancing, while clapping their hands
The fifty-two heroic spirits were wandering in all the four directions
Maru musical mode was being played.9.262.

150.g: ਰਣ ਅਸ ਕਾਲ ਜਲਧ ਜਿਮ ਗਾਜਾ ॥
150.t: ran as kaal jaladh jim gaajaa ||
150.e: The war was waged so violently as if the ocean was thundering
The gathering of ghosts and goblins ran away in great feat.

150.g: ਰਣ ਮਾਰੂ ਇਹ ਦਿਸ ਤੇ ਬਾਜ੍ਯੋ ॥

150.e: The Maru Raga was played from this side,

150.e: The support of the sword remained only with the warriors.
The trunks of many elephants were chopped off.
Somewhere the vamps and Baitals danced.
Somewhere the terrible ghosts and goblins were running here and there.11.264.
Many trunks cut into halves were running.
The princes were fighting and were stabilizing their positions.
The musical modes were played with such intensity,
That even the cowards did not run away from the field.12.265.
Million of drums and musical instruments sounded.
The elephants also joined this music with their trumpets.
The swords gleamed like lightning,
And the shafts came like rain from clouds.13.266.
The wounded warriors with dripping blood revolved,
As if the intoxicated persons are playing Holi.

150.g: ਗਿਰ ਗਏ ਕਹੂੰ ਜਿਰਹ ਅਰੁ ਜੁਆਨਾ ॥

150.e: Somewhere the armour and the warriors had fallen
Somewhere the vultures shrieked and the dogs barked.14.267.

150.g: ਉਨ ਦਲ ਦੁਹੂੰ ਭਾਇਨ ਕੋ ਭਾਜਾ ॥

150.e: The forces of both the brothers ran helter and skelter.

150.e: No pauper and king could stand there (before Ajai Singh).
The running kings with their forces entered the beautiful country of Orissa,
Whose king ‘Tilak’ was a person of good qualities.15.268.

150.g: ਮਦ ਕਰਿ ਮਤ ਭਏ ਜੇ ਰਾਜਾ ॥
150.t: madh kar mat bhe je raajaa ||
150.e: The kings who get intoxicated with wine,

150.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੇ ਗਏ ਐਸ ਹੀ ਕਾਜਾ ॥
150.t: tin ke ge aais hee kaajaa ||
150.e: All their errands are destroyed like this.
(Ajai Singh) sezed the kingdom and held the canopy on his head.
He caused himself to be called Maharaja.16.269.
The defeated Asumedh was running in front,
And the great army was pursuing him.
Asumedh went to the kingdom of Maharaja Tilak,
Who was a most appropriate king.17.270.
There lived a Sanaudhi Brahmin.

150.g: ਪੰਡਤ ਬਡੇ ਮਹਾ ਬਡ ਗੁਨ ਜਨ ॥

150.e: He was a very great Pundit and had many great qualities.

150.e: He was the preceptor of the king and all worshiped him.

150.g: ਤਿਹ ਬਿਨੁ ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਮਾਨਹਿ ਦੂਜਾ ॥੧੮॥੨੭੧॥
150.t: teh bin avar na maaneh dhoojaa ||18||271||
150.e: None other was abored there.18.271.

CHAUPAI
The king (Ajai Singh) sent his messengers (to king Tilak) and (Sanaudhi Brahmin).
Who satisfied all the incoming Brahmin.
(These messengers saidJ “Asumedh and Asumedhan,
“Have run and hid themselves in thy home.1.287.

152.g: ਕੈ ਦਿਜ ਬਾਧ ਦੇਹੁ ਦੁਐ ਮੋਹੂ ॥
152.t: kai dhij baadh dheh dhuaai mohoo ||
152.e: “O Brahmin, either bind and deliver them to us
“O thou shalt be considered like them

152.g: ਕਰਿਓ ਨ ਪੂਜਾ ਦੇਉ ਨ ਦਾਨਾ ॥
152.t: kario na poojaa dheau na dhaanaa ||
152.e: “Thou shalt neither be worshipped nor any gift be given to thee

152.g: ਤੋ ਕੋ ਦੁਖ ਦੇਵੋ ਦਿਜ ਨਾਨਾ ॥੨॥੨੮੮॥
152.t: to ko dhukh dhevo dhij naanaa ||2||288||
152.e: “Thou shalt then be given various types of sufferings.2.288.
“Why hast thou hugged these two dead ones to thy bosom?
“Give them back to us  Why art thou hesitating?

152.g: ਜਉ ਦੁਐ ਏ ਤੁਮ ਦੇਹੁ ਨ ਮੋਹੂ ॥
152.t: jau dhuaai e tum dheh na mohoo ||
152.e: “If thou dost not return both of them to me,

152.g: ਤਉ ਹਮ ਸਿਖ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਹੈ ਤੋਹੂ ॥੩॥੨੮੯॥
152.t: tau ham sikh na hoi hai tohoo ||3||289||
152.e: “Then we shall not be thy disciples.”3.289.
Then the Sanaudhi Brahmin got up early in the morning and took bath.
He worshipped in various ways the gods and manes.
Then he put the frontal marks of sandal and saffron on his forehead.

152.g: ਚਲ ਕਰ ਰਾਜ ਸਭਾ ਮੈ ਆਏ ॥੪॥੨੯੦॥
152.t: chal kar raaj sabhaa mai aae ||4||290||
152.e: After that he walked upto his court.4.290.
The Brahmin said:

152.g: ਹਮਰੀ ਵੈ ਨ ਪਰੈ ਦੁਐ ਡੀਠਾ ॥
152.t: hamaree vai na parai dhuaai ddeeThaa ||
152.e: “Neither have I seen both of them,
“Nor have they taken shelter.
“Whosoever has given thee news about them, he hath told a lie,
“O Emperor, the king of kings.1.291.
“O Emperor, the king of kings,
“O the hero of all the universe and Master of the earth
“While sitting here, I am giving blessings to thee,
“Thou , O monarch, art the Lord of the kings.”2.292.
The king said:
“If thou art thy own well-wisher,

152.g: ਵੈ ਦੁਇ ਬਾਧ ਦੇਹੁ ਮੁਹਿ ਅਬਹੀ ॥
152.t: vai dhui baadh dheh muh abahee ||
152.e: “Bind both of them and give them immediately to me
“I shall make all of them the food of fire,
“And worship thee as my father.”3.293.

152.g: ਜੋ ਨ ਪਰੈ ਵੈ ਭਾਜ ਤਿਹਾਰੇ ॥
152.t: jo na parai vai bhaaj tihaare ||
152.e: “If they have not run and concealed themselves in thy house,
“Then thou obeyest me today
“I shall prepare very tasteful food for thee,

152.g: ਹਮ ਤੁਮ ਵੈ ਤੀਨੋ ਮਿਲ ਖਾਵੈ ॥੪॥੨੯੪॥
152.t: ham tum vai teeno mil khaavai ||4||294||
152.e: “Which they, thou and me, all shall eat together.”4.294.

152.g: ਦਿਜ ਸੁਨ ਬਾਤ ਚਲੇ ਸਭ ਧਾਮਾ ॥
152.t: dhij sun baat chale sabh dhaamaa ||
152.e: Hearing these words of the king, all the Brahmins went to their homes,
And asked their brothers, sons and elders:
“If they are bound and given, then we lose our Dharma,
“If we eat their food, then we pollute our Karmas.”5.295.
“This son of the maid-servant is a mighty warriors,
“Who hath conquered and mashed the Kshatriya forces.
“He hath acquired his kingdom with his own might,

153.g: ਇਨ ਕੋ ਕਾਢਿ ਧਰਨ ਤੇ ਦੀਨਾ ॥੬॥੨੯੬॥
153.t: ein ko kaadd dharan te dheenaa ||6||296||
153.e: “And hath ousted them from his bundaries.”6.296.

153.g: ਤੋਟਕ ਛੰਦ ॥
153.t: toTak chha(n)dh ||
153.e: TOTAK STANZA

153.g: ਇਮ ਬਾਤ ਜਬੈ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਤੇ ਸੁਨਿਯੰ ॥
153.t: eim baat jabai nirap te suniya(n) ||
153.e: When they heard the king saying in this manner,

153.g: ਗ੍ਰਹ ਬੈਠ ਸਬੈ ਦਿਜ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਕੀਯੰ ॥
153.t: greh baiTh sabai dhij ma(n)tr keeya(n) ||
153.e: All the Brahmins sat in their houses and decided,

153.g: ਅਜ ਸੈਨ ਅਜੈ ਭਟ ਦਾਸ ਸੁਤੰ ॥
153.t: aj sain ajai bhaT dhaas suta(n) ||
153.e: That this son of maid-servant is unconquerable hero and his army is unconquerable.

153.g: ਅਤ ਦੁਹਕਰ ਕੁਤਸਿਤ ਕ੍ਰੂਰ ਮਤੰ ॥੭॥੨੯੭॥
153.t: at dhuhakar kutasit kraoor mata(n) ||7||297||
153.e: He is very stern and a man of vicious intellect and actions.7.297.

153.g: ਮਿਲ ਖਾਇ ਤਉ ਖੋਵੈ ਜਨਮ ਜਗੰ ॥
153.t: mil khai tau khovai janam jaga(n) ||
153.e: If we eat in his company, then we lose our birth in the world

153.g: ਨਹਿ ਖਾਤ ਤੁ ਜਾਤ ਹੈ ਕਾਲ ਮਗੰ ॥
153.t: neh khaat ta jaat hai kaal maga(n) ||
153.e: If we do not eat, then we will have to go in the jaws of death.

153.g: ਮਿਲ ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਸੁ ਕੀਜੈ ਕਉਨ ਮਤੰ ॥
153.t: mil mitr su keejai kaun mata(n) ||
153.e: After assembling we should take such decision,

153.g: ਜਿਹ ਭਾਤ ਰਹੇ ਜਗ ਆਜ ਪਤੰ ॥੮॥੨੯੮॥
153.t: jeh bhaat rahe jag aaj pata(n) ||8||298||
153.e: With which we keep up our honour in the world.8.298.

153.g: ਸੁਨ ਰਾਜਨ ਰਾਜ ਮਹਾਨ ਮਤੰ ॥
153.t: sun raajan raaj mahaan mata(n) ||
153.e: After taking decision, they said to the king : “O king of great intellect, listen,

153.g: ਅਨਭੀਤ ਅਜੀਤ ਸਮਸਤ ਛਿਤੰ ॥
153.t: anabheet ajeet samasat chhita(n) ||
153.e: “Thou art fearless and unconquerable monarch on the whole earth

153.g: ਅਨਗਾਹ ਅਥਾਹ ਅਨੰਤ ਦਲੰ ॥
153.t: anagaeh athaeh ana(n)t dhala(n) ||
153.e: “Thou art unfathomable, bottomless and master of innumerable forces

153.g: ਅਨਭੰਗ ਅਗੰਜ ਮਹਾ ਪ੍ਰਬਲੰ ॥੯॥੨੯੯॥
153.t: anabha(n)g aga(n)j mahaa prabala(n) ||9||299||
153.e: “Thou art invincible, unassailable and Soverrign of Supreme might.9.299.

153.g: ਇਹ ਠਉਰ ਨ ਛਤ੍ਰੀ ਏਕ ਨਰੰ ॥
153.t: eeh Thaur na chhatree ek nara(n) ||
153.e: “There is not even one Kshatriya in this place.

153.g: ਸੁਨ ਸਾਚੁ ਮਹਾ ਨ੍ਰਿਪਰਾਜ ਬਰੰ ॥
153.t: sun saach mahaa niraparaaj bara(n) ||
153.e: “O great and superb monarch, listen to his truth.”

153.g: ਕਹਿਕੈ ਦਿਜ ਸਉ ਉਠਿ ਜਾਤ ਭਏ ॥
153.t: kahikai dhij sau uTh jaat bhe ||
153.e: Uttering these words, the Brahmins got up and went away

153.g: ਵੇਹ ਆਨਿ ਜਸੂਸ ਬਤਾਇ ਦਏ ॥੧੦॥੩੦੦॥
153.t: veh aan jasoos batai dhe ||10||300||
153.e: But the spies gave the news (of the presence of his brothers there).10.300.

153.g: ਤਹਾ ਸਿੰਘ ਅਜੈ ਮਨਿ ਰੋਸ ਬਢੀ ॥
153.t: tahaa si(n)gh ajai man ros baddee ||
153.e: Then the anger increased in the mind of Ajai Singh.

153.g: ਕਰਿ ਕੋਪ ਚਮੂੰ ਚਤੁਰੰਗ ਚਢੀ ॥
153.t: kar kop chamoo(n) chatura(n)g chaddee ||
153.e: In great rage, he ordered his forces of four types to move forward.

153.g: ਤਹ ਜਾਇ ਪਰੀ ਜਹ ਖਤ੍ਰ ਬਰੰ ॥
153.t: teh jai paree jeh khatr bara(n) ||
153.e: The army reached there where both the superb Kshatriyas were stationed.

153.g: ਬਹੁ ਕੂਦਿ ਪਰੇ ਦਿਜ ਸਾਮ ਘਰੰ ॥੧੧॥੩੦੧॥
153.t: bahu koodh pare dhij saam ghara(n) ||11||301||
153.e: They jumped from the roof of the house into the abode of Sanaudhi Brahmin to take shelter.11.301.

153.g: ਦਿਜ ਮੰਡਲ ਬੈਠਿ ਬਿਚਾਰੁ ਕੀਯੋ ॥
153.t: dhij ma(n)ddal baiTh bichaar keeyo ||
153.e: The assembly of Brahmins met and reflected on the issue.

153.g: ਸਬ ਹੀ ਦਿਜ ਮੰਡਲ ਗੋਦ ਲੀਯੋ ॥
153.t: sab hee dhij ma(n)ddal godh leeyo ||
153.e: The whole assembly affectionately kept the two in their midst.

153.g: ਕਹੁ ਕਉਨ ਸੁ ਬੈਠਿ ਬਿਚਾਰ ਕਰੈ ॥
153.t: kahu kaun su baiTh bichaar karai ||
153.e: They ruminated over the issue as to what measures be taken?

153.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਸਾਥ ਰਹੈ ਨਹੀ ਏਊ ਮਰੈ ॥੧੨॥੩੦੨॥
153.t: nirap saath rahai nahee euoo marai ||12||302||
153.e: So that they may not offend the king and also save the two refugees.12.302.

153.g: ਇਹ ਭਾਤਿ ਕਹੀ ਤਿਹ ਤਾਹਿ ਸਭੈ ॥
153.t: eeh bhaat kahee teh taeh sabhai ||
153.e: When they said these words, then all of them desired:

153.g: ਤੁਮ ਤੋਰ ਜਨੇਵਨ ਦੇਹੁ ਅਬੈ ॥
153.t: tum tor janevan dheh abai ||
153.e: “Break the secred threads immediately.”

153.g: ਜੋਊ ਮਾਨਿ ਕਹਿਯੋ ਸੋਈ ਲੇਤ ਭਏ ॥
153.t: jouoo maan kahiyo soiee let bhe ||
153.e: Those who accepted it, they became without the thread.

153.g: ਤੇਊ ਬੈਸ ਹੁਇ ਬਾਣਜ ਕਰਤ ਭਏ ॥੧੩॥੩੦੩॥
153.t: teuoo bais hui baanaj karat bhe ||13||303||
153.e: They became Vaishyas and took trade as their occupation.13.303.

153.g: ਜਿਹ ਤੋਰ ਜਨੇਊ ਨ ਕੀਨ ਹਠੰ ॥
153.t: jeh tor janeuoo na keen haTha(n) ||
153.e: Those who did not dare to break the thread doggedly

153.g: ਤਿਨ ਸਿਉ ਉਨ ਭੋਜੁ ਕੀਓ ਇਕਠੰ ॥
153.t: tin siau un bhoj keeo ikaTha(n) ||
153.e: The two refugee kings dined together with them.

153.g: ਫਿਰ ਜਾਇ ਜਸੂਸਹਿ ਐਸ ਕਹਿਓ ॥
153.t: fir jai jasooseh aais kahio ||
153.e: Them the spies went and told (the king Ajai Singh),

153.g: ਇਨ ਮੈ ਉਨ ਮੈ ਇਕ ਭੇਦੁ ਰਹਿਓ ॥੧੪॥੩੦੪॥
153.t: ein mai un mai ik bhedh rahio ||14||304||
153.e: There is one difference between the former and the latter.14.304.

153.g: ਪੁਨਿ ਬੋਲਿ ਉਠਿਯੋ ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਸਰਬ ਦਿਜੰ ॥
153.t: pun bol uThiyo nirap sarab dhija(n) ||
153.e: Then the king (Ajai Singh) addressed all his Brahmins:

153.g: ਨਹਿ ਛਤ੍ਰਤੁ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੁਤਾਹਿ ਤੁਅੰ ॥
153.t: neh chhatrat dheh sutaeh tua(n) ||
153.e: “If there is no Kshatriya amongst them, then give your daughters in marriage to them.”

153.g: ਮਰਿਗੇ ਸੁਨਿ ਬਾਤ ਮਨੋ ਸਬ ਹੀ ॥
153.t: marige sun baat mano sab hee ||
153.e: Hearing these words none replied as though they were dead.

153.g: ਉਠਿ ਕੈ ਗ੍ਰਿਹਿ ਜਾਤ ਭਏ ਤਬ ਹੀ ॥੧੫॥੩੦੫॥
153.t: auTh kai gireh jaat bhe tab hee ||15||305||
153.e: Then they got up and went away to their homes.15.305.

153.g: ਸਭ ਬੈਠਿ ਬਿਚਾਰਨ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਲਗੇ ॥
153.t: sabh baiTh bichaaran ma(n)tr lage ||
153.e: Then all gathered to take a decision.

153.g: ਸਭ ਸੋਕ ਕੇ ਸਾਗਰ ਬੀਚ ਡੁਬੇ ॥
153.t: sabh sok ke saagar beech ddube ||
153.e: All of them seemed to have been drowned in the ocean of sorrow.

153.g: ਵਹਿ ਬਾਧ ਬਹਿਠ ਅਤਿ ਤੇਊ ਹਠੰ ॥
153.t: veh baadh bahiTh at teuoo haTha(n) ||
153.e: He (Ajai Singh) wants to bind his brothers and the Brahmins were full of persistence,

153.g: ਹਮ ਏ ਦੋਊ ਭ੍ਰਾਤ ਚਲੈ ਇਕਠੰ ॥੧੬॥੩੦੬॥
153.t: ham e dhouoo bhraat chalai ikaTha(n) ||16||306||
153.e: We shall all side together with the brothers.’16.306.

153.g: ਹਠ ਕੀਨ ਦਿਜੈ ਤਿਨ ਲੀਨ ਸੁਤਾ ॥
153.t: haTh keen dhijai tin leen sutaa ||
153.e: The Sanaudh Brahmin persisted in not returning the refugee brothers, then the king Ajai Singh married his daughter.

153.g: ਅਤਿ ਰੂਪ ਮਹਾ ਛਬਿ ਪਰਮ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ॥
153.t: at roop mahaa chhab param prabhaa ||
153.e: She was very beautiful, winsome and glorious.

153.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਯੋ ਪੇਟ ਸਨੌਢ ਤੇ ਪੂਤ ਭਏ ॥
153.t: tirayo peT sanauadd te poot bhe ||
153.e: The sons born of that Sanaudh woman,

153.g: ਵਹਿ ਜਾਤਿ ਸਨੌਢ ਕਹਾਤ ਭਏ ॥੧੭॥੩੦੭॥
153.t: veh jaat sanauadd kahaat bhe ||17||307||
153.e: Were called Sanaudh.17.307.

153.g: ਸੁਤ ਅਉਰਨ ਕੇ ਉਹ ਠਾ ਜੁ ਅਹੈ ॥
153.t: sut aauran ke uh Thaa ju ahai ||
153.e: The sons of other kshatryas, who lived at that place,

153.g: ਉਤ ਛਤ੍ਰੀਅ ਜਾਤਿ ਅਨੇਕ ਭਏ ॥
153.t: aut chhatreea jaat anek bhe ||
153.e: They became Kshatriyas of many junior ccastes.

154.g: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ ਕੇ ਸੰਗਿ ਜੋ ਮਿਲਿ ਜਾਤੁ ਭਏ ॥
154.t: nirap ke sa(n)g jo mil jaat bhe ||
154.e: Those Brahmins who ate together with the king.
They were called Rajputs.18.308.

154.g: ਤਿਨ ਜੀਤ ਬਿਜੈ ਕਹੁ ਰਾਉ ਚੜ੍ਯੋ ॥
154.t: tin jeet bijai kahu raau chaRayo ||
154.e: After conquering them, the king (Ajai Singh) moved to gain further conquests.
His glory and magnificence increased enormously.

154.g: ਜੋਊ ਆਨਿ ਮਿਲੇ ਅਰੁ ਸਾਕ ਦਏ ॥
154.t: jouoo aan mile ar saak dhe ||
154.e: Those who surrendered before him and married their daughters to him,
They were also called Rajputs.19.309.

154.g: ਜਿਨ ਸਾਕ ਦਏ ਨਹਿ ਰਾਰਿ ਬਢੀ ॥
154.t: jin saak dhe neh raar baddee ||
154.e: Those who did not marry their daughters, the wrangle increased with them.

154.g: ਤਿਨ ਕੀ ਇਨ ਲੈ ਜੜ ਮੂਲ ਕਢੀ ॥
154.t: tin kee in lai jaR mool kaddee ||
154.e: He (the king) completely uprooted them.

154.g: ਦਲ ਤੇ ਬਲ ਤੇ ਧਨ ਟੂਟਿ ਗਏ ॥
154.t: dhal te bal te dhan TooT ge ||
154.e: The armies, might and wealth were finished.
And they adopted the occupation of traders.20.310.

154.g: ਜੋਊ ਆਨਿ ਮਿਲੇ ਨਹਿ ਜੋਰਿ ਲਰੇ ॥
154.t: jouoo aan mile neh jor lare ||
154.e: Those who did not surrender and fought violently,
Their bodies were bound and reduced to ashes in big fires.
They were burnt in the fire-altar-pit uninformed.
Thus there was a very great sacrifice of Kshatriyas.21.311.

154.g: ਇਤਿ ਅਜੈ ਸਿੰਘ ਕਾ ਰਾਜ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਭਇਆ ॥
154.t: eit ajai si(n)gh kaa raaj sa(n)pooran bhiaa ||
154.e: Here ends the complete Description of the Rule of Ajai Singh.
The King Jag: TOMAR STANZA BY THY GRACE
For eighty-two years, eight months and two days,
Ruled very prosperously the king of kings (Ajai Singh).1.312.
Listen, the king of great kingdom, who was treasure of fourteen learnings
Who recited the mantra of twelve letters and was the Supreme Sovereign on the earth.2.313.
Then the great king Jag took birth, who was very beautiful and affectionate
Who was highly lustrous than the sun, His great effulgence was indestructible.3.314.
He called all the great Brahmins. In order to perform the animal sacrifice,
He called very leaned Brahmins, who called themselves very beautiful like Cupid.4.315.
Many Brahmin beautiful like Cuaid were especially invited by the king.
Innumerable animals of the world, were caught and burnt in altar-pit thoughtlessly.5.316.
Ten times on one animal, the Vedic mantra was recited thoughtlessly.
The animal was burnt in the altar-pit, for which much wealth was received from the king.6.317.
By performing animal-sacrifice, the kingdom prospered in many ways.
For eighty-eight years and two months, the monarch ruled the kingdom.7.318.
Then the terrible sword of death, whose flame hath burnt the world
Broke the unbreakable king, whose rule was entirely glorious.8.319.

155.g: ਇਤਿ ਪੰਚਮੋ ਰਾਜ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥
155.t: eit pa(n)chamo raaj samaapatam sat subham sat ||
155.e: Here ends the Description of the Benign Rule of the Fifth King.
TOMAR STANZA BY THY GRACE
Then Muni became the king of the earth
The Lion-King of this world.
By conquering the unbreakable enemies,
He ruled gloriously over the earth.1.320.
He killed many enemies,
And did not leave even one of them alive.
He then ruled uninterrupted.
He sized other lands and held the canopy over his head.2.321.
He was person of superb and perfect beauty
An impetuous warrior-king
Glory-incarnate and devoid-king
The Sovereign of undivided and imperishable kingdom.3.322.
Conquering many kings,
And shooting many arrows,
Killing innumerable enemies,
He established immeasurable kingdom on the earth.4.323.
Ruling the prosperous kingdom for a long time,
The king of kings said thus
“Prepare and altar for sacrifice,
“And call the Brahmins quickly.”5.324.
Many Brahmins were then invited.
None of them was left at his home.
The consulation with ministers and Brahmins began.
The sagacious friend and ministers began to recite mantras.6.325.
Then the king of king said,
“There is incentive in my mind for a sacrifice
“What type of sacrificial altar be prepared?
“O my friends, tell me quickly.”7.326.
Then the friends consulted one another.
They told the king like this:
O generous monarch, listen,
“Thou art very sagacious in all the fourteen worlds.8.327.
“Listen, O king, in Satyuga,
“The goddess Chandi had performed the sacrifice
“By killing the enemy, the demon Mahishasura,
“She had pleased Shiva greatly”9.328.
After killing Mahishasura in the battlefield,
The canopy was held over the head of Indra.
She had pleased all the vamps,
And effaced the pride of the demons.10.329.
After conquering Mahishasura in the battlefield.
She had made the Brahmins and gods fearless
She called the god Indra,
And seizing the earth from Mahishasura, she held the canopy over his head.11.330.
She called the four-headed Brahma,
With her heart’s desire, she (the mother of the world),
Began the performance of the sacrifice
She had indivisible and powerful glory.12.331.
Then the four-headed Brahma spoke,
“Listen, O Chandi, I bow in obeisance to thee,
“Just as thou hast asked me,
“In the same way, I advise thee.”13.322.
The innumerable beings and creatures of the world,
The goddess herself called them to come,
And within her enemies she cut them in an instant.
With her loud voice she recited the Vedic mantras and performed the sacrifice.14.333.
ROOAAL STANZA BY THE GRACE

155.g: ਬੋਲਿ ਬਿਪਨ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਮਿਤ੍ਰਨ ਜਗ ਕੀਨ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
155.t: bol bipan ma(n)tr mitran jag keen apaar ||
155.e: The Brahmins began the performance of the sacrifice by the recitation of auspicious mantras

155.g: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਅਉਰ ਉਪਿੰਦ੍ਰ ਲੈ ਕੈ ਬੋਲਿ ਕੈ ਮੁਖ ਚਾਰ ॥
155.t: ei(n)dhr aaur upi(n)dhr lai kai bol kai mukh chaar ||
155.e: Brahma, Indra and other gods were also invited.

155.g: ਕਉਨ ਭਾਤਨ ਕੀਜੀਐ ਅਬ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਆਰੰਭ ॥
155.t: kaun bhaatan keejeeaai ab jag ko aara(n)bh ||
155.e: “In what way, the sacrifice be began now?” the king asked again,

155.g: ਆਜ ਮੋਹਿ ਉਚਾਰੀਐ ਸੁਨਿ ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਅਸੰਭ ॥੧॥੩੩੪॥
155.t: aaj moh uchaareeaai sun mitr ma(n)tr asa(n)bh ||1||334||
155.e: “O friends, give me to-day, thy advice in this impossible errand.”1.334.

155.g: ਮਾਸ ਕੇ ਪਲ ਕਾਟਿ ਕੈ ਪੜਿ ਬੇਦ ਮੰਤ੍ਰ ਅਪਾਰ ॥
155.t: maas ke pal kaaT kai paR bedh ma(n)tr apaar ||
155.e: The friend advised that the flesh chopped into bits alongwith the recitation of mantras,

155.g: ਅਗਨਿ ਭੀਤਰ ਹੋਮੀਐ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਾਜ ਰਾਜ ਅਬਿਚਾਰ ॥
155.t: agan bheetar homeeaai sun raaj raaj abichaar ||
155.e: Be burnt in the sacrificial fire  the king was asked to listen and act without any other thoughts

155.g: ਛੇਦਿ ਚਿਛੁਰ ਬਿੜਾਰਾਸੁਰ ਧੂਲਿ ਕਰਣਿ ਖਪਾਇ ॥
155.t: chhedh chichhur biRaaraasur dhool karan khapai ||
155.e: The goddess had killed the demons named Chithar and Biraal and destroyed Dhoolkaran

155.g: ਮਾਰ ਦਾਨਵ ਕਉ ਕਰਿਓ ਮਖ ਦੈਤ ਮੇਧ ਬਨਾਇ ॥੨॥੩੩੫॥
155.t: maar dhaanav kau kario makh dhait medh banai ||2||335||
155.e: After killing the demons she performed the demon-sacrifice.2.335.

155.g: ਤੈਸ ਹੀ ਮਖ ਕੀਜੀਐ ਸੁਨਿ ਰਾਜ ਰਾਜ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ॥
155.t: tais hee makh keejeeaai sun raaj raaj pracha(n)dd ||
155.e: “Listen, O most Glorious Sovereign, thou shouldst perform the sacrifice in that way

155.g: ਜੀਤਿ ਦਾਨਵ ਦੇਸ ਕੇ ਬਲਵਾਨ ਪੁਰਖ ਅਖੰਡ ॥
155.t: jeet dhaanav dhes ke balavaan purakh akha(n)dd ||
155.e: “O mighty and perfect Lord, therefore conquer all the demons of the country

155.g: ਤੈਸ ਹੀ ਮਖ ਮਾਰ ਕੈ ਸਿਰਿ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਫਿਰਾਇ ॥
155.t: tais hee makh maar kai sir i(n)dhr chhatr firai ||
155.e: “Just as the goddess having killed the demons, held the canopy over the head of Indra,

155.g: ਜੈਸ ਸੁਰ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਓ ਤਿਵ ਸੰਤ ਹੋਹੁ ਸਹਾਇ ॥੩॥੩੩੬॥
155.t: jais sur sukh paio tiv sa(n)t hoh sahai ||3||336||
155.e: “And made all the gods happy, similarly Thou mayst help the saints.”3.336.
(VISNU’S TWENTY-FOUR INCARNATIONS.
The Lord One and the Victory is of the Lord.
(VISNU’S TWENTY-FOUR INCARNATIONS.
By the Tenth King (Guru).
BY THY GRACE CHAUPAI
Now I describe the wonderful performance of twenty-four incarnations.

155.g: ਜਿਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਤਿਨ ਕਾ ਲਖਾ ਅਖਾਰਾ ॥
155.t: jeh bidh tin kaa lakhaa akhaaraa ||
155.e: In the way I visualized the same
O saints  listen to it attentively.
The poet Shyam is narrating it according or his own under-standing.1.
Whenever numerous tyrants take birth,
Then the Lord manifests himself in physical form
The KAL (Destroyer Lord) scans the play of all,
And ultimately destroys all.2.
The KAL (Destroyer Lord) causes the expansion of all
The same Temporal Lord ultimately destroys all
He manifests Himself in innumerable forms,
And Himself merges all within Hmself.3.

155.g: ਇਨ ਮਹਿ ਸ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਸੁ ਦਸ ਅਵਤਾਰਾ ॥
155.t: ein meh sirasaT su dhas avataaraa ||
155.e: In this creation is included the world and the ten incarnations
Within them pervades our Lord
Besides ten, other fourteen incarnations are also reckoned

155.g: ਕਹੋ ਜੁ ਤਿਨ ਤਿਨ ਕੀਏ ਅਖਾਰੁ ॥੪॥
155.t: kaho ju tin tin ke'ee akhaar ||4||
155.e: And I describe the performance of all them.4.
The KAL (Temporal Lord) conceals his name,
And imposes the villainy over the head of others

156.e: He Himself remains detached from the world,

156.g: ਜਾਨ ਲਏ ਜਾ ਨਾਮੈ ਤਬ ਤੇ ॥੫॥
156.t: jaan le jaa naamai tab te ||5||
156.e: I know this fact from the very beginning (ancient times).5.
He creates Himself and destroys Himself
But He imposes the responsibility on the head of others
He Himself remains detached and Beyond Everything
Therefore, He is called ‘Infinite’.6.
Those who are called twenty-four incarnations

156.g: ਤਿਨ ਭੀ ਤੁਮ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਤਨਿਕ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥
156.t: tin bhee tum prabh tanik na paae ||
156.e: O Lord! they even could not realise thee in a small measure
They became kings of the world and got deluded
Therefore they were called by innumerable names.7.

156.g: ਸਭ ਹੀ ਛਲਤ ਨ ਆਪ ਛਲਾਯਾ ॥
156.t: sabh hee chhalat na aap chhalaayaa ||
156.e: O Lord! Thou hast been deluding others, but could not be deluded by others
Therefore Thou art called ‘Crafty’
Thou becomest agitated on seeing the saints in agony,
Therefore Thou art also called ‘the fiend of the humble’.8.

156.g: ਅੰਤਿ ਕਰਤ ਸਭ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਕਾਲਾ ॥
156.t: a(n)t karat sabh jag ko kaalaa ||
156.e: At time Thou destroyest the universe

156.g: ਨਾਮੁ ਕਾਲ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਜਗ ਡਾਲਾ ॥
156.t: naam kaal taa te jag ddaalaa ||
156.e: Therefore the world hath named you KAL (the Destroyer Lord)
Thou hast been helping all the saints
Therefore the saints have reckoned Thy incarnations.9.
Seeing Thy mercifulness towards the lowly
Thy name ‘Deen Bandhu’ (the helper of the lowly) hath been thought out
Thou art Compassionate towards the saints
Therefore the world calls Thee ‘Karuna-nidhi’ (the Tresure of mercy).10.
Thou ever removest the distress of the saints
Therefore Thou art named ‘Sankat-haran’, the remover of the distresses

157.e: Thou hast been destroying the sufferings of the saints
Therefore Thou art called ‘Dukh-dahan’ (the destroyer of sufferings.11.
Thou art Infinite and none could know Thy limits
Therefore thou art called ‘Breant’ (the Boundless Lord)

157.g: ਜਗ ਮੋ ਰੂਪ ਸਭਨ ਕੈ ਧਰਤਾ ॥
157.t: jag mo roop sabhan kai dharataa ||
157.e: Thou createst the forms of all in the world
Therefore thou art called Creator.12.
None hath been able to comprehend Thee,
Therefore thou hast been called ‘Alakh’ (Incompre-hensible)

157.g: ਜੋਨਿ ਜਗਤ ਮੈ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਨ ਆਯਾ ॥
157.t: jon jagat mai kabahoo(n) na aayaa ||
157.e: Thou dost not take birth in the world
Therefore all called Thee ‘Ajon’ (Unborn).13.
Brahma and others have got tired in knowing Thy end
Who are the helpless gods Vishnu and Shiva?
The sun and moon also meditate on Thee
Therefore Thou art known as the Creator.14.
Thou art ever guiseless, and shall be guiseless
Therefore the world calls Thee ‘Abhekhi’ (Guiseless)
None knows Thy Invisible form
Therefore Thou art described as ‘Alekh’ (Incompre-hensible).15.
Thy beauty is unique and Thy forms are Innumerable
Thou art distinctly separate from all guise and not committed to any faith or idea
Thou art the Universal Donor and Thou Thyself dost not beg

157.g: ਜਾਨ ਲਯੋ ਕਰਤਾ ਹਮ ਤਬ ਤੇ ॥੧੬॥
157.t: jaan layo karataa ham tab te ||16||
157.e: Therefore I have known Thee as the Creator.16.
Thou art not influenced by any omen or auspicious time

157.g: ਹੈ ਯਹ ਕਥਾ ਜਗਤ ਮੈ ਮਾਲਮ ॥
157.t: hai yeh kathaa jagat mai maalam ||
157.e: This fact is known to all the world
None of the Yantras, Mantras and Tantras please Thee
And none could realise Thee by adopting different guises.17.
All the world is engaged in its own interests
And none comprehends the Transcendental Brahman
For Thy realization many go to the cremation ground and graveyards
But the Lord is not there in both of them.18.

157.g: ਏ ਦੋਊ ਮੋਹ ਬਾਦ ਮੋ ਪਚੇ ॥
157.t: e dhouoo moh baadh mo pache ||
157.e: Both of them (the Hindus and Muslims) are destroying themselves in attachments and in vain discussions and disputes
But O Lord! Thou art distinctly separate from both of them

157.g: ਜਾ ਤੇ ਛੂਟਿ ਗਯੋ ਭ੍ਰਮ ਉਰ ਕਾ ॥
157.t: jaa te chhooT gayo bhram ur kaa ||
157.e: He, with whose realization, the illusion of the mind is removed
Before that Lord, none is a Hindu of a Muslim.19.
One of them wears a Tasbi (the rosary of Muslims) and the other one wears Mala (the rosary of a Hindu)
One of them recites the Quran and the other one reads Puranas
The adherents of both the religions are foolishly dying in opposing each other,

157.g: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੋ ਰੰਗੁ ਨ ਲਾਗਾ ਗੂੜਾ ॥੨੦॥
157.t: prabh ko ra(n)g na laagaa gooRaa ||20||
157.e: And none of them is dyed in the love of the Lord.20.

157.g: ਜੋ ਜੋ ਰੰਗ ਏਕ ਕੇ ਰਾਚੇ ॥
157.t: jo jo ra(n)g ek ke raache ||
157.e: Those who are imbued in the love of the Lord,

157.g: ਤੇ ਤੇ ਲੋਕ ਲਾਜ ਤਜਿ ਨਾਚੇ ॥
157.t: te te lok laaj taj naache ||
157.e: They forsake their shyness and dance in ecstasy
Those who have recognized that Primal Purusha,

157.g: ਦੁਤੀਆ ਭਾਵ ਨ ਮਨ ਮਹਿ ਆਨਾ ॥੨੧॥
157.t: dhuteeaa bhaav na man meh aanaa ||21||
157.e: The duality is destroyed form their hearts.21.

157.g: ਜੋ ਜੋ ਭਾਵ ਦੁਤਿਯ ਮਹਿ ਰਾਚੇ ॥
157.t: jo jo bhaav dhutiy meh raache ||
157.e: Those who are absorbed in duality,

157.g: ਤੇ ਤੇ ਮੀਤ ਮਿਲਨ ਤੇ ਬਾਚੇ ॥
157.t: te te meet milan te baache ||
157.e: They are far away from the union of the Lord. Their supreme friend
They who have recognized the Supreme Purusha even a little,

157.g: ਤਿਨ ਹੀ ਪਰਮ ਤਤ ਕਹ ਜਾਨਾ ॥੨੨॥
157.t: tin hee param tat keh jaanaa ||22||
157.e: They have Comprehended Him as the Supreme Essence.22.
All the Yogis and Sannyasis
All the ascetics and monks with shaven heads and Muslims

158.e: They are all plundering the world in different guises
The real saints whose prop is the Name of the Lord, they hide themselved.23.
The people of he world, exhibit here in order to fill their bellies,
Because without heresy, they do not gain money

158.g: ਜਿਨ ਨਰ ਏਕ ਪੁਰਖ ਕਹ ਧਿਆਯੋ ॥
158.t: jin nar ek purakh keh dhiaayo ||
158.e: The person, who hath meditated only on the Supreme Purusha,

158.g: ਤਿਨ ਕਰਿ ਡਿੰਭ ਨ ਕਿਸੀ ਦਿਖਾਯੋ ॥੨੪॥
158.t: tin kar ddi(n)bh na kisee dhikhaayo ||24||
158.e: He hath never exhibited an act of heresy to anyone.24.

158.g: ਡਿੰਭ ਕਰੇ ਬਿਨੁ ਹਾਥਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ॥
158.t: ddi(n)bh kare bin haath na aavai ||
158.e: One’s interest remain unfulfilled without heresy
And none bows down his head before anyone without interest

158.g: ਜੋ ਇਹੁ ਪੇਟ ਨ ਕਾਹੂੰ ਹੋਤਾ ॥
158.t: jo ih peT na kaahoo(n) hotaa ||
158.e: If the belly been not attached with anyone,
Then there would have not been any king or pauper in this world.25.
Those who have recognized only God as the Lord of all,

158.g: ਤਿਨ ਕਰ ਡਿੰਭ ਨ ਕਿਸੂ ਦਿਖਾਯੋ ॥
158.t: tin kar ddi(n)bh na kisoo dhikhaayo ||
158.e: They have never exhibited any heresy to anyone

158.g: ਸੀਸ ਦੀਯੋ ਉਨ ਸਿਰਰ ਨ ਦੀਨਾ ॥
158.t: sees dheeyo un sirar na dheenaa ||
158.e: Such a person gets his head chopped off but never his creed
And such person considers his body equivalent only to a particle of dust.26.
One is called a Yogi on perforating his ears
And goes to the forest, performing many deceitful acts

158.g: ਏਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੋ ਤਤੁ ਨ ਲਯੋ ॥
158.t: ek naam ko tat na layo ||
158.e: But the person who hath not absorbed the essence of the Name in his heart,

158.g: ਬਨ ਕੋ ਭਯੋ ਨ ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਕੋ ਭਯੋ ॥੨੭॥
158.t: ban ko bhayo na gireh ko bhayo ||27||
158.e: He neither belongs to the forest nor his home.27.
Upto what extent this poor can describe?
Because one person cannot know the mystery of the Infinite Lord
Undoubtedly, if one may have millions of tongues,

158.g: ਗੁਣ ਸਮੁੰਦ੍ਰ ਤ੍ਵ ਪਾਰ ਨ ਪਰੈ ॥੨੮॥
158.t: gun samu(n)dhr tavai paar na parai ||28||
158.e: Even then the ocean of Thy Attributes cannot be fathomed.28.

158.g: ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਕਾਲ ਸਭ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਤਾਤਾ ॥
158.t: pratham kaal sabh jag ko taataa ||
158.e: First of all the Lord as KAL is the primal farther of the whole universe
And from him emanated the Powerful Lustre
The same Lord was considered as Bhavani,
Who created the whole world.29.
First of all, He uttered ‘Oankar’:

158.g: ਸੋ ਧੁਨਿ ਪੂਰ ਜਗਤ ਮੋ ਰਹਾ ॥
158.t: so dhun poor jagat mo rahaa ||
158.e: And the sound of “Onkar’ Pervanded the whole world,
There was expansion of the whole world,
From the union of Purusha and Prakriti.30.

158.g: ਜਗਤ ਭਯੋ ਤਾ ਤੇ ਸਭ ਜਨੀਯਤ ॥
158.t: jagat bhayo taa te sabh janeeyat ||
158.e: The world was created and from that time, everyone knows it as world
Four divisions of creation became manifest and as such they were described
I have no power to give their description,
And tell their names separately.31.
That Lord created both the powerful and the weak
They were shown distinctly as high and low
The powerful KAL, adopting the physical form,
Manifested Himself in numerous forms.32.
According as the Lord adopted different forms,
In the same manner, he became renowned as different incarnations
But whatever is the Supreme form of the Lord
Ultimately all merged in Him.33.
Consider all the beings in the world,

158.g: ਏਕ ਜੋਤਿ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਮਹਿ ਜਾਨੋ ॥
158.t: ek jot sabh hee meh jaano ||
158.e: Ad the illumination of the same Light,
The Lord, Who is known as KAL

158.g: ਤਾ ਮਹਿ ਲੀਨ ਜਗਤਿ ਸਭ ਹ੍ਵੈਬੋ ॥੩੪॥
158.t: taa meh leen jagat sabh havaibo ||34||
158.e: All the world will merge in Him.34.
Whatever appears inconceivable to us,
The mind gives it the name of Maya

159.e: Only one lord pervades all

159.g: ਸਭ ਕੋਈ ਭਿੰਨ ਭਿੰਨ ਕਰ ਥਾਪਾ ॥੩੫॥
159.t: sabh koiee bhi(n)n bhi(n)n kar thaapaa ||35||
159.e: But appears to everyone as distinctly separate accofding to his discernment.35.

159.g: ਸਭ ਹੀ ਮਹਿ ਰਮ ਰਹਿਯੋ ਅਲੇਖਾ ॥
159.t: sabh hee meh ram rahiyo alekhaa ||
159.e: That inconceivable Lord pervades all
And all the beings beg from him according to their writ
He, who hath comprehended the Lord as One,

159.g: ਤਿਨ ਹੀ ਪਰਮ ਤਤੁ ਕਹੁ ਪਾਯੋ ॥੩੬॥
159.t: tin hee param tat kahu paayo ||36||
159.e: Only he hath realized the Supreme Essence.36.
That One Lord hath a hath a Unique Beauty and Form
And he Himself is somewhere a king and somewhere a pauper
He hath involved all through various means

159.g: ਸਭ ਤੇ ਜੁਦੋ ਨ ਕਿਨਹੁੰ ਪਾਯੋ ॥੩੭॥
159.t: sabh te judho na kinahu(n) paayo ||37||
159.e: But he Himself is separate from all and none could know His mystey.37.
He hath created all in separate forms
And He Himself destroys all

159.g: ਆਪ ਕਿਸੂ ਕੋ ਦੋਸ ਨ ਲੀਨਾ ॥
159.t: aap kisoo ko dhos na leenaa ||
159.e: He doth not take any blame on His own Head
And fixes the responsibility of vicious acts on others.38.
Now begins the description of the first Machh Incarnation
CHAUPAI
Once there was born a demon named Shankhasura

159.g: ਬਹੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਕੈ ਜਗ ਕੋ ਦੁਖ ਦਯੋ ॥
159.t: bahu bidh kai jag ko dhukh dhayo ||
159.e: Who, in many ways, distressed the world
Then the Lord manifested Himself as Machh (Fish) incarnation,
Who repeated His Own name Himself.39.
At first he Lord manifested Himself as small fish,
And shook the ocean violenty
Then He enlarged his body,
Seeing which Shankhasura got greatly enraged.40.

160.e: BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

160.g: ਤਬੈ ਕੋਪ ਗਰਜਿਯੋ ਬਲੀ ਸੰਖ ਬੀਰੰ ॥
160.t: tabai kop garajiyo balee sa(n)kh beera(n) ||

160.g: ਧਰੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਅਸਤ੍ਰੰ ਸਜੇ ਲੋਹ ਚੀਰੰ ॥
160.t: dhare sasatr asatra(n) saje loh cheera(n) ||
160.e: Then in great anger, the mighty Shankhasura thundered and wore his armour bedecking himself with weapons and arms

160.g: ਚਤੁਰ ਬੇਦ ਪਾਤੰ ਕੀਯੋ ਸਿੰਧੁ ਮਧੰ ॥
160.t: chatur bedh paata(n) keeyo si(n)dh madha(n) ||

160.g: ਤ੍ਰਸ੍ਰਯੋ ਅਸਟ ਨੈਣੰ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਜਾਪੁ ਸੁਧੰ ॥੪੧॥
160.t: trasrayo asaT naina(n) kariyo jaap sudha(n) ||41||
160.e: He threw the fore Vedas in the ocean, which frightened the eitht-eyed Brahma and caused him to remember the Lord.41.

160.g: ਧਰੇ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾਲੰ ॥
160.t: dhare loh kroha(n) kirapaa kai kirapaala(n) ||
160.e: Then the Lord, the well-wisher of both (the Vedas as well as Brahma) ws filled with kindness and highly enraged, He wore His steel-armour.

160.g: ਮਹਾ ਅਸਤ੍ਰ ਪਾਤੰ ਕਰੇ ਸਸਤ੍ਰ ਘਾਤੰ ॥
160.t: mahaa asatr paata(n) kare sasatr ghaata(n) ||

160.g: ਟਰੇ ਦੇਵ ਸਰਬੰ ਗਿਰੇ ਲੋਕ ਸਾਤੰ ॥੪੨॥
160.t: Tare dhev saraba(n) gire lok saata(n) ||42||
160.e: The bows of weapons were struck alongwith arms causing destruction. All the gods in groups moved away from their seats and the seven worlds trembled because of this horrible war.42.

160.g: ਭਏ ਅਤ੍ਰ ਘਾਤੰ ਗਿਰੇ ਚਉਰ ਚੀਰੰ ॥
160.t: bhe atr ghaata(n) gire chaur cheera(n) ||

160.g: ਰੁਲੇ ਤਛ ਮੁਛੰ ਉਠੇ ਤਿਛ ਤੀਰੰ ॥
160.t: rule tachh muchha(n) uThe tichh teera(n) ||
160.e: With the blows of arms, the fly-whisks and the garments behan to fall and with the volley of arrows, the chopped bodies began to fall on the ground.

160.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਸੁੰਡ ਮੁੰਡੰ ਰਣੰ ਭੀਮ ਰੂਪੰ ॥
160.t: gire su(n)dd mu(n)dda(n) rana(n) bheem roopa(n) ||
160.e: The chopped trunks and heads of huge elephants began to fall

160.g: ਮਨੋ ਖੇਲ ਪਉਢੇ ਹਠੀ ਫਾਗੁ ਜੂਪੰ ॥੪੩॥
160.t: mano khel paudde haThee faag joopa(n) ||43||
160.e: It appeared that the group of persistent youths was playing Holi.43.

160.g: ਬਹੇ ਖਗਯੰ ਖੇਤ ਖਿੰਗੰ ਸੁ ਧੀਰੰ ॥
160.t: bahe khagaya(n) khet khi(n)ga(n) su dheera(n) ||
160.e: The sword and daggers of the warriors with the power of endurance have been struck
And the brave fighters are bedecked with weapons and armours.

160.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਗਉਰਿ ਗਾਜੀ ਖੁਲੇ ਹਥ ਬਥੰ ॥
160.t: gire gaur gaajee khule hath batha(n) ||
160.e: The mighty heroes have fallen down with empty hands and seeing all this spectacle,

160.g: ਨਚਿਯੋ ਰੁਦ੍ਰ ਰੁਦ੍ਰੰ ਨਚੇ ਮਛ ਮਥੰ ॥੪੪॥
160.t: nachiyo rudhr rudhra(n) nache machh matha(n) ||44||
160.e: The god Shiva is busy in another dance and on the other side, the Machh incarnation, being pleased, is stirring the ocean.44.
RASAAVAL STANZA
Bedecked with auspicious weapons,
The brave fighters are thundering and seeing the killing of huge and mighty warriors like elephants,
The heavenly damsels, being passed with their feats,
Are waiting in heaven, in order to wed them.45.
The noises of the knocking on the shields and
The blows of the swords are being heard,
The daggers are being struck with clattering sound,
And both the side are desirous of their victory.46.
The whickers on the faces and terrible swords in the hands of the warriors look impressive,
The mighty warriors are wandering in the battlefield and supremely swift horses are dancing.47.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
On seeing the army, Shankhasura was highly enraged,

160.g: ਤਪੇ ਬੀਰ ਬਕਤ੍ਰੰ ਕੀਏ ਰਕਤ ਨੈਣੰ ॥
160.t: tape beer bakatra(n) ke'ee rakat naina(n) ||
160.e: Other heroes also blazing with anger began to shout loudly, with their eyes reddened with blood.

160.g: ਭੁਜਾ ਠੋਕ ਭੂਪੰ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਨਾਦ ਉੱਚੰ ॥
160.t: bhujaa Thok bhoopa(n) kariyo naadh u'cha(n) ||
160.e: The king Shankhasura, knocking his arms, raised a terrible thunder and
Hearing his frightening sound, the pregnancy of women was miscarried.48.
All resisted at their place and the trumpets began to resound violently,

160.g: ਖੁਲੇ ਖੇਤ ਮੋ ਖਗ ਖੂਨੀ ਖਿਮੰਕੇ ॥
160.t: khule khet mo khag khoonee khima(n)ke ||
160.e: He bloody daggers coming out (from) the scabbards) glistened in the battlefield.
The voice of the cracking of the cruel bows were heard and
The ghosts and goblins began to dance furiously.49.
The warriors began to fall in the battlefield alongwith their weapons, and
The headless trunks began to dance unconsciously in the war.
The bloody daggers and sharp arrow were struck,
The trumpets began to resound violently and the warriors began to run hither and thither.50.

160.g: ਕਟੇ ਚਰਮ ਬਰਮੰ ਗਿਰਿਯੋ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਸਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
160.t: kaTe charam barama(n) giriyo satr sasatra(n) ||

160.g: ਭਕੈ ਭੈ ਭਰੇ ਭੂਤ ਭੂਮੰ ਨ੍ਰਿਸਤ੍ਰੰ ॥
160.t: bhakai bhai bhare bhoot bhooma(n) nirasatra(n) ||

160.g: ਰਣੰ ਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਸਭੀ ਰੰਗ ਭੂਮੰ ॥
160.t: rana(n) ra(n)g rate sabhee ra(n)g bhooma(n) ||

160.g: ਗਿਰੇ ਜੁਧ ਮਧੰ ਬਲੀ ਝੂਮਿ ਝੂਮੰ ॥੫੧॥
160.t: gire judh madha(n) balee jhoom jhooma(n) ||51||
160.e: All were dyed in the dye of war and the mighty warriors began to fall in the battlefield swinging and reeling.51

160.g: ਭਯੋ ਦੁੰਦ ਜੁਧੰ ਰਣੰ ਸੰਖ ਮਛੰ ॥
160.t: bhayo dhu(n)dh judha(n) rana(n) sa(n)kh machha(n) ||

161.g: ਮਨੋ ਦੋ ਗਿਰੰ ਜੁਧ ਜੁਟੇ ਸਪਛੰ ॥
161.t: mano dho gira(n) judh juTe sapachha(n) ||
161.e: Such a horrible battle was fought between Shankhasura and Machh. It appeared clearly that two mountains were waging war with each other.

161.g: ਕਟੇ ਮਾਸ ਟੁਕੰ ਭਖੇ ਗਿਧਿ ਬ੍ਰਿਧੰ ॥
161.t: kaTe maas Tuka(n) bhakhe gidh biradha(n) ||

161.g: ਹਸੈ ਜੋਗਣੀ ਚਉਸਠਾ ਸੂਰ ਸੁਧੰ ॥੫੨॥
161.t: hasai joganee chausaThaa soor sudha(n) ||52||
161.e: The bits of flesh began to fall, which were devoured by huge vultures, and the sixty-four vampires (Yoginis) began to laugh on seeing this terrible war.52.

161.g: ਕੀਯੋ ਉਧਾਰ ਬੇਦੰ ਹਤੇ ਸੰਖਬੀਰੰ ॥
161.t: keeyo udhaar bedha(n) hate sa(n)khabeera(n) ||

161.g: ਤਜ੍ਯੋ ਮਛ ਰੂਪੰ ਸਜ੍ਯੋ ਸੁੰਦ੍ਰ ਚੀਰ ॥
161.t: tajayo machh roopa(n) sajayo su(n)dhr cheer ||
161.e: After killing Shankhasura, the Machh (fish) incarnation redeemed the Vedas and Lord, forsaking the Fish-form, bedecked himself with winsome garments.

161.g: ਸਬੈ ਦੇਵ ਥਾਪੇ ਕੀਯੋ ਦੁਸਟ ਨਾਸੰ ॥
161.t: sabai dhev thaape keeyo dhusaT naasa(n) ||

161.g: ਟਰੇ ਸਰਬ ਦਾਨੋ ਭਰੇ ਜੀਵ ਤ੍ਰਾਸੰ ॥੫੩॥
161.t: Tare sarab dhaano bhare jeev traasa(n) ||53||
161.e: After destroying the tyrants, the Lord established again all the gods, and demons frightening the creatures were destroyed.53.

161.g: ਤ੍ਰਿਭੰਗੀ ਛੰਦ ॥
161.t: tirabha(n)gee chha(n)dh ||
161.e: TRIBHANGI STANZA

161.g: ਸੰਖਾਸੁਰ ਮਾਰੇ ਬੇਦ ਉਧਾਰੇ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਸੰਘਾਰੇ ਜਸੁ ਲੀਨੋ ॥
161.t: sa(n)khaasur maare bedh udhaare satr sa(n)ghaare jas leeno ||
161.e: The Lord received great approbation of killing the demon Shankhasura, redeeming the Vedas and destroying the enemies.

161.g: ਦੇਵੇ ਸੁ ਬੁਲਾਯੋ ਰਾਜ ਬਿਠਾਯੋ ਛਤ੍ਰ ਫਿਰਾਯੋ ਸੁਖ ਦੀਨੋ ॥
161.t: dheve su bulaayo raaj biThaayo chhatr firaayo sukh dheeno ||
161.e: He called Indra, the king of gods and blessed him with royalty and its comforts.

161.g: ਕੋਟੰ ਬਜੇ ਬਾਜੇ ਅਮਰੇਸੁਰ ਗਾਜੇ ਸੁਭ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜੇ ਸੋਕ ਹਰੇ ॥
161.t: koTa(n) baje baaje amaresur gaaje subh ghar saaje sok hare ||
161.e: Millions of musical instruments began to resound, the gods began to play the tune of bliss and the sorrows of every house were destroyed.

161.g: ਦੈ ਕੋਟਕ ਦਛਨਾ ਕ੍ਰੋਰ ਪ੍ਰਦਛਨਾ ਆਨਿ ਸੁ ਮਛ ਕੇ ਪਾਇ ਪਰੇ ॥੫੪॥
161.t: dhai koTak dhachhanaa kror pradhachhanaa aan su machh ke pai pare ||54||
161.e: All the gods bowed in respect at the feet of Fish incarnation presenting various types of gifts and making millions of circumambulations.54.

161.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਮਛ ਪ੍ਰਥਮ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਸੰਖਾਸੁਰ ਬਧਹ ਸਮਾਪਤਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੧॥
161.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the machh pratham avataar sa(n)khaasur badheh samaapatam sat subham sat ||1||
161.e: End of the description of the first Machh (fish) Incarnation and Killing of Shankhasura in BACHITTAR NATAK.

161.g: ਅਥ ਕਛ ਅਵਤਾਰ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
161.t: ath kachh avataar kathana(n) ||
161.e: Now begins the description of Kachh (Tortoise) Incarnation:

161.g: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਛੰਦ ॥
161.t: bhuja(n)g prayaat chha(n)dh ||
161.e: BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

161.g: ਕਿਤੋ ਕਾਲ ਬੀਤਯੋ ਕਰਿਯੋ ਦੇਵ ਰਾਜੰ ॥
161.t: kito kaal beetayo kariyo dhev raaja(n) ||

161.g: ਭਰੇ ਰਾਜ ਧਾਮੰ ਸੁਭੰ ਸਰਬ ਸਾਜੰ ॥
161.t: bhare raaj dhaama(n) subha(n) sarab saaja(n) ||
161.e: Indra, the king of gods, ruled for a long time and his palaces were full of all materials of comfort

161.g: ਗਜੰ ਬਾਜ ਬੀਣੰ ਬਿਨਾ ਰਤਨ ਭੂਪੰ ॥
161.t: gaja(n) baaj beena(n) binaa ratan bhoopa(n) ||

161.g: ਕਰਿਯੋ ਬਿਸਨ ਬੀਚਾਰ ਚਿਤੰ ਅਨੂਪੰ ॥੧॥
161.t: kariyo bisan beechaar chita(n) anoopa(n) ||1||
161.e: But once Vishnu reflected upon a unique idea in his mind that this king is without elephants, horses and jewels (therefore something should be done in this direction).1.

161.g: ਸਬੈ ਦੇਵ ਏਕਤ੍ਰ ਕੀਨੇ ਪੁਰਿੰਦ੍ਰੰ ॥
161.t: sabai dhev ekatr keene puri(n)dhra(n) ||

161.g: ਸਸੰ ਸੂਰਜੰ ਆਦਿ ਲੈ ਕੈ ਉਪਿੰਦ੍ਰੰ ॥
161.t: sasa(n) sooraja(n) aadh lai kai upi(n)dhra(n) ||
161.e: Indra gathered together all the gods including Chandra. Surya and Upendra.

161.g: ਹੁਤੇ ਦਈਤ ਜੇ ਲੋਕ ਮਧ੍ਰਯੰ ਹੰਕਾਰੀ ॥
161.t: hute dhieet je lok madhraya(n) ha(n)kaaree ||

161.g: ਭਏ ਏਕਠੇ ਭ੍ਰਾਤਿ ਭਾਵੰ ਬਿਚਾਰੀ ॥੨॥
161.t: bhe ekaThe bhraat bhaava(n) bichaaree ||2||
161.e: Considering this gathering as some stratagem against them, the proud demons also gathered together.2.

161.g: ਬਦ੍ਯੋ ਅਰਧੁ ਅਰਧੰ ਦੁਹੂੰ ਬਾਟਿ ਲੀਬੋ ॥
161.t: badhayo aradh aradha(n) dhuhoo(n) baaT leebo ||

161.g: ਸਬੋ ਬਾਤ ਮਾਨੀ ਯਹੇ ਕਾਮ ਕੀਬੋ ॥
161.t: sabo baat maanee yahe kaam keebo ||
161.e: Now both the groups decided that whatever shall be attained, the same shall be distributed equally. All of them agreed on this proposal and the work was begun

161.g: ਕਰੋ ਮਥਨੀ ਕੂਟ ਮੰਦ੍ਰਾਚਲੇਯੰ ॥
161.t: karo mathanee kooT ma(n)dhraachaleya(n) ||

161.g: ਤਕ੍ਰਯੋ ਛੀਰ ਸਾਮੁੰਦ੍ਰ ਦੇਅੰ ਅਦੇਯੰ ॥੩॥
161.t: takrayo chheer saamu(n)dhr dhea(n) adheya(n) ||3||
161.e: Both the gods and demons settled the programme of churning the milk-ocean, making churning-stick of the Mandrachal mountain.3.

161.g: ਕਰੀ ਮਥਕਾ ਬਾਸਕੰ ਸਿੰਧ ਮਧੰ ॥
161.t: karee mathakaa baasaka(n) si(n)dh madha(n) ||

161.g: ਮਥੈ ਲਾਗ ਦੋਊ ਭਏ ਅਧੁ ਅਧੰ ॥
161.t: mathai laag dhouoo bhe adh adha(n) ||
161.e: The serpent Vasuki was made the rope of the churning-stick and dividing the participants equally, both the ends of the rope were held tighty.

161.g: ਸਿਰੰ ਦੈਤ ਲਾਗੇ ਗਹੀ ਪੁਛ ਦੇਵੰ ॥
161.t: sira(n) dhait laage gahee puchh dheva(n) ||

161.g: ਮਥ੍ਰਯੋ ਛੀਰ ਸਿੰਧੰ ਮਨੋ ਮਾਟਕੇਵੰ ॥੪॥
161.t: mathrayo chheer si(n)dha(n) mano maaTakeva(n) ||4||
161.e: The demons caught hold of the side of the head and the gods the tail, they began to churn like the curd in a vessel.4.

161.g: ਇਸੋ ਕਉਣ ਬੀਯੋ ਧਰੇ ਭਾਰੁ ਪਬੰ ॥
161.t: eiso kaun beeyo dhare bhaar paba(n) ||

161.g: ਉਠੇ ਕਾਪ ਬੀਰੰ ਦਿਤ੍ਰਯਾਦਿਤ੍ਰਯ ਸਬੰ ॥
161.t: auThe kaap beera(n) dhitrayaadhitray saba(n) ||
161.e: Now they reflected on this idea as to who can be the mighty hero, who can endure the load of the mountain (because a base was required for the purpose)? Hearing this Ditya, Aditya etc., the heroes shuddered, faltering in absurd prattle.

161.g: ਤਬੈ ਆਪ ਹੀ ਬਿਸਨ ਮੰਤ੍ਰੰ ਬਿਚਾਰਿਯੋ ॥
161.t: tabai aap hee bisan ma(n)tra(n) bichaariyo ||

161.g: ਤਰੇ ਪਰਬਤੰ ਕਛਪੰ ਰੂਪ ਧਾਰਿਯੋ ॥੫॥
161.t: tare parabata(n) kachhapa(n) roop dhaariyo ||5||
161.e: Then observing this difficulty of both the gods and demons, Vishnu himself thought about it and transforming himself in the form of Kachh (tortoise), seated himself at the base of the mountain.5.

161.g: ਇਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਬਚਿਤ੍ਰ ਨਾਟਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੇ ਕਛੁ ਦੁਤੀਆ ਅਉਤਾਰ ਬਰਨਨੰ ਸੰਪੂਰਨਮ ਸਤੁ ਸੁਭਮ ਸਤੁ ॥੨॥
161.t: eit sree bachitr naaTak gra(n)the kachh dhuteeaa aautaar baranana(n) sa(n)pooranam sat subham sat ||2||
161.e: End of the description of the second Kachh (tortoise), incarnation in BACHITTAR NATAK.2.

161.g: ਅਥ ਛੀਰ ਸਮੁੰਦ੍ਰ ਮਥਨ ਚਉਦਹ ਰਤਨ ਕਥਨੰ ॥
161.t: ath chheer samu(n)dhr mathan chaudheh ratan kathana(n) ||
161.e: Now begins the description of the Churing of the Milkocean and the Fourteen Jewels:

161.g: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਭਗਉਤੀ ਜੀ ਸਹਾਇ ॥
161.t: sree bhagautee jee sahai ||
161.e: Let Shri Bhagauti Ji (The Primal Power) be helpful.

161.g: ਤੋਟਕ ਛੰਦ ॥
161.t: toTak chha(n)dh ||
161.e: TOTAK STANZA

161.g: ਮਿਲਿ ਦੇਵ ਅਦੇਵਨ ਸਿੰਧੁ ਮਥਿਯੋ ॥
161.t: mil dhev adhevan si(n)dh mathiyo ||

161.g: ਕਬਿ ਸ੍ਯਾਮ ਕਵਿਤਨ ਮਧਿ ਕਥਿਯੋ ॥
161.t: kab sayaam kavitan madh kathiyo ||
161.e: Both the gods and demons unitedly churned the ocean, which hath been narrated in verse by the poet Shyam.

161.g: ਤਬ ਰਤਨ ਚਤੁਰਦਸ ਯੋ ਨਿਕਸੇ ॥
161.t: tab ratan chaturadhas yo nikase ||

161.g: ਅਸਿਤਾ ਨਿਸਿ ਮੋ ਸਸਿ ਸੇ ਬਿਗਸੇ ॥੧॥
161.t: asitaa nis mo sas se bigase ||1||
161.e: Then the fourteen jewels, in their splendour emanated from the sea, just as the moon looks elegant during the night.1.

161.g: ਅਮਰਾਤਕ ਸੀਸ ਕੀ ਓਰ ਹੂਅੰ ॥
161.t: amaraatak sees kee or hooa(n) ||

161.g: ਮਿਲਿ ਪੂਛ ਗਹੀ ਦਿਸਿ ਦੇਵ ਦੂਅੰ ॥
161.t: mil poochh gahee dhis dhev dhooa(n) ||
161.e: The demons caught Vasuki from the side of the head and the gods from the side of the tail.

161.g: ਰਤਨੰ ਨਿਕਸੇ ਬਿਗਸੇ ਸਸਿ ਸੇ ॥
161.t: ratana(n) nikase bigase sas se ||

161.g: ਜਨੁ ਘੂਟਨ ਲੇਤ ਅਮੀ ਰਸ ਕੇ ॥੨॥
161.t: jan ghooTan let amee ras ke ||2||
161.e: On seeing the jewels emanating from the sea, they became pleased as though they had drunk the ambrosia.2.

161.g: ਨਿਕਸ੍ਰਯੋ ਧਨੁ ਸਾਇਕ ਸੁਧ ਸਿਤੰ ॥
161.t: nikasrayo dhan saik sudh sita(n) ||

162.g: ਮਦ ਪਾਨ ਕਢ੍ਯੋ ਘਟ ਮਦ੍ਰਯ ਮਤੰ ॥
162.t: madh paan kaddayo ghaT madhray mata(n) ||
162.e: The bow and of purely white colour came out, and those intoxicated ones brought out from the ocean a pitcher of honey.
The elephant, horse, nectar and Lakshmi came out and looked splendid like the flash of lightning from the clouds.3.

162.g: ਜਿਹ ਮੋਹਿ ਰਹੈ ਲਖਿ ਇੰਦ੍ਰ ਸਭਾ ॥
162.t: jeh moh rahai lakh i(n)dhr sabhaa ||
162.e: After Kalapdrum (Elysian, wish-fulfilling tree) and poison, the heavenly damsel Rambha came out, seeing whom, the people of Indrs’s court allured.

162.g: ਮਨਿ ਕੌਸਤੁਭ ਚੰਦ ਸੁ ਰੂਪ ਸੁਭੰ ॥
162.t: man kauasatubh cha(n)dh su roop subha(n) ||

162.e: The Kaustubh jewel and the moon also came out, which are remembered by the demons in the battlefield.4.
Kamadhenu (the wish-fulfilling cow) also came out which was seized by the mighty Sahasrajun.

162.g: ਗਨਿ ਰਤਨ ਗਨਉ ਉਪ ਰਤਨ ਅਬੈ ॥
162.t: gan ratan ganau up ratan abai ||

162.g: ਤੁਮ ਸੰਤ ਸੁਨੋ ਚਿਤ ਲਾਇ ਸਬੈ ॥੫॥
162.t: tum sa(n)t suno chit lai sabai ||5||
162.e: After reckoning the jewels, now I mention the minor jewels, O saints  listen to me attentively.5.

162.g: ਜਨ ਪੰਚ ਸੁ ਨਾਮਯ ਸੰਖ ਸੁਭੰ ॥
162.t: jan pa(n)ch su naamay sa(n)kh subha(n) ||
162.e: These minor jewels are leech, myrobalan, honey, conch ( panchjanay), ruta, hemp, discus and mace

162.g: ਸਸਿ ਬੇਲ ਬਿਜਿਯਾ ਅਰੁ ਚਕ੍ਰ ਗਦਾ ॥
162.t: sas bel bijiyaa ar chakr gadhaa ||

162.e: The later two look impressive in the hands of princes always.6.

162.g: ਜਿਨ ਖੰਡਿ ਕਰੇ ਗਨ ਦਈਤ ਰਣੰ ॥
162.t: jin kha(n)dd kare gan dhieet rana(n) ||
162.e: The bow and arrow, the bull Nandi and the dagger (which had destroyed the demons) came out of the ocean.
The trident of Shiva, Barvanal (the fire), Kapil Muni and Dhanwantri came out as the fourteenth jewel.7.

162.g: ਗਨਿ ਰਤਨ ਉਪਰਤਨ ਔ ਧਾਤ ਗਨੋ ॥
162.t: gan ratan uparatan aau dhaat gano ||

162.e: After counting the greater and minor jewels, now I count the metals and afterwards I shall count the lesser metals.
All these names have been reckoned by the poet Shyam according to his own understanding

162.g: ਘਟ ਜਾਨ ਕਵੀ ਜਿਨਿ ਨਿੰਦ ਕਰੋ ॥੮॥
162.t: ghaT jaan kavee jin ni(n)dh karo ||8||
162.e: Considering them in small number, poets requested not to slander me.8.

163.e: First of tall I reckon iron, lead and gold alongwith the fourth white metal silver

163.g: ਕਥਿ ਅਸਟਮ ਜਿਸਤੁ ਹੈ ਧਾਤ ਧਰੰ ॥੯॥
163.t: kath asaTam jisat hai dhaat dhara(n) ||9||
163.e: Then mentioning copper, tin and brass, I consider the eighth metal as zinc, which is found within the earth.9.
Updhat Description:
TOTAK STANZA
Now I describe the minor metals  they are : antimony, cinnabar, yellow orpiment, bombax,
Potash, conchshell, mica, artemesia and calomel.10.
DOHRA

163.g: ਧਾਤੁ ਉਪਧਾਤ ਜਥਾ ਸਕਤਿ ਸੋਹੂੰ ਕਹੀ ਬਨਾਇ ॥
163.t: dhaat upadhaat jathaa sakat sohoo(n) kahee banai ||
163.e: These metals, minor metals have been described by me according to my own understanding.

163.g: ਖਾਨਨ ਮਹਿ ਭੀ ਹੋਤ ਹੈ ਕੋਈ ਕਹੂੰ ਕਮਾਇ ॥੧੧॥
163.t: khaanan meh bhee hot hai koiee kahoo(n) kamai ||11||
163.e: He, who desires to have them, can get them.11.
CHAUPAI

163.g: ਧਾਤ ਉਪਧਾਤ ਦਿਰਬ ਮੋ ਸਬ ਹੀ ॥
163.t: dhaat upadhaat dhirab mo sab hee ||
163.e: As the major and minor jewels, the major and minor metals came out

163.g: ਤਿਹ ਤਬ ਹੀ ਬਿਸਨਹਿ ਹਿਰ ਲਯੋ ॥
163.t: teh tab hee bisaneh hir layo ||

163.e: They were taken away by Vishnu and distributed the remaining things amongst all.12.

163.g: ਸਾਰੰਗ ਸਰ ਅਸਿ ਚਕ੍ਰ ਗਦਾ ਲੀਅ ॥
163.t: saara(n)g sar as chakr gadhaa leea ||

163.e: He took away himself the bow and arrows, the sword, the discus, the mace and the (Panchjanay) conch etc.
And taking the trident, the cow named Pinak and Poison in his hands, gave them to Shva.13.
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA

163.g: ਉਠੇ ਦੀਹ ਦਾਨੋ ਜੁਧੰ ਲੋਹ ਪੂਰੰ ॥
163.t: auThe dheeh dhaano judha(n) loh poora(n) ||
163.e: The elephants named Airavat was given to Indra and the horse to the sun seeing which the demons, in great fury,Marched to wage war.

163.g: ਤਬੈ ਬਿਸਨ ਜੂ ਚਿਤਿ ਕੀਨੀ ਬਿਚਾਰੰ ॥੧੪॥
163.t: tabai bisan joo chit keenee bichaara(n) ||14||
163.e: Seeing the advancing army of the demons, Vishnu thought in his mind.14.
Here begins the description of the incarnations named Nar and Narayan:
BHUJANG PRAYAAT STANZA
Manifesting himself as Nar and Narayan, Vishnu, managing his weapons and arms, came in front of the demon-forces.

163.g: ਭਟੰ ਐਠਿ ਫੈਂਟੇ ਭੁਜੰ ਠੋਕਿ ਭੂਪੰ ॥
163.t: bhaTa(n) aaiTh fai(n)Te bhuja(n) Thok bhoopa(n) ||
163.e: The warriors tied their garments tightly and the kings beat their arms

163.g: ਬਜੇ ਸੂਲ ਸੇਲੰ ਭਏ ਆਪ ਰੂਪੰ ॥੧੫॥
163.t: baje sool sela(n) bhe aap roopa(n) ||15||
163.e: It, that war, the tridents and the spears began to collide with each other.15.

163.g: ਪਰਿਯੋ ਆਪ ਮੋ ਲੋਹ ਕ੍ਰੋਹੰ ਅਪਾਰੰ ॥
163.t: pariyo aap mo loh kroha(n) apaara(n) ||

163.e: In great anger. The blows of the steel-arms began to rain and at this juncture Vishnu manifested his third incarnation.

163.g: ਦਿਪੈ ਜੋਤਿ ਸਉਦਰ ਜੁ ਧਾਰੇ ਅਨੂਪੰ ॥੧੬॥
163.t: dhipai jot saudhar ju dhaare anoopa(n) ||16||
163.e: Nar and Narayan both had similar forms and their effulgence assumed unparalleled Lustre.16.

163.g: ਜੁਟੇ ਜੰਗ ਕੋ ਜੰਗ ਜੋਧਾ ਜੁਝਾਰੇ ॥
163.t: juTe ja(n)g ko ja(n)g jodhaa jujhaare ||
163.e: Wearing their helmets the warriors are striking their blows with maces and the mighty heroes are engrossed in the war.

163.g: ਉਡੀ ਧੂਰਿ ਪੂਰੰ ਛੁਹੀ ਐਨ ਗੈਨੰ ॥
163.t: auddee dhoor poora(n) chhuhee aain gaina(n) ||

163.e: The dust hath both the gods and demons, having gone astray, were falling and even the three-eyed god Shiva trembled.17.

163.g: ਸੁਭੈ ਜੰਗ ਮੋ ਜੰਗ ਜੋਧਾ ਜੁਝਾਰੰ ॥
163.t: subhai ja(n)g mo ja(n)g jodhaa jujhaara(n) ||
163.e: Many types of warriors fell in the field and the great fighters looked impressive in the war.

163.g: ਪਰੀ ਤਛ ਮੁਛੰ ਸਭੈ ਅੰਗ ਭੰਗੰ ॥
